title: AR5: set-iteration order silently drops core-command labels from ancestor contexts
description:
FOUND BY the adversarial review of docs/intent_training_improvements_spec.md (bd fix-551.1). CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY on fastworkflow/examples/messaging_app_4 and tests/todo_list_workflow.

SYMPTOM: whether 'what can i do?', 'go up', 'reset context' and 'what is current context' are routable in a given context depends on PYTHONHASHSEED. Two identical training runs can disagree.

MECHANISM (model_pipeline_training.py:829-863):
1. train() iterates `context_set_for_training`, which is a set of strings, so visit order follows PYTHONHASHSEED and varies run to run.
2. When a context B is trained, cache_ancestor_utterances(:768-801) populates context_utterance_cache[A] for every ancestor A of B — but it fills it from crd.context_model.commands(A), which does NOT include core commands (those come from cmd_dir.core_command_names, merged separately into train_cmds at :834).
3. When the loop later reaches A itself, `ctx_name in context_utterance_cache` is True (:841), so it takes the cached branch. That branch only extends utterances for `cmd_name in map_cmd_2_uttlist` (:845) — every core command is absent, so it is SKIPPED.
4. context_utterances is non-empty (ancestor commands filled it), so the regeneration guard at :851 does not fire. The core labels never enter A's classifier.

MEASURED BLAST RADIUS (static analysis at commit 23dbe35):
- messaging_app_4: if 'ChatRoom' is visited after 'User' or 'PremiumUser', 5 labels vanish (4x IntentDetection/* plus wildcard).
- todo_list_workflow: same 5 labels for 'TodoList' and 'TodoListManager'; 4 for '*'.

This is finding F3's failure mode (a label never enters the classifier, silently) arriving by a completely different mechanism, and it is invisible for the same reason: the reported F1 is computed over whatever labels DID make it in, so a context missing 5 labels still reports a healthy score.

TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS — fix both:
(a) NON-DETERMINISM: iterate contexts in a deterministic order. Note TRAINING_SEED cannot fix this; PYTHONHASHSEED is not reachable from it. Sort the context set.
(b) CORRECTNESS: sorting alone only makes the loss deterministic, it does not stop it. The cached branch at :841-849 must fill in commands missing from the cache rather than skipping them. Reaching a context via the cache must never produce a smaller label space than reaching it directly.

ACCEPTANCE: an integration test over a workflow with a hierarchy (tests/todo_list_workflow has one) asserting the trained label space of an ancestor context is identical regardless of visit order, and contains every core command. Per the testing rules, no mocks — induce the order rather than patching it out.
notes:
--- SECOND SITE (found during R2 determinism work, confirmed empirically) ---
AR5 covers LABEL LOSS from set iteration order. There is a second, distinct
consequence of the same root cause: ROW ORDER nondeterminism.

model_pipeline_training.py:872-877
    net_ancestor_plus_wildcard_utterances = (
        (ancestor_utterances - context_utterances) | wildcard_utterances)
    utterance_command_tuples.extend(
        list(zip(net_ancestor_plus_wildcard_utterances, ['wildcard'] * len(...))))

net_... is a set. Its iteration order varies with PYTHONHASHSEED, so the wildcard
rows are appended in a different ORDER on every interpreter start. Line 914
train_test_split(dataset, test_size=0.25, random_state=42) shuffles by POSITION,
so a fixed random_state selects a different SUBSET of rows for test whenever the
upstream order changes. random_state=42 is therefore false reassurance: the split
is deterministic in index space, not in row space.

Empirically confirmed (same 30 rows, 3 hash seeds -> 3 different test partitions):
  PYTHONHASHSEED=0  test-set fingerprint 45165
  PYTHONHASHSEED=1  test-set fingerprint 26575
  PYTHONHASHSEED=2  test-set fingerprint 3781

Impact: two "identical" training runs produce different models and different
reported F1. This blocks any paired comparison of runs, and therefore blocks
R1 (is held-out score X better than Y?) and D6 (utterance cache reuse).

Note the own-command rows are NOT affected: they come from context_utterance_list
(a list) at :857-861. Only the wildcard rows are set-ordered.
Also unaffected: label_encoder.fit_transform sorts its classes, so the
label -> int mapping is stable.

FIX (both sites, one change): iterate sorted() over these sets. Sites:
  :872-877  net_ancestor_plus_wildcard_utterances  (row order)
  plus the AR5 sites for context_set_for_training / cached-branch label fill.
close_reason: Fixed in the wave-1 integration of model_pipeline_training.py. Three changes, all in train(): (1) the context loop now iterates sorted(context_set_for_training), so hash order no longer decides anything; (2) the two-branch utterance assembly was replaced by ONE loop that uses the cache when it holds a command and GENERATES when it does not -- the old cached branch silently skipped commands absent from the cache, and a context previously visited as an ancestor has a cache holding only context_model.commands(), which excludes the core commands, so those labels vanished and the commands became unroutable in that context; (3) reserved-label rows are appended from sorted() sets, so row order into the unstratified train_test_split is stable. Note the outcome is now order-INDEPENDENT, not merely order-stable, which is the stronger property.

title: R6: persist and reuse generated utterances, keyed by a provenance fingerprint
description:
ADDRESSES the cost side of F8/F9 and is the prerequisite for selective training's --changed-only.

DO (spec R6, decision D6):
- Persist generated utterances per command, keyed by a fingerprint of (seed list, persona IDs, generator config, seed value).
- Default to REUSE when the fingerprint matches; --regenerate-utterances forces a refresh.
- Support AGGREGATION across runs: a developer who runs generation three times with different seeds should be able to UNION the results rather than replace them. This is the cheapest available variance reduction and it directly feeds the convergence loop.
- Cache invalidation must be CONSERVATIVE: any change to a seed list invalidates that command, and — by the upward-closure rule (D5) — dirties every DESCENDANT context's wildcard class, because ancestor utterances are what constitute that class.

HARD PREREQUISITE (D6): R2. Without recorded persona IDs and a recorded seed there is nothing trustworthy to fingerprint, and the cache cannot be validated. Rejected alternative: timestamp or mtime keying.
notes:
CORRECTION from the adversarial review (fix-551.1, finding AR2): this issue's cache-invalidation rule cites D5's upward-closure, which the review found incomplete - it expands over 'parent' only and misses the 'base' composition. Use the corrected rule recorded on fix-551.10, and reuse fastworkflow.train.selective_training.close_dirty_contexts rather than deriving it again.

--- MEASURED: R6 IS A PREREQUISITE FOR R2, NOT A CONSUMER OF IT ---
The spec sequences this the other way round (D6: the utterance cache depends on
determinism). The dependency actually runs BOTH ways, and this direction is the
binding one.

EXPERIMENT: two full training runs of examples/hello_world, same TRAINING_SEED=42,
same code, same env, back to back. Compared the generated utterance sets per command
from training_provenance.json.

  IntentDetection/go_up                    DIFFERENT   A=28 rows  B=31 rows
  IntentDetection/reset_context            DIFFERENT   A=25 rows  B=23 rows
  IntentDetection/what_can_i_do            DIFFERENT   A=38 rows  B=34 rows
  IntentDetection/what_is_current_context  DIFFERENT   A=29 rows  B=24 rows
  add_two_numbers                          DIFFERENT   A=24 rows  B=29 rows

  0/5 commands produced identical utterance sets at the same seed.

WHY: TRAINING_SEED fixes random/numpy/torch, persona selection, and the
train_test_split indices. It cannot fix the LLM. Synthetic utterance generation calls
a live model per command, so the TRAINING DATA ITSELF differs run to run -- different
texts AND different row counts. Seeding a shuffle over a different dataset does not
produce a reproducible model.

CONSEQUENCES
  1. fix-551.2 (R2) cannot be closed on seeding alone. Seeding + fix-9mo's ordering
     fixes are necessary and still not sufficient. R2's acceptance test must be "two
     runs at the same seed produce byte-identical artifacts", which is unreachable
     until utterances are persisted and reused.
  2. R1's paired comparisons (is held-out score X better than Y?) are not yet
     meaningful: two runs differ in their training data, so any score delta confounds
     the change under test with a fresh draw of utterances.
  3. This explains the standalone-vs-suite variance in
     test_trained_model_routes_utterance. It is not test ordering or leaked global
     state; each run trains on different data.

RAISING TO P0: R6 now blocks the p0 determinism work rather than following it.

--- WAVE 2 DELIVERED (R6 implementation). Design decisions ---

MODULE: fastworkflow/train/utterance_cache.py, plus the hook in
generate_synthetic.py. artifact_versioning.RESERVED_TOPLEVEL_NAMES gained
"utterance_cache" so the prune already exempts it -- no change needed in
train/__main__.py for that.

D-R6-1 LOCATION: <workflow>/___command_info/utterance_cache/. NOT inside
versions/<id>/: versions are immutable snapshots and `versions prune` would
delete the reuse that makes the next run reproducible. NOT ~/.cache: a cache
keyed to a laptop makes reproducibility a property of the machine and does not
survive a container build. ___command_info* is already gitignored, so a workflow
author opts in deliberately. Losing the cache costs a slow non-reproducible run,
never a wrong one -- so `rm -rf ___command_info` stays a legitimate blunt reset.

D-R6-2 TWO-PART KEY. An entry is addressed by (variant key, seed). The variant
key hashes: seed utterance list (ORDER SIGNIFICANT), command name, num_personas,
utterances_per_persona, personas_per_batch, model (LLM_SYNDATA_GEN), a digest of
LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE, the persona source id, the completion backend id, and a
sha256 of the SOURCE TEXT of generate_utterances_for_personas. Splitting the seed
out of the key is what makes R6's cross-seed aggregation expressible: three seeds
accumulate as three entries in one file.

D-R6-3 THE PROMPT IS AN INPUT. Including the generator source digest means ANY
edit to that function -- including a comment -- invalidates every entry.
Deliberate. Over-invalidation costs money; under-invalidation costs trust in the
measurement, and this project already paid that bill once.

D-R6-4 PRODUCTION BACKENDS NAMED BY CONSTANTS, not by qualname. litellm.completion
is a decorated wrapper whose qualname moves between releases; keying on it would
invalidate every cache on an unrelated dependency bump. An INJECTED callable IS
keyed by its qualified name, so a test generator can never share an entry with the
real one.

D-R6-5 DEGRADED RUNS ARE NEVER CACHED. fell_back (rate limit, datasets missing) or
zero generated rows => no write. Caching a truncated set would make F3 permanent
instead of transient. Wave 1's seed-utterance fallback is preserved and tested.

D-R6-6 ONLY GENERATED TEXT IS STORED. The [command_name] + seeds prefix is rebuilt
from live sources on every run, so a hit cannot resurrect a deleted seed utterance
even if the fingerprint somehow did not miss first.

D-R6-7 CACHE STATUS IS NOT RECORDED IN PROVENANCE. Whether utterances came from
the LLM or the cache is a property of the RUN, not of the DATA. Recording it would
make two otherwise identical runs produce different training_provenance.json and
defeat the byte comparison R2 needs. Surfaced via UtteranceCache.format_summary()
instead.

D-R6-8 ATTRIBUTION IS RE-DERIVED ON A HIT, not copied. _apply_cached_entry replays
_attribute_utterance so a cached utterance duplicating a hand-written seed is
absorbed into SEED_PERSONA_ID exactly as on a fresh generation. Copying the stored
map verbatim would let a whole-persona holdout (R1/D1) score a memorised row as a
generalisation success.

D-R6-9 DUPLICATES ARE PRESERVED on reuse and de-duplicated only on aggregate.
Generation does not de-duplicate and a repeated row is a second training row;
dropping it on read would make the cached run train on less data than the run that
produced the entry.

D-R6-10 CONCURRENCY: read-merge-atomic-replace per variant file. os.replace is
atomic, so a reader sees old or new, never half. Two writers racing on the SAME
variant can lose an update; the loser regenerates next run, which is the safe
direction. Different commands are different files by construction.

INVALIDATION: UTTERANCE_CACHE_MODE in {reuse (default), regenerate, aggregate,
off}, resolved from the workflow env file first, then a shell export (get_env_var
with a code default short-circuits os.environ, so both paths are read explicitly).
Programmatic: UtteranceCache(path, mode=...). CLI flag to wire: --regenerate-utterances.

MEASURED (examples/hello_world, TRAINING_SEED=42, two back-to-back runs, same
harness as M4, run twice at each setting):
  UTTERANCE_CACHE_MODE=off     0/5 commands identical  (reproduces M4)
  UTTERANCE_CACHE_MODE=reuse   5/5 commands identical
training_provenance.json is BYTE-IDENTICAL between the two reuse runs.

TESTS: tests/test_utterance_cache.py (57, network-free) and
tests/test_utterance_cache_determinism.py (8, real training, skips without a key).
Full suite after: 793 passed / 13 skipped / 1 xfailed, no failures.

CONTRADICTS THE SPEC / CARRY FORWARD:
1. R6 as specified says "keyed by a fingerprint of (seed list, persona IDs,
   generator config, seed value)". Persona IDs are NOT in the key and cannot be:
   computing them requires len(persona_dataset), i.e. downloading PersonaHub,
   which is exactly the cost a hit is supposed to avoid. They are a deterministic
   function of (seed, command_name, num_personas, dataset_size), all of which
   except dataset_size ARE in the key; persona_ids and persona_dataset_size are
   RECORDED in the entry for inspection and for R1's whole-persona holdout. The
   residual exposure is a PersonaHub revision changing row count, which no
   available cheap key can detect.
2. R2 STILL CANNOT CLOSE ON THIS. generate_dspy_examples
   (utils/generate_param_examples.py:333) is a SECOND unseeded LLM call, at
   temperature 0.9, writing <command>_param_labeled.json on every train. R6 does
   not cover it. "Byte-identical artifacts" needs that path cached too (plus
   whatever nondeterminism remains in fine-tuning). Filed as a follow-up.
R6 DELIVERED AND INTEGRATED. Cache at <workflow>/___command_info/utterance_cache/, keyed on a two-part (variant, seed) fingerprint including a source digest of generate_utterances_for_personas -- that function IS the prompt, so any edit invalidates. UTTERANCE_CACHE_MODE in {reuse, regenerate, aggregate, off}; --regenerate-utterances wired on the CLI train subparser and the module parser. MEASURED (this unblocks the R2 chain): at TRAINING_SEED=42 on hello_world, cache off gives 0/5 commands identical across two runs (reproducing M4), cache on gives 5/5, and training_provenance.json is byte-identical. Integration defect I introduced and fixed while wiring R9a: generator_config['persona_source'] was set on the generation path only, so a cache hit (which returns early) omitted it and two runs produced different provenance -- caught by test_provenance_is_byte_identical, not by inspection. Now recorded before the cache is consulted via a new corpus-free personas.active_persona_source_name(). General rule: anything written into provenance must be written on both sides of the cache branch.
close_reason: R6 delivered, integrated and measured: 0/5 -> 5/5 identical utterance sets at a fixed seed on hello_world, byte-identical training_provenance.json. Dependency direction corrected while closing: the graph had R6 depending on R2, which is backwards -- M4 measured that seeding alone does not make training reproducible because the LLM redraws every run, so R2 depends on R6, not the reverse. Edge reversed. R2 now also blocked by fix-czb (generate_dspy_examples, a second unseeded LLM call R6 does not cover).

title: R1b: developer-supplied benchmark file, escalation recall, and seed-disjointness enforcement
description:
ADDRESSES F10 (S2) and completes R1. Escalation recall is not measured anywhere — no test, metric, or log covers it — yet it is the behaviour that makes context hierarchies usable. Any change to `wildcard` trades routing accuracy against escalation silently: the IDO cap moved escalation 91.9% -> 83.8% and nothing in the package would have noticed.

The two axes (spec §2):
- ROUTING — held-out phrasings, scored top-1 and in-list.
- ESCALATION — phrasings aimed at a command that is PROVABLY ABSENT from the tested context's label space but present in one of its ancestors. A confident `wildcard` is the only correct answer, because that is what makes the runtime walk up the parent chain.

DO (spec R1, decision D2):
- Accept an optional developer-supplied benchmark file: utterance -> expected label, plus utterance -> `wildcard` escalation cases. This is what the IDO team built by hand (446 routing + 37 escalation cases) and it is the only thing that told them the truth.
- ENFORCE DISJOINTNESS between the benchmark file and the seed table, and FAIL THE RUN on overlap. The IDO harness caught a real leak this way. Without the check, a benchmark silently decays into a memorisation test the first time someone pastes a failing case into their seeds to "fix" it.
- Report escalation recall as a SEPARATE metric (D2). Never fold it into accuracy — the two trade against each other and one blended score hides the trade.

REFERENCE: tests/eval_intent_benchmark.py in the IDO app-side harness (spec §7) demonstrates both axes plus disjointness enforcement. Illustrative, not a submission.

DEPENDS ON R1a (the held-out evaluation surface this plugs into).
notes:
DELIVERED (wave 1, not yet integrated). The benchmark half of fastworkflow/train/heldout_evaluation.py, with the format documented in docs/intent_benchmark_format.md.

load_benchmark_file plus assert_benchmark_disjoint_from_seeds: hard failure on exact normalised overlap with the seed table, warning on near-duplicates at 0.90 similarity. Without that enforcement a benchmark silently decays into a memorisation test the first time someone pastes a failing case into their seeds to "fix" it.

Escalation recall is scored by score_escalation, and only a LONE confident escalation label counts as correct -- an escalation label buried in a top-k list takes the ambiguity branch at runtime and the signal is discarded (finding F7). Scoring that as a success would measure something the runtime never acts on.

DEFAULT_ESCALATION_LABELS now imports nlu_labels.ESCALATION_LABELS instead of redefining the string, so the trainer, the runtime and the evaluator cannot drift apart. Note parameter_value is non-routable but deliberately NOT an escalation: a bare value says nothing about whether an ancestor can serve the request.

Also reconciled with the determinism work: split_by_persona now expands composite persona ids ("1041+37822", and the __unresolved__: form) to their contributors, and holds a row out only when EVERY contributing persona is held out. Treating a composite id as an opaque persona of its own would have let it be reserved for evaluation while a contributor was still in training -- exactly the leak D1 exists to prevent.
R1b SHIPPED. Developer benchmark file loaded and seed-disjointness enforced BEFORE training, so a leaked benchmark fails fast rather than producing a flattering score -- BenchmarkLeakError verified firing in ~13s. Near-duplicates warn. Escalation recall scored. Two integration defects of my own found and fixed here: fix-588 (escalation was never actually scored -- benchmark_cases_for_context called without its required `kind` argument, and the resulting TypeError was swallowed by a broad guard, so it silently reported nothing) and fix-eia (two of the four benchmark validators had no call site). All four validators now verified to be called.
close_reason: Shipped and integrated; see notes

title: R1a: replace the memorisation metric with whole-persona held-out evaluation
description:
ADDRESSES F1 (S1) — the root blocker of the entire epic. model_pipeline_training.py:914 splits the SAME synthetic utterance set the model trains on:

    train_data, test_data = train_test_split(dataset, test_size=0.25, random_state=42)

Utterances for one command are generated by a handful of personas from one seed list, so a random 25% holdout is near-duplicated in the training 75%. Measured gap on the IDO workflow: ~0.94 reported F1 against 46.2% held-out top-1. There is no held-out concept anywhere in the package. Every other improvement in this epic needs a trustworthy signal to be evaluated against, and the convergence loop is unimplementable without one.

DO (spec R1, decision D1):
- Hold out WHOLE PERSONAS, not random utterances. Holding out 25% of rows from a persona whose other rows are in training IS the defect; holding out every utterance produced by personas k..n is a real generalisation test. Rejected alternative: simply enlarging test_size — that dilutes the leak, it does not fix it.
- Report `top-1` and `in-list` (correct label among returned candidates) separately.
- KEEP the existing in-distribution F1 but LABEL IT AS SUCH, so the number that has been quietly misleading people is still available and no longer misread.

VERIFY: grep -n "train_test_split" fastworkflow/model_pipeline_training.py

DEPENDS ON R2: persona selection must be seeded and recorded before "personas k..n" is a reproducible holdout rather than a different set of personas every run.
notes:
CORRECTION from the adversarial review (fix-551.1, finding AR1): decision D1's claim that whole-persona holdout is 'a real generalisation test' DID NOT SURVIVE and is now stated in a weaker form. Every persona for a command is conditioned on three things identical across any persona split: the full seed list injected verbatim, a keyword bag built from the union of every word of every seed and injected as 'use varied phrasing based on these themes', and the command name. Persona holdout removes only persona-specific styling - the one factor that varies - so both halves remain draws from the same conditional distribution. Personas are also generated in batches within a single completion, so a split that is not batch-aligned shares the sampler, not just the prompt. WHAT THIS CHANGES: whole-persona holdout is strictly better than the random row split and is still worth shipping, but it is NOT a generalisation test and it CANNOT demote the developer-supplied benchmark file (fix-551.6) to optional. The benchmark is the only trustworthy signal. Two cheap string-only leak detectors are recorded in the spec: (1) max token-containment distribution compared across random-split / persona-split / benchmark; (2) the fraction of held-out content tokens appearing in the injected keyword bag.
R1a SHIPPED. heldout_evaluation wired into train(): whole-persona holdout reserved BEFORE training, scored through the real CommandRouter path rather than a reimplementation of it. hello_world: in-distribution F1 0.907 against held-out top-1 90.0% on 30 reserved utterances -- the gap between those two numbers is the whole point of the requirement. Fixed a numpy-array truthiness bug in the predict adaptation (CommandRouter.predict returns an array, used in a boolean context) while wiring it.
close_reason: Shipped and integrated; see notes

title: R3a: a rate-limited command silently becomes unroutable — retry with backoff, never return []
description:
ADDRESSES F3 (S1). train/generate_synthetic.py:120-122:

    except litellm.exceptions.RateLimitError:
        logger.error("LiteLLM Rate limiting error!")
        return []

It returns [] — not the seed utterances, nothing. The caller (model_pipeline_training.py:857-863) zips that empty list with the command name, so the command contributes ZERO rows and ITS LABEL NEVER ENTERS THE CONTEXT'S CLASSIFIER. The command becomes permanently unroutable until the next training run. The only trace is one log line in a run that prints tens of thousands of progress-bar lines.

The correct behaviour already exists ten lines above it: the `datasets`-missing path at generate_synthetic.py:26-32 degrades to `[command_name] + seed_utterances`.

DO (spec R3):
- Retry RateLimitError with exponential backoff.
- On terminal failure, return `[command_name] + seed_utterances` — NEVER []. Match the existing datasets-missing path.
- Make the terminal-failure case loud enough to survive a run that prints tens of thousands of progress-bar lines (this is what the R3b report is for; at minimum it must not be a lone logger.error).

VERIFY: grep -n "RateLimitError" -A 3 fastworkflow/train/generate_synthetic.py ; grep -n "return \[command_name\]" fastworkflow/train/generate_synthetic.py

ACCEPTANCE: an integration test that forces the terminal-failure path shows the command's label present in the trained context classifier. Per the testing rules, no mocks of fastWorkflow components — induce the condition rather than patching it out.
notes: DELIVERED (wave 1, not yet integrated). generate_synthetic.py now retries RateLimitError and similar transient exceptions with exponential backoff + jitter. On terminal failure it returns [command_name] + seeds + whatever was generated, instead of [] -- so a rate-limited command degrades to weak-but-routable rather than silently unroutable (F3). Fallback is recorded on the provenance record (fell_back / fallback_reason) so R3b's report can surface it. Tuning knobs SYNTHETIC_UTTERANCE_GEN_MAX_RETRIES / _RETRY_BASE_SECONDS documented in fastworkflow/examples/fastworkflow.env.
close_reason: R3a delivered. Synthetic utterance generation now retries with backoff on RateLimitError and falls back to the command's seed utterances instead of returning [], so a rate-limited command can no longer end a training run silently unroutable. The fallback is recorded in provenance (fell_back / fallback_reason) rather than only logged, which is what makes it visible to the R3b report (fix-551.4) instead of scrolling past in training output.

title: R2: full determinism — seed everything, record provenance
description:
ADDRESSES F2 (S1). No manual_seed, random.seed, np.random.seed, or set_seed call exists anywhere in the package. The only determinism is random_state=42 on the train/test split. Persona selection is free-running (train/generate_synthetic.py:43: selected_indices = random.sample(range(len(persona_dataset)), num_personas)) and model initialisation is unseeded. Consequence: 20.6% verdict churn between two identical runs (92 of 446 held-out routing cases). This blocks incremental training (a command retrained today is not comparable to its neighbours trained last week), blocks utterance caching (no provenance — see D6, R2 is a HARD prerequisite for R6), and blocks any convergence loop.

DO (spec R2):
- Add a single TRAINING_SEED config value that seeds `random`, `numpy`, and `torch` (including CUDA where applicable). Follow the existing env-var conventions — see the fastworkflow-config-and-flags skill; do not invent a parallel config mechanism.
- Persist, PER COMMAND, the seed and the PERSONA IDS ACTUALLY USED. This provenance record is what R6's cache fingerprint is keyed on, so its shape is load-bearing for a later issue, not just a log.
- Document that unseeded runs on a benchmark of a few hundred cases exhibit ~20% verdict churn, and that differences below that floor are not interpretable from a single run.

VERIFY: grep -rn "manual_seed\|random.seed\|set_seed\|np.random.seed" --include=*.py fastworkflow/ ; grep -n "random.sample" fastworkflow/train/generate_synthetic.py

ACCEPTANCE: two full training runs of tests/example_workflow with the same TRAINING_SEED produce byte-identical (or at minimum verdict-identical) artifacts, and the per-command provenance record round-trips.
notes:
DELIVERED (wave 1, not yet integrated). fastworkflow/train/determinism.py plus a reworked generate_synthetic.py; 27 integration tests in tests/test_training_determinism.py.

Provides seed_everything (random / numpy / torch / CUDA / transformers), derived_seed for stable sub-seeds, the TRAINING_SEED env var, and a process-wide ProvenanceRecorder. The recorder exists because generate_diverse_utterances CANNOT return provenance: its signature is public API, called from user-authored command files in every workflow. It pushes into a module-level sink that the trainer installs for the duration of a run and collects afterwards.

CAUTION -- seeding alone does NOT deliver determinism, so this issue is not done when the module lands. See AR5 in docs/intent_training_improvements_spec.md section 10, and blocker fix-9mo (p0), which covers BOTH consequences of non-deterministic set iteration:
  1. LABEL LOSS: core-command labels silently vanish from ancestor contexts depending on PYTHONHASHSEED, which can make a command unroutable.
  2. ROW ORDER: model_pipeline_training.py:872-877 appends wildcard rows in set order, and :914 train_test_split(random_state=42) shuffles by POSITION -- so the fixed seed is false reassurance. Empirically confirmed: same 30 rows, 3 PYTHONHASHSEED values, 3 different test partitions.

This blocks paired comparison of two runs, and therefore blocks R1 (is score X better than Y?) and D6 (utterance cache reuse). fix-9mo must close before fix-551.2 can.

--- BLOCKER ADDED: seeding is not sufficient, measured ---
Two runs at TRAINING_SEED=42, same code and env, produced DIFFERENT training data:
0/5 commands had identical utterance sets, with row counts differing by up to 5
(add_two_numbers 24 vs 29). Synthetic utterances come from a live LLM, which no seed
controls. See the measurement recorded on fix-551.9.

R2 therefore has TWO blockers, not one:
  fix-9mo    ordering (set iteration -> label loss and row order)
  fix-551.9  utterance persistence (R6), now p0, without which the training DATA
             varies run to run and no seed can make the artifacts reproducible

R2's acceptance test should be: two consecutive runs at the same seed produce
byte-identical per-context artifacts. Do not close this issue on "seed_everything is
wired in".
CLOSING R2. Evidence, stated at the strength it actually has:

CLAIM: two runs at a fixed TRAINING_SEED produce identical artifacts, measured on hello_world and messaging_app_4, on a CUDA machine WITHOUT deterministic-algorithm enforcement. Not the broader claim 'training is deterministic'.

It took three findings to get here, and only the first was foreseen:
1. Seeding alone does nothing -- 0/5 commands identical at the same seed, because the LLM redraws the training data every run. This inverted D6's sequencing: R6 blocks R2, not the reverse.
2. There were TWO LLM generation paths, not one. R6 fixed utterances; generate_dspy_examples was still unseeded at temperature 0.9 (fix-czb). Parameter files went 0/1 -> 1/1 on hello_world and 0/5 -> 5/5 on messaging_app_4.
3. Fine-tuning was ALREADY reproducible and needed no change: artifacts were byte-identical in every condition measured (24/24 and 96/96), including cache-off runs where the training data itself differed. determinism.seed_everything is sufficient here.

METHODOLOGY CORRECTION worth carrying forward (spec section M6): measuring reproducibility on hello_world ALONE is not evidence. Its parameter fields are already alphabetical, so it structurally cannot detect key-ordering divergence -- an earlier version of the param cache scored 5/5 there while leaving 3/5 artifacts differing on messaging_app_4. Any future determinism claim needs a workflow with non-alphabetical fields.

RESIDUAL RISK, not papered over: nothing sets torch.use_deterministic_algorithms or cudnn.deterministic, so a different GPU, cuDNN version, or batch shape could reintroduce drift. Two workflows measured, not all.
close_reason: Determinism achieved: seed + R6 utterance cache + fix-czb param cache; verified on 2 workflows
