title: Synthetic generator emits the literal prompt token 'utterance' as a training row
description:
The utterance-generation prompt in fastworkflow/train/generate_synthetic.py:320-324 ends with a verbatim format template:

    Format your response exactly as follows:
    [Persona_Name]
    utterance
    utterance
    ...

The LLM sometimes echoes those template lines literally, and the response parser does not filter them out. generate_synthetic.py:382-383 keeps any line with len(u) > 3 that does not start with '[', and the bare string 'utterance' is 9 characters, so it is admitted as a generated training utterance.

MEASURED, retail_workflow, TRAINING_SEED=42, 4 personas x 5 utterances (from the R6 utterance cache of the E-PV1 run, so it is byte-exact and re-checkable):
  21 of 412 generated rows (5.1%) are the literal string 'utterance'
  spread across 7 of the 19 commands:
    IntentDetection/what_can_i_do    5/25   (20% of that command's generated rows)
    find_user_id_by_email            4/24
    find_user_id_by_name_zip         4/24
    modify_user_address              2/22
    get_order_details                2/28
    cancel_pending_order             2/22
    modify_pending_order_items       2/22

REPRODUCE:
  python -c "import json,glob,collections;c=collections.Counter();[c.update({json.load(open(f))['command_name']:sum(1 for u in json.load(open(f))['entries']['42']['generated_utterances'] if u.strip().lower()=='utterance')}) for f in glob.glob('.pv_tradeoff_cache/utterance_cache_seed42/*.json')];print({k:v for k,v in c.items() if v})"

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A 5% NOISE RATE. The SAME contentless token is trained as a positive example for SEVEN DIFFERENT real commands. That is not merely a wasted row, it is a row that teaches the classifier a contradiction: an input carrying no lexical content is evidence for what_can_i_do AND find_user_id_by_email AND cancel_pending_order simultaneously. Its gradient contribution pushes those classes toward the contentless region of input space.

This was found while measuring fix-2m5's alleged mechanism on retail (see docs/experiments/E-PV1_parameter_value_tradeoff_retail.md). It is a confound for that whole line of work: fix-2m5 reasons about which class owns the low-content region of input space, and this bug silently puts real commands into that region for reasons that have nothing to do with their intent. Any future measurement of parameter_value competition should be re-run after this is fixed, because the row counts it reasons about are contaminated.

Secondary observation, same parser: the len(u) > 3 filter is the only content check anywhere in the path, so any echoed instruction or preamble longer than 3 characters becomes a training row. A stricter reading would drop lines that exactly match tokens from the prompt template ('utterance', 'Persona_Name', '...') and would log how many rows were rejected, so contamination is visible in training_provenance.json rather than invisible.

NOT FIXED HERE: found during a measurement task that is scoped to measuring rather than changing behaviour, and fixing it would invalidate the cached utterances the in-flight E-PV1 experiment is paired on.
notes: FIXED by the integrator. Root cause at generate_synthetic.py: the system prompt demonstrates its output format using the literal word 'utterance' as the placeholder, and models copy the scaffolding through. Neither existing filter catches it -- 'utterance' is 9 chars so len(u)>3 passes it, and it does not start with '['. Verified independently in cached artifacts BEFORE fixing: list_all_product_types has 7 generated_utterances whose value is exactly 'utterance', across 10+ command caches. Live production data defect, not a measurement artifact. FIX: _is_template_echo() drops it at extraction. Deliberately did NOT reword the prompt -- that changes the training-data distribution for every command in every workflow in an unmeasured way. The filter is in the R6 cache fingerprint alongside the generator; without that, editing it would leave cached entries looking valid under a filter that had changed, a determinism hole of exactly the kind R6 exists to close. tests/test_template_echo_filter.py (23 tests) pins the echoes AND the boundary.
close_reason: Fixed: template echo filtered at extraction, in R6 fingerprint, 23 tests

title: parameter_value belongs in a pre-classifier gate, not the intent label space
description:
The bare-value catcher and the intent classifier are fighting over one softmax, and
re-sizing or re-weighting the class cannot separate them (measured, see fix-2m5).

MEASURED FACT THIS RESTS ON (not a hypothesis): on examples/hello_world, 10 seeds per
configuration, paired on identical utterances, every reduction of the parameter_value
class improved routing and cost the HELD-OUT bare-value catch at a ratio of roughly
2-3 verdicts lost per verdict gained. Shrinking the class from 7 rows to 2 took the
fix-2m5 probes from 33/40 to 39/40 and the held-out bare-value catch from 57/70 to
2/70. At equal row count, WHICH literals are kept made no difference on either axis --
so it is the size of the class's decision region, and that region IS the capability.
Loss weighting over a 15x range did nothing at all (fix-551.13).

The structural reading: parameter_value is a label in the intent-detection label space
whose job belongs to a different stage. A bare literal ("3", "france", "id=3636") is
recognisable without a trained classifier, and while it sits inside the same softmax as
the real commands it will keep beating some of them on lexical proximity -- an
arithmetic command is genuinely close to "25.73 and Howard St".

TWO CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, NEITHER MEASURED. Both need their own experiment and both
must be judged on BOTH axes (D2) with a paired test (R8):

(a) A pre-classifier gate ahead of intent detection: cheap, deterministic, "is this a
    bare literal with no verb / no command-shaped content?". If it fires, resolve to
    PARAMETER_VALUE_LABEL directly and never consult the classifier; parameter_value
    then leaves the trained label space entirely, taking its competition with it.
    Risk to check: the gate's false-positive rate on short real commands ("go up").
(b) Calibrated abstention at the router. Section 11 M2 records that there is no
    out-of-scope rejection anywhere (fix-d28), and that the only rejection mechanism is
    a threshold computed as the MEAN CONFIDENCE OF MISCLASSIFIED TEST SAMPLES -- a
    descriptive statistic of the training run, not an operating point. A calibrated
    threshold would serve this, fix-d28, and F7 at once.

(a) and (b) are complementary, not alternatives. (a) is the smaller change and does not
depend on fixing calibration; (b) is the more general and is already independently
motivated.

DO NOT re-attempt this by removing parameter_value from intent detection WITHOUT
putting (a) in front of it. The class earns its place: without either the class or the
gate, "france" routes to whichever real command is lexically nearest, which is worse
than today.
close_reason: Duplicate of fix-cm2, created by a bd write-loss retry (fix-46c). fix-cm2 is the authoritative copy.

title: parameter_value belongs in a pre-classifier gate, not the intent label space
description:
The bare-value catcher and the intent classifier are fighting over one softmax, and
re-sizing or re-weighting the class cannot separate them (measured, see fix-2m5).

MEASURED FACT THIS RESTS ON (not a hypothesis): on examples/hello_world, 10 seeds per
configuration, paired on identical utterances, every reduction of the parameter_value
class improved routing and cost the HELD-OUT bare-value catch at a ratio of roughly
2-3 verdicts lost per verdict gained. Shrinking the class from 7 rows to 2 took the
fix-2m5 probes from 33/40 to 39/40 and the held-out bare-value catch from 57/70 to
2/70. At equal row count, WHICH literals are kept made no difference on either axis --
so it is the size of the class's decision region, and that region IS the capability.
Loss weighting over a 15x range did nothing at all (fix-551.13).

The structural reading: parameter_value is a label in the intent-detection label space
whose job belongs to a different stage. A bare literal ("3", "france", "id=3636") is
recognisable without a trained classifier, and while it sits inside the same softmax as
the real commands it will keep beating some of them on lexical proximity -- an
arithmetic command is genuinely close to "25.73 and Howard St".

TWO CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, NEITHER MEASURED. Both need their own experiment and both
must be judged on BOTH axes (D2) with a paired test (R8):

(a) A pre-classifier gate ahead of intent detection: cheap, deterministic, "is this a
    bare literal with no verb / no command-shaped content?". If it fires, resolve to
    PARAMETER_VALUE_LABEL directly and never consult the classifier; parameter_value
    then leaves the trained label space entirely, taking its competition with it.
    Risk to check: the gate's false-positive rate on short real commands ("go up").
(b) Calibrated abstention at the router. Section 11 M2 records that there is no
    out-of-scope rejection anywhere (fix-d28), and that the only rejection mechanism is
    a threshold computed as the MEAN CONFIDENCE OF MISCLASSIFIED TEST SAMPLES -- a
    descriptive statistic of the training run, not an operating point. A calibrated
    threshold would serve this, fix-d28, and F7 at once.

(a) and (b) are complementary, not alternatives. (a) is the smaller change and does not
depend on fixing calibration; (b) is the more general and is already independently
motivated.

DO NOT re-attempt this by removing parameter_value from intent detection WITHOUT
putting (a) in front of it. The class earns its place: without either the class or the
gate, "france" routes to whichever real command is lexically nearest, which is worse
than today.
notes:
--- E-PV1: YOUR PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD AT RETAIL SCALE. READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTING EITHER
    DIRECTION. (agent, 2026-08-02) ---

Card: docs/experiments/E-PV1_parameter_value_tradeoff_retail.md
30 runs, 6 arms x 5 seeds, examples/retail_workflow (19 labels), fixed 72-case external
benchmark, variance floor measured at EXACTLY ZERO so every effect below is all-signal.
Full detail and the confounds are on fix-2m5.

This issue's stated premise is 'the bare-value catcher and the intent classifier are
fighting over one softmax'. On retail they are not fighting at all, and the direction of
the problem is reversed.

1. THERE IS NO FIGHT TO SEPARATE. parameter_value takes top-1 on 0 of 360 routing cases.
   Wilson 95% [0.000, 0.011]. It is not even in the runtime candidate list on one case.
   Median rank among 20 classes: 15th. The 'arithmetic command is genuinely close to
   "25.73 and Howard St"' intuition is right about the direction and wrong about the
   winner: on retail, calculate WINS that literal outright and parameter_value is nowhere
   near it.

2. THE MEASURED FACT THIS ISSUE RESTS ON DOES NOT GENERALISE. 'Every reduction of the
   parameter_value class improved routing' is hello_world-specific. On retail:
     7 rows -> 220/360 routing, 5/35 catch
     4 rows -> 227/360 (+1.9pp, p=0.450), 10/35 catch   <-- BOTH AXES IMPROVED
     2 rows -> 229/360 (+2.5pp, p=0.298), 0/35
     0 rows -> 218/360 (-0.6pp, p=0.906), 0/35
   No significant routing gain at any level. pv4 improving both axes is impossible under a
   trade-off model. What capping actually does on retail is perturb the boundary: pv4 moved
   63 of 360 verdicts (35 fixed, 28 broken) for a net +7, against a zero noise floor.

3. THE MECHANISM IS REAL BUT 12x TOO WEAK TO MATTER HERE. Both directional predictions of
   'no semantic centre, expands into unclaimed space' hold:
     Spearman rho(P(parameter_value), P(best real)) = -0.405 over 360 cases
     stripping words raises P(pv) 0.014 -> 0.034 (2.5x), up in 35/40 paired probes, p=1e-5
   But P(pv) > P(best real) in 0 of 360 cases, and at the shortest utterances pv holds
   0.034 against the best real command's 0.405. So a pre-classifier gate would be aimed at
   a force that exists and is an order of magnitude short of causing a single error at this
   scale. The sharpened mechanism -- the low-content region goes to whichever class has the
   most low-content TRAINING ROWS, not to whichever class is contentless -- explains both
   workflows and predicts WHICH class wins, which the original does not.

4. THE THING TO ACTUALLY FIX IS THE OPPOSITE, AND IT NEEDS NO ARCHITECTURE CHANGE.
   Exploratory arm, 28 diverse literals instead of 7 (all disjoint from the probes):
     held-out bare-value catch  5/35 -> 35/35, PERFECT AT EVERY SEED (p = 0.0000)
     routing top-1              -0.8pp (p = 0.804), i.e. free
     steals                     3/360 (p = 0.250), still essentially zero
   The capability IS recoverable inside the softmax on retail, by adding coverage. I
   predicted at most 2/7 and got 7/7 -- this is the single largest effect in the experiment
   and it was found in the direction nobody was sweeping.

5. A SPECIFIC HAZARD FOR DIRECTION (a), THE PRE-CLASSIFIER LEXICAL GATE. This issue already
   flags 'the gate's false-positive rate on short real commands ("go up")'. Retail shows a
   second and worse case: a gate that intercepts bare literals must decide '32 * 4',
   '16.7,.002' and 'id=3636'. On retail 'calculate' is a REAL command whose entire domain
   IS bare numeric literals, and it legitimately wins them (24 of 70 bare-value probes).
   A gate firing before the classifier would resolve those to PARAMETER_VALUE_LABEL and
   make calculate unreachable from its own natural input. So the gate is not merely
   risky on short commands, it is UNSOUND on any workflow with a literal-domain command
   (arithmetic, id lookup, code/ref entry). If (a) is built, it needs a way for a command
   to claim a literal shape, and that is a bigger design than 'is this a bare literal'.

6. DIRECTION (b), CALIBRATED ABSTENTION, IS UNAFFECTED BY THIS AND LOOKS BETTER FOR IT.
   Retail's real failure mode is 'the catcher LEADS but cannot CLOSE': parameter_value is
   top-1 on 31 of 70 bare values yet yields a clean catch on only 5/35, because an
   unconfident classifier returns its top-3 and a real command stays on the menu, so the
   turn never resolves to command_name=None. That is precisely an operating-point problem,
   which is what (b) addresses and (a) does not. It is also consistent with the note here
   that the only rejection mechanism is a threshold computed as the mean confidence of
   misclassified test samples -- a descriptive statistic, not an operating point.

RECOMMENDATION. Do not implement (a) on the strength of the hello_world curve. Before
either direction: (i) re-justify at retail scale, since the competition the gate removes
does not occur there; (ii) test whether reserved-class COVERAGE alone is sufficient, which
is one cheap arm away and already looks decisive; (iii) if (a) proceeds, resolve the
literal-domain-command conflict in item 5 first. (b) can proceed on its own independent
motivation.

Both arms of a future test are already runnable without harness changes:
  .venv/bin/python tests/measure_parameter_value_tradeoff.py --seeds 42 7 1234 2026 99
Adding an arm is a dict entry in ARMS.

CAVEAT: measured on top of fix-iy0 (5% of generated rows are the literal token 'utterance',
injected into 7 real command classes) which pushes toward these results; and see fix-16d.
n = 1 workflow at this scale, and retail is unusual in owning calculate.
DO NOT BUILD -- premise inverted by the retail multi-seed measurement (30 runs). fix-cm2 assumed parameter_value is too STRONG and steals mass from real commands. On retail it takes top-1 on 0 of 360 routing cases (Wilson 95% [0.000, 0.011], median rank 15/20) -- it is too WEAK. Raising it from 7 to 28 diverse literals took bare-value catch from 5/35 to 35/35 at every seed for -0.8pp routing (p=0.804). Coverage, not gating. CONCRETE HAZARD: a lexical pre-gate would intercept '32 * 4' and 'id=3636' and route them away from `calculate`, a real retail command whose seed utterances ARE arithmetic -- making a command unreachable from its own natural input. Closing wontfix.
close_reason: wontfix: premise inverted by retail measurement

title: generate_dspy_examples is a second unseeded LLM call: R6 alone does not make training reproducible
description:
R6's utterance cache makes the INTENT training data byte-identical across runs at a fixed seed (verified: 5/5 hello_world commands identical, training_provenance.json byte-identical). It does not cover the parameter-extraction example path.

fastworkflow/utils/generate_param_examples.py:312 generate_dspy_examples runs at a hardcoded temperature of 0.9 (line 335) with no seed anywhere in the file, and writes <command>_param_labeled.json on every train. Two runs at the same TRAINING_SEED therefore still produce different DSPy few-shot examples, so 'two runs produce byte-identical artifacts' remains false even with the cache on.

Options, roughly in order of cost: (a) extend the R6 cache to this call, which is the same shape of problem and the same solution -- fingerprint the prompt source, the model, the seeds and the config, and reuse; (b) drop the temperature to 0 and pass a seed where the provider supports it, which reduces but does not eliminate drift; (c) declare parameter examples out of scope for determinism and say so in the spec.

(a) is the consistent answer: the argument for caching utterances applies unchanged here.

Also unquantified: whatever nondeterminism remains inside fine-tuning itself, after both LLM paths are pinned. R2 should not close until that is measured rather than assumed.
notes:
DELIVERED (not yet integrated -- needs a 3-line patch to train/__main__.py, see below).

New module fastworkflow/train/param_example_cache.py: a SIBLING of utterance_cache,
not a generalisation of it. Generic parts imported from utterance_cache (Fingerprint,
source_digest, callable_identity, normalize_mode, slugify, atomic_write_model -- the
last two promoted from private to public there, no behaviour change). The payload is
what differs: an utterance entry is strings + persona attribution + a cross-seed union;
a param entry is two lists of dicts where persona is meaningless and a union would
silently change how many few-shot examples DSPy gets.

Cache at <workflow>/___command_info/param_example_cache/<cmd>.<variant>.json, keyed
(variant, seed). CACHE_DIRNAME added to artifact_versioning.RESERVED_TOPLEVEL_NAMES so
prune/publish/migrate skip it. Mode via PARAM_EXAMPLE_CACHE_MODE, falling back to
UTTERANCE_CACHE_MODE so --regenerate-utterances refreshes BOTH LLM paths. aggregate ==
reuse. Empty draws are never cached (same ruling as R6).

Fingerprint: command_name, digest of str(model_fields), digest of extract_field_details
output, num_examples, validation_threshold, temperature, model, digest of
LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE, completion backend name, and a SHA-256 over the source of
generate_dspy_examples + extract_field_details + transform_examples_to_dict_format +
validate_parameters + normalized_levenshtein_distance + normalize_text + canonicalized.
Excluded: API key (identifies a caller, not a generator), max_tokens (a literal inside
the digested function).

MEASURED, TRAINING_SEED=42, two back-to-back full trains per condition, real LLM:
  hello_world      cache off: 0/1 param files identical (0 of 15 examples shared)
  hello_world      cache on : 1/1
  messaging_app_4  cache off: 0/5 (1 of 75 examples shared)
  messaging_app_4  cache on : 5/5
Model artifacts (.pth, threshold.json, label_encoder.pkl, ambiguous thresholds) were
byte-identical in EVERY condition: 24/24 hello_world, 96/96 messaging_app_4, on a CUDA
box. So determinism.seed_everything is already sufficient for the fine-tuning half; the
LLM draws were the only thing left. No new bd issue needed for residual nondeterminism.

CAUGHT BY THE SECOND WORKFLOW: hello_world alone would have shipped a bug. A generated
example is built in regex-match order (command, strings, bools, numbers) while a cached
one round-trips through json.dump(sort_keys=True), which sorts nested keys too. The
dicts compare EQUAL and serialise to DIFFERENT bytes. hello_world hid it (command <
first_number < second_number is already alphabetical); messaging_app_4 showed 2/5 with
every example identical. Fixed by canonicalized() applied on BOTH paths -> 5/5.

TEMPERATURE: left at 0.9, deliberately, now a named constant DSPY_EXAMPLE_TEMPERATURE
in the fingerprint. Lowering it would be a training-data QUALITY change disguised as a
determinism fix, and no hosted provider guarantees bitwise-identical output at
temperature 0 anyway. Caching is sufficient for R2 as stated.

Tests: tests/test_param_example_cache.py (41, no network, no mocks -- real files, real
Pydantic models, real exceptions) and tests/test_param_example_determinism.py (trains
hello_world twice end to end, skips without a real API key).
DELIVERED, NOT YET WIRED. fastworkflow/train/param_example_cache.py is a sibling to R6's utterance cache, sharing the plumbing (Fingerprint, source_digest, callable_identity, normalize_mode, slugify, atomic_write_model) but not the entry model -- an utterance entry is strings with persona attribution and a defined cross-seed union; a parameter entry is dicts where persona is meaningless and a union would silently change HOW MANY few-shot examples the runtime gets. Merging them would have produced one model whose fields are always empty for one of its two users.

MEASURED at TRAINING_SEED=42 with the real LLM, two back-to-back full trains per condition: <command>_param_labeled.json went 0/1 -> 1/1 identical on hello_world and 0/5 -> 5/5 on messaging_app_4.

TEMPERATURE STAYS AT 0.9, now a named constant and in the fingerprint so a future change invalidates loudly. Lowering it would not fix the FIRST draw at a new fingerprint (no hosted provider guarantees bitwise-identical completions at temperature 0), and the prompt explicitly asks for diverse examples, so collapsing it is a training-data QUALITY change disguised as a determinism fix.

INTEGRATION HELD: the 3-line patch to train/__main__.py is not applied yet, because the R5 selective-training work was concurrently writing that same file (the file changed between a grep and a read seconds apart). Applying it during another agent's write risks a lost update. Apply after R5 lands, then re-run tests/test_param_example_determinism.py.

Verified independently by the integrator: canonicalized() is applied on BOTH the generation path (generate_param_examples.py:800-801) and the cache-hit path (523-524), which is what makes the byte-identity hold rather than merely the dict equality.
WIRED AND VERIFIED. train/__main__.py now installs ParamExampleCache around _generate_dspy_examples_helper, bracketed in try/finally, before the version is cut. cli.py --regenerate-utterances help text updated to name both caches (the env fallback already made the flag refresh both).

CLOSED A GAP THE DELIVERY DID NOT COVER: tests/test_param_example_determinism.py installs the cache handle ITSELF (line 200) so it can run standalone. So does the utterance-cache determinism suite. That means the entire test suite passed identically whether or not the production path installed the cache -- `fastworkflow train` could have gone on being non-reproducible with 929 tests green, which is exactly the state the repo was in between delivery and integration. Added tests/test_cache_installation_wiring.py (8 tests) asserting all three module-level handles (param cache, utterance cache, provenance recorder) are installed AND torn down in finally, and that install precedes generation precedes teardown -- ordering matters because installing after the generator ran would be a no-op that still passes a naive 'is it installed' check. These tests would have failed before this patch.

Suite: 963 passed, 14 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed.
close_reason: Wired into train_workflow + installation guard tests added

title: R1b benchmark validators are never called: seed/benchmark disjointness is not enforced
description:
fastworkflow/train/heldout_evaluation.py defines four guard functions that the spec (R1) and docs/intent_benchmark_format.md describe as active:

  assert_benchmark_disjoint_from_seeds   -- raises BenchmarkLeakError on overlap
  find_near_duplicate_benchmark_cases    -- warns on near-duplicates
  validate_routing_cases                 -- expected_label must be in the context label space
  validate_escalation_cases              -- expected command must be ABSENT locally and PRESENT in an ancestor

None of them has a call site outside tests/. Verify:

  rg -n 'assert_benchmark_disjoint_from_seeds|find_near_duplicate_benchmark_cases|validate_escalation_cases|validate_routing_cases' -g '*.py' . | grep -v tests/ | grep -v heldout_evaluation.py
  -> no output

model_pipeline_training.train() loads the benchmark with load_benchmark_file() and scores it directly, skipping every guard.

WHY THIS MATTERS MOST: docs/intent_benchmark_format.md line 77 states 'assert_benchmark_disjoint_from_seeds() fails the run if any benchmark utterance is also a seed utterance. Without that check a benchmark decays into a memorisation test the first time someone pastes a failing case into their seeds to fix it.' That is exactly right about the hazard and currently wrong about the mitigation -- a developer reading the doc will believe they are protected. Spec R1 lists 'ENFORCE DISJOINTNESS ... and FAIL THE RUN on overlap' as a requirement, and the IDO harness caught a real leak this way.

Secondary: an invalid routing case (expected_label not in that context's label space) can never pass and silently drags the reported score down for a benchmark defect rather than a model failure; an invalid escalation case scores a behaviour that was never tested.

DO: call the guards from the training path -- disjointness against the seed table as a hard failure before scoring, near-duplicates and case validation as warnings. Seed utterances per command are available from the command directory / Signature.plain_utterances, and per-command seed counts already land in training_provenance.json.

Found while verifying code claims for fix-551.15 (R8 skill re-point). Not fixed: that task is docs/skill-only and forbidden from editing fastworkflow/. Related: fix-588 (the escalation scoring call raises TypeError in the same block). docs/intent_benchmark_format.md should be corrected or the code wired up -- preferably the latter.
close_reason: FIXED. Half stale, half correct: assert_benchmark_disjoint_from_seeds and find_near_duplicate_benchmark_cases were wired into train() shortly before this was filed; validate_routing_cases and validate_escalation_cases were genuinely uncalled and are now invoked in the same pre-flight block, logging 'Benchmark defect: ...' warnings. Warn not raise for those two: a leak silently turns the evaluation into a memorisation score and must abort, whereas a malformed case only mis-scores itself. All four now have call sites in model_pipeline_training.py (887, 890, 911, 913).

title: heldout evaluation never scores escalation: benchmark_cases_for_context called without required 'kind'
description:
model_pipeline_training.py:1362 calls heldout_evaluation.benchmark_cases_for_context(cases, ctx_name) with two positional arguments, but the function signature is (cases, context, kind) and 'kind' has no default (fastworkflow/train/heldout_evaluation.py:783-789). Every call therefore raises TypeError: benchmark_cases_for_context() missing 1 required positional argument: 'kind'.

The call sits inside the try/except Exception at model_pipeline_training.py:1354-1372, so the failure is swallowed into report.notes as 'held-out evaluation failed: ...' plus a logger.error. Consequence: for any workflow that supplies <workflow>/intent_benchmark.json, report.escalation is ALWAYS None and escalation recall is never measured -- which is exactly the F10 blindness R1b exists to remove. report.routing is assigned before the raise so routing survives, making the failure easy to miss.

REPRODUCE (no training run needed):
  .venv/bin/python -c "from fastworkflow.train import heldout_evaluation as he; he.benchmark_cases_for_context([], 'X')"
  -> TypeError: benchmark_cases_for_context() missing 1 required positional argument: 'kind'

FIX: pass kind='escalation' at the call site.

SECOND OBSERVATION, same call site, probably a separate decision: even with the arity fixed, the developer-supplied benchmark's ROUTING cases are never scored. score_routing (line 1356) is only ever given the persona-holdout records. Per spec R1/AR1 the benchmark file is the primary generalisation instrument and persona holdout cannot substitute for it, so its routing cases should feed score_routing too (reported separately from, or merged with, the persona-holdout routing score -- that is a design call).

Found while verifying code claims for fix-551.15 (R8 skill re-point). Not fixed: that task is docs/skill-only and forbidden from editing fastworkflow/.
close_reason: FIXED and covered by a regression test. model_pipeline_training.py now passes kind='escalation' to benchmark_cases_for_context, and also scores the benchmark's routing cases into a new HeldoutReport.benchmark_routing field (kept separate from the persona-holdout 'routing' score because they are different populations and only the benchmark is pairable across runs). Root cause of the miss: every existing test either trained without a benchmark file or expected the leak guard to abort before scoring, so the escalation branch was never executed. tests/test_train_modern_stack.py::test_benchmark_routing_cases_are_scored now trains with a clean benchmark and asserts a score came back AND that no 'evaluation failed' note was swallowed.

title: parameter_value competes with real commands in intent detection (needs R7.2 cap / R7.3 weighting)
description:
The parameter_value class (7 contentless bare-value literals) competes with, and sometimes
beats, real commands during INTENT DETECTION. Measured on hello_world after the R7.1 split
and the wave-1 integration.

MEASUREMENT (5 training runs of tests/../examples/hello_world, one per TRAINING_SEED,
everything else identical; label space is
['IntentDetection/go_up','IntentDetection/reset_context','IntentDetection/what_can_i_do',
 'IntentDetection/what_is_current_context','add_two_numbers','parameter_value'])

  utterance            expected          correct
  'add 2 and 3'        add_two_numbers      4/5
  'add two numbers'    add_two_numbers      5/5
  'sum 5 and 7'        add_two_numbers      3/5
  'what can i do'      what_can_i_do        5/5

The failures are CONFIDENT single-label predictions of parameter_value, not ambiguity.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM R7.1. The pre-wave-1 committed artifacts for the same workflow give
'add 2 and 3'->add_two_numbers, 'add two numbers'->add_two_numbers, 'sum 5 and 7'->wildcard.
The same seven literals were previously trained under the 'wildcard' label, so the same
competition existed; only the winning label's NAME changed. 'sum 5 and 7' failed at
baseline too. The observed spread is the ~20% verdict churn F2 documents.

WHY IT HAPPENS: the seven literals include '3', '16.7,.002' and '25.73 and Howard St'.
Against an arithmetic command whose utterances are 'add 2 and 3' / 'sum 5 and 7', a
"numbers joined by and" pattern is lexically closer to the placeholder class than to the
command. In a workflow with ONE real command, 7 contentless rows are a large share of the
label mass.

THIS IS THE TARGET FOR R7.2 / R7.3, and it gives them a concrete acceptance number:
  fix-551.12 (R7.2, cap the class by budget) -- parameter_value needs the same budget
    treatment as the ancestor wildcard class. It is currently uncapped at 7 rows in EVERY
    context regardless of how many real utterances that context has.
  fix-551.13 (R7.3, class weighting) -- a context with one real command and one 7-row
    reserved class is exactly the imbalance that issue exists for.
Target: 5/5 on all four probes across seeds, without losing the bare-value catch (a bare
'3' or 'france' must still resolve to a non-routable label).

DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY REMOVING parameter_value FROM INTENT DETECTION. It earns its place:
a bare value typed at a command prompt resolves to a non-routable label, then to
command_name=None, then to you_misunderstood. Without the class, 'france' would route to
whichever real command is lexically nearest, which is worse. The problem is its WEIGHT,
not its existence.

SIDE EFFECT ON THE TEST SUITE: tests/test_train_modern_stack.py::test_trained_model_routes_utterance
asserts 'add 2 and 3' routes to add_two_numbers. It was previously flaky (an unseeded coin
flip). Now that training is seeded (R2), seed 42 -- the default -- is one of the draws
where parameter_value wins, so the flake has become a deterministic failure. Determinism
did not cause the defect; it made an existing one reproducible.
notes:
CROSS-RUN EVIDENCE from the R3b work. In one real hello_world run, IntentDetection/what_can_i_do was the healthiest command in the workflow by every input measure (38 rows, 12 seeds, the only command classified healthy) and scored 0 of 5 on held-out routing. In a separate run of the same workflow the same command was fine and add_two_numbers scored 15/15. Two consequences: row count is not a proxy for accuracy (R3b's report grew a NEVER ROUTED section it was not asked for), and a command flipping between 0/5 and healthy across runs of the SAME workflow is another instance of the M4 finding that generation is not reproducible at a fixed seed. Until R6's utterance cache lands, any single-run measurement of label competition -- including the one that got test_trained_model_routes_utterance marked xfail -- is a sample of one from a distribution we cannot hold still. Do not tune class budgets (R7.2/R7.3) against single-run numbers.

--- WAVE 2: NEITHER R7.2 NOR R7.3 CAN FIX THIS. THE TARGET IS UNREACHABLE BY EITHER
    LEVER, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL. --- (agent, 2026-08-02)

MEASUREMENT: tests/measure_class_balance.py, examples/hello_world, 10 TRAINING_SEED
values per configuration, paired within a seed on BYTE-IDENTICAL utterances (the
harness caches _get_utterances and replays it, so the M4 confound is removed). Two
axes reported separately per D2. 7 HELD-OUT bare values, none of them a training
literal -- probing with the seven literals measures memorisation, and any config that
removes a literal scores 0 on it by construction. The whole sweep was repeated end to
end and reproduced cell for cell.

BASELINE REPRODUCES THIS ISSUE at 10 seeds (vs the 5 recorded above):
  'add 2 and 3'      7/10   (was 4/5)
  'add two numbers' 10/10   (was 5/5)
  'sum 5 and 7'      6/10   (was 3/5)
  'what can i do'   10/10   (was 5/5)
Held-out bare-value catch 57/70. Failures are still confident lone parameter_value
predictions.

1. R7.2's CAP CANNOT BIND. parameter_value is a fixed 7-row literal list. The
   re-derived budget is ratio * own_rows floored at the literal count, and
   hello_world's five commands contribute ~150 rows, so the budget is ~150 and the
   class is untouched. This is now a regression test in tests/test_class_balance.py so
   nobody later claims otherwise.

2. R7.3's WEIGHTING DOES NOTHING. Four schemes, twelve paired comparisons, no
   improvement on any axis; details in fix-551.13. A 15x swing in the reserved class's
   loss weight is indistinguishable from noise.

3. WHAT DOES MOVE IT -- AND WHY IT IS NOT A FIX. Removing ROWS from parameter_value
   improves routing and destroys the bare-value catch, roughly one for one, and the
   exchange rate is bad:

     config                        rows  fix-2m5  bare-value(held-out)  routing p  bare p
     baseline                         7    33/40   57/70                     --      --
     drop 1 literal (street)          6    34/40   46/70                  1.000   0.019
     drop 2 numeric colliders         5    38/40   31/70                  0.027   0.000
     earliest-first cap to 5          5    37/40   26/70                  0.023   0.000
     earliest-first cap to 2          2    39/40    2/70                  0.001   0.000

   param_rows_2 reaches 39/40 -- essentially the acceptance target -- and catches 2 of
   70 held-out bare values. That is exactly the trade this issue forbids.

   AT EQUAL ROW COUNT (5) the two variants behave the same on both axes, so a
   PREDICTION MADE BEFORE THE RUN IS REFUTED: it is not about WHICH literals are kept.
   The colliding literals ('16.7,.002', '25.73 and Howard St') are not the cause. It
   is the SIZE of the class's decision region, and that region is the capability.

CONCLUSION: routing accuracy against parameter_value and the bare-value catch are the
SAME DIAL, not two dials. Every point of one is bought with two to three of the other.
No setting of a row budget or a loss weight escapes that, because both levers only move
the dial. The target as written -- 5/5 on the four probes with the catch intact -- is
not reachable by re-sizing or re-weighting this class.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY BE NEEDED (design, NOT measured -- do not cite as a result):
the bare-value decision does not belong in the intent-detection label space at all. A
bare literal is recognisable without a classifier, and while it competes lexically with
real commands inside one softmax it will keep winning some of them. Two candidate
directions, both needing their own experiment:
  (a) a cheap pre-classifier gate ('is this a bare literal with no verb?') ahead of
      intent detection, leaving parameter_value out of the trained label space;
  (b) a calibrated abstention at the router. Section 11 M2 already records that there
      is NO out-of-scope rejection anywhere (fix-d28), and that the thresholds are the
      mean confidence of misclassified test samples -- a descriptive statistic, not an
      operating point. Both defects have the same shape as this one.
Filed as a follow-up linked discovered-from this issue.

SIDE EFFECT ON THE TEST SUITE UNCHANGED: test_trained_model_routes_utterance still
XFAILs/XPASSes seed-dependently. It was NOT fixed by this work and the marker must stay.
MEASURED TRADE-OFF CURVE, and it changes what this issue can ask for. Capping parameter_value's row count does fix routing, but it breaks the bare-value catch by roughly two to three points per point gained. hello_world, 5 seeds, paired on identical training data:
  rows=7 (current): 4 target probes 14/20, all 12 routing probes 41/60, catch 30/35
  rows=4          : 17/20, 47/60, catch 22/35
  rows=2          : 19/20, 52/60, catch 12/35
  rows=0          : 20/20, 57/60, catch  3/35

So the acceptance target on this issue (5/5 on the probes WITHOUT losing the bare-value catch) is unreachable by row count or by class weight. There is no setting where both halves hold.

Proposed mechanism: parameter_value's rows are contentless by construction ('3', '16.7,.002'), so the class has no semantic centre and its decision region is defined only by distance from everything else -- it expands to fill whatever space the real commands do not confidently claim. Row count and class weight are then the same knob on the same region, which is exactly why R7.2 and R7.3 both fail to separate the two behaviours. NOTE this mechanism is inferred from one small workflow (5 commands, ~60 routing verdicts) and is being tested for replication on retail (19 commands), together with its own prediction: that parameter_value's wins should concentrate where the runner-up real command has LOW confidence and on short/low-content utterances. Structural fix filed as fix-cm2: stop asking one classifier to do two jobs -- either a pre-classifier lexical gate for bare literals, or a calibrated abstention at the router. R7.2 remains shipped for wildcard only; it does not bind on parameter_value.

  signature changes again in an incompatible way). 31 passed after the change; the full

  Both files stub the agent seam with MagicMock/lambdas, which .cursor/rules/testing_rules.mdc

title: bd writes are silently lost ~50% of the time; bd show gives false positives
description:
Roughly half of all bd writes in this repo are silently lost, and `bd show` reports them as successful.

SYMPTOMS
  1. Every bd invocation logs: "auto-importing N bytes from .beads/issues.jsonl into empty database..."
     -- the database is EMPTY at the start of every single command, so each invocation
     rebuilds its whole view from the JSONL.
  2. Every write logs, in .beads/dolt-server.log:
       level=warning msg="error running query" ... error="nothing to commit"
  3. Writes therefore land in the freshly-imported in-process database but are not
     committed, and the next invocation re-imports the stale JSONL and reverts them.

OBSERVED IMPACT (during the fix-551 wave-1 parallel work)
  - `bd close fix-551.1` reported success and `bd show` confirmed status=closed.
    Minutes later `bd list` showed it open again, with its notes gone.
  - Batched `bd update --append-notes` across 3 issues persisted 1 of 3, twice.
  - Notes on fix-551.2/.6/.12/.14 were lost and had to be re-applied up to 5 times each.

WHY IT IS EASY TO MISS
  `bd show <id>` starts a new process, imports the JSONL, applies nothing, and prints the
  in-process state -- so immediately after a write it reflects the write regardless of
  whether it was committed. Verifying with `bd show` gives a FALSE POSITIVE. The only
  durable evidence is .beads/issues.jsonl, which is also what git tracks.

WORKAROUND CURRENTLY IN USE
  One write per invocation, then poll .beads/issues.jsonl (not `bd show`) until the change
  appears, retrying the write up to 5 times with ~10s between attempts. This is slow but
  it is the only shape observed to hold.

NOTE ON DOCS
  AGENTS.md states "bd automatically syncs with git ... No manual export/import needed!".
  That is not true in this checkout and should be corrected or qualified once the root
  cause is known.

SUSPECTED ROOT CAUSE
  The dolt sql-server (pid in .beads/dolt-server.pid) and the bd CLI disagree about which
  database/working set is authoritative. "nothing to commit" on every write plus an
  always-empty database on every read suggests writes are being applied to a session
  working set that is discarded rather than committed. Restarting the dolt server was NOT
  attempted, to avoid risking the store while work was in flight.

notes:
MECHANISM OBSERVED. A bd update emitted: 'auto-importing 305219 bytes from .beads/issues.jsonl into empty database... auto-imported 126 issues'. The sqlite database is being reset to empty and rebuilt from the JSONL mid-session. That explains both symptoms: a write lands in a db that is later discarded (write appears lost), and a read during the window returns pre-import state (bd show false positives).

title: R7.4: stop discarding a top-k wildcard — it silently suppresses escalation
description:
ADDRESSES F7 (S2). Only a LONE `wildcard` triggers the parent walk. When the classifier is unconfident and returns `wildcard` ALONGSIDE local candidates, intent_detection.py:124-128 takes the ambiguity branch instead, and _formulate_ambiguous_command_error_message (line 281) FILTERS `wildcard` OUT of the displayed list. The user is offered local commands and the model's "this belongs upstairs" signal is discarded with no trace.

OBSERVED on IDO: in context ReviewTicket, "approve everything from this app at once" returned ['wildcard', 'ReviewTicket/certify_approve', 'ReviewTicket/show_review_item'] and produced a two-option prompt, when the correct behaviour was to escalate to AccessReviewWorkspace/bulk_decide.

DO (spec R7.4): decide EXPLICITLY between escalating and prompting rather than defaulting to a local prompt. At minimum, LOG that the signal was dropped — the current behaviour leaves no trace at all, which is why this went unnoticed.

VERIFY: grep -n "len(predictions)==1\|command_name == \"wildcard\"" fastworkflow/_workflows/command_metadata_extraction/intent_detection.py ; grep -n "route_choice != 'wildcard'" fastworkflow/_workflows/command_metadata_extraction/intent_detection.py

DEPENDS ON R1b: this changes escalation behaviour, and escalation recall is currently unmeasured (F10). Do not ship a change to the escalation path before the metric that would catch a regression exists.
notes:
DELIVERED (wave 1, not yet integrated). New env var INTENT_DETECTION_TOPK_WILDCARD_POLICY with three values:

  log_only (DEFAULT) -- behaviour-identical to today, but logs the discarded escalation signal: utterance, context, full prediction list, suppressed labels, and the env var to set to change it.
  escalate           -- fully implemented. A top-k wildcard leaves command_name unset and falls through to the same non-routable branch a LONE wildcard already takes, so it drives the identical parent-chain walk rather than adding a second code path to validate.
  prompt             -- today's behaviour, silent. Kept so an operator who has read the diagnosis but is not ready to change behaviour can silence the log without losing the distinction between "silenced deliberately" and "never enabled".

Default is log_only because escalation recall is currently unmeasured (F10): nothing would catch a regression if the default flipped now.

FLIP CONDITION, recorded at the decision point in should_escalate_topk: (1) fix-551.6's held-out escalation metric must exist and be runnable, and (2) a PAIRED run of escalate against log_only on identical cases must show escalation recall not regressing. A single-run number does not clear R7's acceptance bar, since both axes trade against each other.

Env-var convention: read with NO code default so a shell export takes effect, giving ops a kill switch a benchmark harness can toggle per run. This is a deliberate departure from the sibling INTENT_DETECTION_* model vars, which are env-file-only. Resolver is lru_cached so the "variable does not exist" warning cannot repeat every turn; get_topk_wildcard_policy.cache_clear() re-reads. An unrecognised value warns and falls back to the default, because silently running the conservative policy when the operator asked for escalate would invalidate a benchmark run.

Also fixed in scope: _store_suggested_commands persists the raw prediction list, so a reserved label could come back as a "suggested command" during INTENT_AMBIGUITY_CLARIFICATION and hit .endswith() on a None fully-qualified name -- a latent AttributeError that parameter_value widens. Guarded on None rather than changing what gets stored, so log_only stays byte-identical.

title: R7.2: cap the ancestor wildcard class by budget, round-robin across ancestor commands
description:
ADDRESSES F8 (S3) — AS A COST AND HYGIENE ISSUE, NOT AN ACCURACY ISSUE (decision D3).

Because ancestor utterances arrive already expanded by the synthetic generator and nothing reweights or resamples, `wildcard` is the majority class in every context that has ancestors — 48-91% across the 29 IDO contexts with ancestors (Subscription 28 own rows vs 286 wildcard = 91%; ControlFinding 91%; Exception 88%; Account 76%), against 5-8% for the ancestor-less ones.

READ THE JUSTIFICATION CAREFULLY. Capping was tested directly and did NOT produce a significant accuracy change (routing p=0.25, escalation p=0.38). What it produced is a 44% REDUCTION IN TRAINING TIME, 3h35m -> 2h00m. Do not claim the observed +2.7 routing points; it will not reproduce. The correlation between wildcard share and top-1 is only -0.21.

DO (decision D4):
- Size the ancestor contribution RELATIVE TO THE AVERAGE REAL COMMAND CLASS rather than letting it arrive at 10x.
- Selection must be ROUND-ROBIN ACROSS ANCESTOR COMMANDS, so a context with 40 ancestor intents keeps all 40 represented instead of spending the budget on whichever commands generated the most text. Rejected: uniform random sample, head truncation — both drop whole intents.
- Take EARLIEST-FIRST within each command: _get_utterances returns [command_name] + seeds + synthetic (generate_synthetic.py:158), so earliest-first preserves the hand-written seeds and discards the synthetic tail first.

MEASURED EFFECT on IDO's Exception context: 2352 ancestor utterances -> 170, an 88% -> 27% share, with all 33 ancestor intents still represented.

REFERENCE: train_ido.py (spec §7) implements this by monkeypatching cache_ancestor_utterances — illustrative, and itself evidence that the package needs a real extension point here.

ACCEPTANCE: BOTH axes measured (R1) plus a paired exact McNemar test. A single-run routing number is not acceptance — the noise floor is 20.6% verdict churn.
notes:
NOT STARTED (wave 2). Blocked on re-derivation before any implementation begins.

The adversarial review removed the sizing rule this issue was written against. See AR4 and AR6 in docs/intent_training_improvements_spec.md section 10, and R7.2 in section 4, where the superseded text is struck through. Do NOT cite the Exception wildcard-share figures anywhere: fix-lfz (p2) tracks the fact that they do not reconcile with each other. R7.2 must be re-derived from the training-time target with an explicit coverage floor, not from "the average real command class".

Interaction with R7.1 (fix-551.11): the wildcard class no longer contains the seven parameter-extraction placeholders -- they now train under parameter_value. So the class composition, and therefore any wildcard-share figure computed before that split, has changed. Re-measure after fix-551.11 lands, not before, or the cap will be sized against a distribution that no longer exists.

  budget = max(cost_budget, one row per ancestor command)             coverage wins
Three steps, no fitted constants:
  1. D3: cost is the only effect capping was measured to have, so cost is the only
     thing the constant may be principled about.
  2. Per-context cost is linear in rows (12 tiny + 5 large epochs, fixed batch, two
     models). A row cap IS a training-time target.
  3. Ratio 1.0 is the unique value that states a nameable invariant -- 'the reserved
     data never outweighs the real data', i.e. at most 2x the real-command-only cost.
     It is NOT claimed accuracy-optimal. No accuracy claim attaches to any value.
The coverage floor is derived, not fitted: it is the minimum satisfying the escalation
requirement the class exists to serve. Coverage overrides cost when they conflict.
None of AR6's non-citable Exception figures are used or reproduced.

SELECTION (D4) is two-pass: a coverage pass taking one row from every ancestor command
(ignores the budget, so the floor holds by construction), then a fill pass cycling over
ancestor contexts and within each over its commands, one row per command per cycle.
Earliest-first within a command preserves the hand-written seeds.

VERIFIED ON A REAL HIERARCHY (tests/todo_list_workflow, patched trainer, full training):
  TodoItem  377 ancestor rows -> 240 (budget 240 = own rows; 23 ancestor commands covered)
  TodoList  138 ancestor rows -> 139 (budget 436; does not bind)
At RESERVED_CLASS_BUDGET_RATIO=0.01 the coverage floor takes over and TodoItem keeps
exactly one row per ancestor command.

THIS DOES NOT FIX fix-2m5, AND MUST NOT BE CLAIMED TO. parameter_value is a fixed
7-row literal list; the cost invariant only binds on it in a context whose real
commands contribute fewer than 7 rows. On hello_world (~150 own rows) the budget is
~150 and the class is untouched. The integration patch therefore applies the budget to
the ESCALATION class only, and class_balance.py documents parameter_value as
deliberately exempt. See fix-2m5 for the measurement that says shrinking it is
actively harmful.

The ratio is derived from a MEASURED cost model rather than picked: training time is linear in row count (3 settings, r-squared 0.98), so ratio 1.0 means the escalation class can at most double a context's training time. Rows are chosen round-robin across ancestor contexts and then across commands, so one verbose ancestor cannot crowd out the others.

title: R7.1: split the overloaded wildcard label — escalation signal vs bare-value catcher
description:
ADDRESSES F6 (S2). `wildcard` carries two unrelated meanings across two NLU stages:

1. During INTENT_DETECTION it is an ESCALATION SIGNAL. train() assigns it to every ancestor-context utterance not also valid locally (model_pipeline_training.py:872-877 and cache_ancestor_utterances, lines 769-801). At runtime a `wildcard` prediction sets command_name=None (intent_detection.py:141), which drives the parent-chain walk in wildcard.py:100-104 and falls back to you_misunderstood only when every ancestor declines. THIS DESIGN IS SOUND AND IT WORKS — 91.9% escalation recall on IDO. Do not redesign it.
2. During PARAMETER_EXTRACTION it is a BARE-VALUE CATCHER, which is what its seven literal placeholders plus the command name are for (wildcard.py:10-24: "3", "france", "id=3636", ...).

Role 2's literals are trained into role 1's classifier. The escalation classifier is being taught that "france" means "escalate to my parent".

DO: give the parameter-extraction placeholders their own label so the two roles stop sharing a class.

FIRST of the four wildcard changes (spec R7), and the one the other three sit on top of.

VERIFY: sed -n '9,24p' fastworkflow/_workflows/command_metadata_extraction/_commands/wildcard.py ; grep -n "net_ancestor_plus_wildcard_utterances" -B 4 fastworkflow/model_pipeline_training.py
notes:
--- RULING: drop the wildcard label in root contexts (orchestrator, int1) ---
Question raised by the R7.1/R7.4 implementation: after the split,
generate_utterances('wildcard') returns exactly ONE row (the humanised name).
In a context with no ancestors, ancestor_utterances is empty, so the wildcard
class collapses from 8 rows to 1.

DECISION: when (ancestor_utterances - context_utterances) is empty, do NOT emit
WILDCARD_LABEL for that context at all. Always emit PARAMETER_VALUE_LABEL
(7 rows) in every context.

Decisive argument: before this change, a root context's 8-row wildcard class was
7 placeholders + 1 name. The placeholders were the only substantive content --
they were acting as the bare-value sink. R7.1 moves exactly those 7 rows to
parameter_value. So the sink SURVIVES under its correct label, and what is left
behind is a 1-row class that can only ever match the literal string "wildcard".
Dropping it removes a degenerate class without removing any capability.

Why the 1-row class is actively harmful, not merely useless:
  :914  train_test_split(test_size=0.25, random_state=42) is NOT stratified, so
        the single row lands in train or test at random.
  If it lands in test, the label has zero training rows but is still a valid
  class -> guaranteed misclassification.
  :1183-1186  tiny_ambiguous_threshold = tiny_stats['failed']['mean'], i.e. the
        mean confidence of MISCLASSIFIED test samples. Verified by reading.
  So one pathological row moves a LIVE RUNTIME THRESHOLD. Confirmed.

Safety check (done): nothing requires 'wildcard' to be present in every trained
label space.
  command_routing.py:85-86  strips it from the routable command list.
  intent_detection            treats it as non-routable, resolves to None.
  command_executor.py:44      dispatches an ACTION named "wildcard" to the CME
                              workflow -- a command invocation, not a classifier
                              label lookup. Unaffected.
  command_metadata_api.py:62  already skips it.
Escalation is meaningless in a root context regardless: wildcard.py:100-104
terminates the parent walk immediately at the response-generation root, so a
wildcard prediction there can only reach you_misunderstood, which an unconfident
classifier already reaches.

Knock-on: num = len(set(y)) and therefore k_val at :887-888 shift for root
contexts. Held-out escalation scoring must skip root contexts (no ancestors ->
no escalation cases are constructible), which the heldout module already
reports via its uncovered-label notes.

title: R5: selective training of a command, context, or subtree, with upward closure
description:
Adds `fastworkflow train <workflow> [--command C] [--context X] [--changed-only]`.

THE NON-OBVIOUS PART (spec R5, decision D5): retraining a single command is NOT local. "Only this command changed" is never only one context.
- A context's classifier must be retrained if ANY of its own commands changed.
- A context must ALSO be retrained if any of its ANCESTORS' commands changed, because those utterances form its `wildcard` class (F6). This is the dependency that makes naive per-command retraining silently desync wildcard classes across the hierarchy.
- Contexts that inherit a changed command through the `base` axis must be retrained.
- --changed-only computes the dirty set from command-file fingerprints plus the R6 utterance cache, then CLOSES IT UPWARDS over the hierarchy.
- The output must STATE which contexts were retrained and which were carried forward, so the developer can see the closure that was computed rather than trusting it.

DEPENDS ON: R6 (fingerprints for --changed-only) and R4 (D8 — merging new per-command work into a live artifact set with no rollback is the same hazard class as F5).

CONTEXT MODEL: the inheritance semantics here are load-bearing and already specified elsewhere — consult the fastworkflow-architecture-contract skill on context_inheritance_model.json / the context hierarchy before deriving the closure rule from scratch.
notes:
CORRECTION from the adversarial review (fix-551.1, finding AR2): the closure rule stated in this issue and in decision D5 is INCOMPLETE. It expands over the 'parent' hierarchy from a changed command's home context only. The 'base' axis creates a composition it misses.

cache_ancestor_utterances reaches ancestor commands via context_model.commands(), which is base-RESOLVED. So a command enters a context's wildcard class through ANY ancestor that inherits it — the command's home context need not be on that context's parent chain at all.

Worked example (neither axis alone catches AdminSession):
  Account       owns Account/close
  AdminAccount  base:   [Account]       -> inherits Account/close
  AdminSession  parent: [AdminAccount]  -> wildcard class carries Account/close

CORRECTED RULE:
  Carriers(C) = { X : C in commands(X) }              # commands() is base-resolved
  Dirty(C)    = Carriers(C) union { X : ancestors(X) intersect Carriers(C) != {} }

Compute carriers by membership-testing the RESOLVED commands() output so simple-name shadowing is honoured.

STATUS: implemented and tested in fastworkflow/train/selective_training.py::close_dirty_contexts, which takes a base-resolved context->commands map and checks ancestors against that same map, so it satisfies the corrected rule. Covered by tests/test_selective_training.py::test_base_and_parent_axes_compose. Remaining work on this issue is the CLI surface (--command/--context/--changed-only) and wiring into train().

WAVE 2 (opt-in delivery). Reviewed selective_training.py against the real train() path and wired it behind --changed-only. Full retrain remains the default.

DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED in the pre-existing module (it had no call site, so none of this had ever run):
1. It fingerprinted COMMANDS ONLY. Editing context_inheritance_model.json or the context hierarchy moves a label space with every command file byte-identical, and nothing detected it. Added TrainingSignature: per-context label_space / ancestors / wildcard_sources / expects_wildcard_label, plus global inputs (seed, tiny+large model ids, LLM_SYNDATA_GEN, persona source, generator prompt digest, train() source digest, PARAMETER_VALUE_PLACEHOLDERS hash, ARTIFACT_FORMAT_VERSION).
2. Unresolvable fingerprints compared EQUAL to each other. Two runs that both failed to read a command produced two identical (None, None) fingerprints, i.e. "unchanged forever". Added resolved/unresolved_reason; an unresolved fingerprint differs from everything including itself.
3. build_context_maps swallowed lookup failures and substituted a SMALLER command set, so a context whose ancestors would not resolve appeared to have none and no ancestor change could dirty it. It now returns the failures and the caller retrains those contexts.
4. It never hydrated commands before reading map_command_2_utterance_metadata. That map is lazily populated, so un-hydrated commands fingerprinted empty and agreed across runs.
5. No artifact-completeness check. An interrupted run leaves a half-written context dir; carrying it forward publishes a workflow that looks trained and raises FileNotFoundError on the first turn.
6. No carry-forward step at all. publish_version REMOVES the compatibility entry of any context its version lacks, so a selective run would have silently un-trained every context it skipped. carry_forward_contexts() raises rather than degrading, and runs before publish.
7. Interaction with R6 was undefined. Under regenerate/off/aggregate cache modes a retrained context is built on fresh utterances while a carried context keeps the old ones, including in its wildcard class. --changed-only now degrades to a full retrain unless the cache mode is reuse.
8. train() rewrites heldout_evaluation.json from only the contexts it trained, so a selective run silently narrowed a 4-context report to 1 context. Added capture/merge_heldout_evaluation; carried entries are tagged carried_forward and the totals are re-aggregated exactly (every total is a sum or a ratio of sums).

MEASURED (messaging_app_4, 4 contexts, R6 cache warm, paired back-to-back runs after editing exactly one leaf command): full 83.2s vs selective 62.9s wall, a 20.3s / 24% saving; inside train() 55.8s vs 39.0s. Floor for a no-op selective run: 25.6s, nearly all of it DSPy parameter-example generation, which --changed-only does not skip. hello_world: full 24.0s vs selective 24.5s -- selective is SLOWER by the planner's cost.
STRUCTURAL FINDING: hello_world and retail_workflow both train exactly ONE context ('*'), so selective retraining can save nothing on either by construction. Every bundled example except messaging_app_4 is single-context. Wall-clock on this box varied 45.8s-279.6s for the same 4-context full train, so the per-context marginal fit cost (~6s) is small next to the noise.

DO NOT RECOMMEND when: the workflow has one trainable context (no saving, small loss); the run is dominated by LLM calls rather than fitting; correctness of the published models matters more than minutes (releases, benchmark runs, published numbers); after changing anything global (env, models, seed) since it degrades to a full retrain anyway; combined with --regenerate-utterances (mutually exclusive). Worth it only on a many-context workflow during tight edit/train iteration.

TESTS: tests/test_selective_training_integration.py -- 16 planner tests against a real messaging_app_4 copy with a real published artifact version (both inheritance axes, context-model-only edits, new commands, incomplete artifacts, changed seed, corrupt baseline, no baseline, default full retrain, carry-forward, report merge), plus one API-key-gated end-to-end test that trains twice and asserts the retrained context's bytes changed, the carried contexts' bytes did NOT, every context is present in the published version, and the retrained model routes the newly added utterance.

REMAINS OPEN: the three call-site files (model_pipeline_training.py, train/__main__.py, cli.py) are owned by the integrating agent and were delivered as patches, not applied. The end-to-end test skips itself until train_workflow accepts changed_only.
R5 SHIPPED as opt-in --changed-only, default OFF. Wired into train_workflow + model_pipeline_training.train(contexts_to_train=...) + cli.py. 17 integration tests including a real end-to-end that no longer skips (it self-skipped until train_workflow accepted changed_only): trains messaging_app_4 fully, edits one PremiumUser command, retrains with --changed-only, and asserts PremiumUser's bytes changed while *, ChatRoom and User are byte-identical SHA-for-SHA, all four contexts publish complete, and the real CommandRouter routes the new utterance correctly.

EIGHT DEFECTS fixed in the pre-existing module. The two worth remembering:
* NO CARRY-FORWARD (D6). publish_version removes the compatibility entry of any context its version lacks, so a selective run would have published a version holding only the retrained context and UN-TRAINED THE REST OF THE WORKFLOW WHILE PRINTING SUCCESS. This interaction is nowhere in the R5 spec; anyone implementing from the spec alone ships it.
* ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE READ AS EVIDENCE (D2/D3). An unresolvable command fingerprint returned (None, None), which compares EQUAL to the next run's (None, None) -- so a command whose source could not be read looked unchanged forever. And build_context_maps swallowed ancestor-lookup failures and substituted a smaller command set, weakening exactly the axis hardest to reason about. General rule: a comparison that can fail must not fail EQUAL.

ALSO: the closure is only half the problem. A context_inheritance_model.json edit changes a label space with every command file byte-identical, so ~half the implementation is a recorded TrainingSignature rather than the command closure the spec describes.

VALUE IS THIN, and this is the honest headline. 24% (83.2s -> 62.9s) on messaging_app_4, the ONLY bundled example with more than one trainable context. ZERO on hello_world and retail_workflow -- both train exactly one context ('*'), all 19 retail commands being global -- and on hello_world it is measurably SLOWER (24.5s vs 24.0s) because you pay the planner for nothing. The ~25s floor is mostly DSPy parameter-example generation, which the flag does not skip; marginal per-context fit is ~6s, so it starts paying for itself north of ten contexts and no workflow here is close.

NOT DOING: --command/--context CLI flags, which this issue asks for. They express a developer's assertion about what changed, and an assertion wrong in the unsafe direction is the exact failure the module exists to prevent. Available programmatically as ADDITIVE hints (never substituted for the fingerprint-derived dirty set). Say so if you want them exposed.

Recommend keeping it opt-in; do not promote to default on this evidence. A false retrain costs minutes, a false skip costs a stale model nothing in the package would surface.
close_reason: Shipped opt-in --changed-only; 8 defects fixed; value measured thin

title: R4: versioned artifacts with a current pointer
description:
ADDRESSES F5 (S1). Training writes directly into ___command_info/<Context>/. There is no version, no "current" pointer, and no rollback. To compare two runs the IDO team had to `mv` 8.6 GB by hand, and a separate scaffold-regeneration step DESTROYED a complete trained set because nothing marks these directories as expensive.

DO (spec R4, decision D8):
- Write to ___command_info/<version>/ with a `current` symlink or pointer file.
- Never destroy a previous version implicitly; prune only on explicit request.
- The output must make it obvious these directories are expensive to regenerate.

WHY THIS ORDERS BEFORE SELECTIVE TRAINING (D8): merging new per-command work into a live artifact set with no rollback is the same class of hazard as F5 itself. Versioning also makes paired evaluation possible at all — scoring two versions on identical cases is the acceptance mechanism for R7 and the substrate for the convergence loop.

INTERACTS WITH the artifact-size issue (F11): a shared encoder changes what a "version" costs from 8.6 GB to something a developer can keep ten of. Consider the two together; the size work is tracked separately so it cannot block this.

CONSTRAINT: the runtime artifact layout is consumed elsewhere (see the fastworkflow-diagnostics-and-tooling and fastworkflow-nlu-pipeline-reference skills for what reads ___command_info). Changing the layout without updating every reader will produce FileNotFoundError on threshold.json — a known failure signature in this repo.
notes: CORRECTION from the adversarial review (fix-551.1, finding AR3): decision D8's ORDERING survives but its RATIONALE does not. Versioning gives an immutable prior version and paired comparison; neither PREVENTS an inconsistent version being produced and promoted. A carried-forward context whose ancestor was regenerated has a wildcard class that no longer matches the ancestor's live label space, and per F1/F10 nothing currently surfaces that. Rollback only lets you undo AFTER you notice. Versioning therefore buys RECOVERY, not SAFETY. What would actually make merging safe, and should be built here: (1) a per-version manifest recording ancestor-contribution fingerprints per context; (2) a PROMOTION-TIME CONSISTENCY CHECK that refuses to publish a version whose carried-forward contexts disagree with their ancestors' current contributions; (3) an atomic pointer flip. The consistency check is load-bearing because it is INDEPENDENT of the dirty-set computation, so it catches a closure bug of exactly the kind AR2 found in D5.
close_reason: R4 delivered and integrated. Artifacts are written under ___command_info/versions/<id>/ with a current pointer and per-context compatibility entries, so existing readers resolve unchanged. train_workflow migrates any pre-versioning artifacts into a version BEFORE writing, so a run cannot merge new work into an unrollbackable set; publishes ONLY on success, so a failed train leaves the previous version published and complete with its partial version beside it rather than on top of it; and stamps the manifest with the seed. Provenance is written both top-level (a stable path for the R3b report) and into the version, so a version can still say which personas and seed produced its utterances after a later run overwrites the top-level copy. _prune_stale_artifacts now calls unroute_context instead of shutil.rmtree for compatibility entries -- rmtree refuses to follow a symlink, so without this the prune would have silently stopped cleaning orphans. CLI: fastworkflow versions list|show|publish|prune, and train --version-notes.

title: R3b: per-command training-data report and a minimum-row floor
description:
ADDRESSES F4 (S2). train() prints "Generating utterances for context X, command Y ..." with no count, and never validates that a command ended up with a usable number of rows. A developer cannot answer "which of my commands are starved?" — which, per F13, is the highest-leverage question they can ask, since seed count is the dominant input to routing accuracy (3.2 seeds/cmd -> 46.2% top-1, 8.0 -> 70.4%, 9.3 -> 73.8%).

DO (spec R3):
- Emit a per-command table at the end of training with: seed count, generated count, final row count, whether generation FELL BACK (the R3a path), and — once R1 lands — the per-command held-out score.
- Fail the run, or warn loudly, when any command's row count falls below a floor.
- The fallback column is the visible surface for the F3 bug: a silent [] today becomes a visible "fell back" row here.

DEPENDS ON the R3a fix, which introduces the fallback state this report surfaces.
notes: DELIVERED (wave 2, not yet integrated). New module fastworkflow/train/training_report.py reads training_provenance.json (+ command_directory.json, routing_definition.json, heldout_evaluation.json) and produces a per-command table: rows / seeds / generated / held-out top-1 / contexts, grouped worst-first as FELL BACK, BELOW ROW FLOOR, NO PROVENANCE, THIN SEEDS, NEVER ROUTED, with healthy commands summarised rather than enumerated. Reserved NLU labels (wildcard, parameter_value) are reported distinctly and exempt from every floor except fallback. Two floors, both DEFAULTS: TRAINING_REPORT_MIN_ROWS=4 (structural -- unstratified 25%% split means n rows carry ~0.25**n chance of contributing nothing to training; 4 puts that under 1%%) and TRAINING_REPORT_MIN_SEEDS=8 (advisory, F13, ONE workflow's curve). WARNS, never fails: artifacts already exist by report time and the dominant fallback cause is a transient provider rate limit; a CI gate opts in via has_blocking_problems / the JSON report. Missing, partial or corrupt provenance degrades to a described problem, never a traceback. 22 integration tests in tests/test_training_report.py including an API-key-gated end-to-end run. Integration into train/__main__.py and cli.py handed to the epic owner; no change needed in model_pipeline_training.py.
close_reason:
R3b DELIVERED AND NOW INTEGRATED. fastworkflow/train/training_report.py plus 22 integration tests. Wired in this session: train/__main__.py writes the report for every workflow trained (including children, print_report=False) and prints it once for the top-level workflow after the versions table; cli.py gains a 'report' subcommand with --json, --write and --fail-on-problems. Verified by running 'fastworkflow report' against a real trained hello_world -- table renders with THIN SEEDS and SUMMARY sections populated from real provenance.

Two thresholds with different standing, both labelled as such in the output: the row floor of 4 is DERIVED (the unstratified 25% split gives ~0.25^n odds a command contributes nothing to training; 4 is the smallest n under 1%) and is not an accuracy claim; the seed floor of 8 is ONE workflow's observed curve and is advisory only. The report warns and never fails a run, because by report time the artifacts exist and have been published, and the commonest cause of a fallback is a transient rate limit; --fail-on-problems is the opt-in CI gate.

Known limitation carried forward as fix-5vb: ROWS is per-last-generation, not summed across contexts, because provenance is keyed by command name alone.

title: Intent training: trustworthy measurement, determinism, versioning, and wildcard construction
description:
Implement docs/intent_training_improvements_spec.md (R1-R9).

SYMPTOM: `fastworkflow train` reports ~0.94 mean per-context F1 while the same models route only 46.2% of held-out phrasings to the right command, because model_pipeline_training.py:914 splits the SAME synthetic set the model trains on (train_test_split(dataset, test_size=0.25, random_state=42)) and utterances for one command come from a handful of personas — so the 25% holdout is near-duplicated in the 75% train. Nothing in the package is seeded, so two identical runs disagree on 20.6% of held-out routing cases (92/446). That churn is larger than any effect measured after initial seed expansion, which means no change in this area can currently be evaluated at all.

EVIDENCE BASE: the IDO workflow (160 application commands, 33 contexts) trained 4x against a purpose-built held-out benchmark of 446 routing cases + 37 escalation cases. Runs: baseline 3.2 seeds/cmd -> 46.2% top-1; v2 8.0 -> 70.4%; v3 9.3 -> 73.8% (91.9% escalation, 3h35m); v4 (wildcard capped 3x) -> 76.5% (83.8% escalation, 2h00m). Paired exact McNemar v3->v4: routing 52 fixed / 40 broken, p=0.25; escalation 1 fixed / 4 broken, p=0.38.

FINDINGS ADDRESSED: F1 reported metric measures memorisation (S1) - F2 nothing seeded, runs not reproducible (S1) - F3 a rate-limited command silently becomes unroutable (S1) - F4 no per-command visibility (S2) - F5 artifacts overwritten in place, no versioning (S1) - F6 `wildcard` overloaded across two NLU stages (S2) - F7 a top-k `wildcard` silently suppresses escalation (S2) - F8 `wildcard` is the majority class (48-91%) in every context with ancestors (S3) - F9 no class weighting (S3) - F10 escalation recall unmeasured (S2) - F11 ~276MB/context, 8.6GB per workflow (S3) - F12 persona sampling domain-agnostic (S3) - F13 seed count is the dominant input and nobody is told (S2) - F14 duplicate capabilities undiagnosed (S3).

SCOPE BOUNDARY: three things are explicitly NOT established and must not be used as justification (spec §8): contentless seeds colliding with wildcard literals (untested, not refuted); wildcard imbalance depressing routing accuracy (tested, NOT supported, p=0.25); the 66.1% vs 78.7% deep-vs-shallow gap has no established cause (correlation with wildcard share only -0.21, capping did not close it). The wildcard cap is justified on TRAINING COST (44% reduction, 3h35m -> 2h00m), not accuracy.
design:
Spec: docs/intent_training_improvements_spec.md (Proposal, awaiting adversarial review — house lifecycle stage 1 of 7). Pinned against v2.23.0, commit 23dbe35. All file:line references verified at that commit; re-verification one-liners in spec §9.

SEQUENCING (spec §6) — R2 and R4 are prerequisites for almost everything and are individually small; R1 is the gate on being able to evaluate anything at all:
1. R2 (determinism) + R3 (generation robustness) — small, independently valuable
2. R1 (held-out evaluation) — unblocks all measurement
3. R4 (versioning) — unblocks safe iteration
4. R6 (utterance persistence) -> R5 (selective training)
5. R7 (wildcard) — measurable only once R1 is in
6. R8 (skill), R9 (personas, duplicates)

DECISION LOG (spec §5), binding on all children:
D1 Hold out WHOLE PERSONAS, not random rows. A random split of one persona's output is near-duplicate data — that is exactly F1. Rejected: a larger test_size (dilutes the leak, does not fix it).
D2 Escalation recall is a SEPARATE reported metric, never folded into accuracy. The two axes trade against each other and one blended score hides the trade (F10).
D3 The wildcard cap is justified on TRAINING COST, not accuracy. Directly tested: p=0.25 routing, p=0.38 escalation. Rejected: claiming the +2.7 points — it will not reproduce.
D4 Round-robin selection across ancestor commands. Preserves every ancestor intent; a flat sample drops whole intents. Rejected: uniform random sample, head truncation.
D5 Selective training closes UPWARD over ancestors. Ancestor utterances constitute the descendant's wildcard class (F6), so "only this command changed" is never only one context. Rejected: per-command retraining in isolation (would silently desync wildcard classes).
D6 Utterance cache keyed by a fingerprint including persona IDs and seed value. Without R2 the cache cannot be validated, so R2 is a HARD prerequisite for R6. Rejected: timestamp/mtime keying.
D7 Convergence loop as a skill, not a CLI flag. Judgement-bearing protocol; composes with existing methodology skills. Rejected: CLI subcommand (would hard-code statistical policy).
D8 Artifact versioning BEFORE selective training. Merging new per-command work into a live artifact set with no rollback is the same class of hazard as F5. Rejected: shipping R5 first.

ACCEPTANCE BAR FOR THE EPIC: no requirement whose effect is an accuracy claim may be accepted on a single-run number. Acceptance is both axes measured (R1) plus a paired exact McNemar test (R8 protocol), because the noise floor of one training run is ~20.6% verdict churn. Statistics conventions defer to the fastworkflow-proof-and-analysis-toolkit skill; the loop protocol lives in the fastworkflow-intent-training-convergence skill.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATIONS (spec §7) — these exist and run against the 160-command IDO workflow, as monkeypatches / app-side harnesses because the package offers no extension point. Illustrative, not submissions: train_ido.py (R7.2 wildcard cap with round-robin ancestor selection, by patching cache_ancestor_utterances), tests/eval_intent_benchmark.py (R1 two-axis benchmark with seed-disjointness enforcement), tests/compare_runs.py (R8 paired scoring with exact McNemar). That all three had to be written outside the package, one by reaching into a module global, is itself an argument for R1 and R4.
