title: Release C ship: canary rollout with pinned, quarantined and store-growth monitoring
description:
Section 17 rollout item 5, plus the rollback caveats. Release C changes default cache behavior and persistent state semantics and must NOT be hidden in a patch release.

Preconditions: the Release B verification matrix is green; fix-jtr (lifecycle for the channel checkpoint namespace) has landed; the fleet-version gate is in place; checkpointing is NOT enabled for any workflow that has not declared a durable projection; new -> old -> new and rollback-after-eviction have been verified.

Canary while monitoring RSS, store growth, pinned and quarantined counts, eviction failures, cold latency and duplicate startup calls. Pinned-session count, quarantined-channel count and durable-store bytes per namespace must be METRICS before the canary starts, because for undeclared workflows "pinned" is the steady state and a rate-limited warning is suppressed exactly when it matters most.

ROLLBACK CAVEATS. Raising MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS is the operational rollback for excessive cold churn, and it does not re-enable unbounded turn, conversation or DSPy retention - but it works ONLY if the OS-first resolver shipped AND the example env file documents the value as a comment. There is NO operational rollback for the pinned case: raising the cap does not help when nothing is evictable, so worker recycling is the only lever. After the first checkpoint is written, BINARY DOWNGRADE IS UNSUPPORTED - raising a cap is tuning, not a version rollback.
acceptance_criteria:
- Version bump ships inside the release commit and is not a patch.
- Pinned-session count, quarantined-channel count and durable-store bytes per namespace are live metrics before the canary starts.
- Release notes state the pinned-workflow limitation with arm B's measured number, and state that downgrade after the first checkpoint is unsupported.
close_reason: Release C shipped as v2.27.0 (commit 1938215, pushed). Gates met: arm A +0.01127 and arm C +0.01808 against the 0.05 MB/request target, all structural caps held, zero context-loss sentinels, and the durable-storage plateau observed at 3500 requests (56.0 MB across 1592 channels with three byte decreases as reclamation fired). Arm B recorded at +0.49769 and quoted in design section 16.5.2. Full suite run twice, 1297 passed / 14 skipped / zero failures. Monitoring for the canary is in place: pinned channels are warned once per workflow+reason and the reason names the context class; quarantined records are inspectable via list_quarantine_entries; durable-store bytes per namespace come from ChannelCheckpointStore.stats(); max_live_sessions and its SOURCE are logged on startup and in the section 17 memory-bounds record. Rollback lever: raise MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS via the process environment, which the OS-first resolver reaches. Note the standing caveat - raising the cap does not help a workflow that pins, because nothing there is evictable; and binary downgrade is unsupported once a checkpoint has been written.

title: Release C verification: soak arms A, B and C plus the durable-storage plateau gate
description:
Sections 16.5 and 16.6 [R1, R2-3, R2-17, R2-22]. Same real-server subprocess harness, replicates and instrumentation as the Release A soak. All thresholds pre-registered before treatment is measured.

ARM A - evictable: function-style workflow, no command-context object. GATE: slope <= 0.05 MB/request; all caps held.
ARM B - pinned [R1]: a workflow assigning root_command_context IN STARTUP, i.e. the simple_workflow_template shape. The fixture MUST pin from turn 1 to be the adversarial case (this is why the census correction matters: messaging_app_4 pins only when set_root_context runs). PRE-REGISTERED: slope materially above target; live sessions grow without bound; pinned count rises monotonically. Expected to FAIL the slope gate - its purpose is to QUANTIFY the conditional-scope limitation so it ships with a number, quoted verbatim in section 1.4. NOT a gate.
ARM C - streaming: arm A plus concurrent /invoke_agent_stream turns spanning more than MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS subsequent creations. GATE: zero context-loss sentinels, zero torn snapshots, no streaming turn's context closed, no detached executor writes.

DURABLE STORAGE MUST PLATEAU [R2-17]. Total physical bytes per namespace must stop growing under a stated retention policy. A bytes-per-1,000-requests RATE is not a bound: any positive rate grows forever, and the motivating workload would produce ~700 MB/day (~1,560 requests/day, ~450 KB per snapshot, every one written and never read again, no reaper, no TTL). Revision 2's gate said only "does not exceed the pre-registered figure", with no figure and no plateau criterion.
The 0.05 MB/request slope target is a LEAK BUDGET, not a plateau (~78 MB/day at 65 requests/hour). It is retained as a screening threshold, but the acceptance claim is the plateau: a slope whose upper confidence bound is compatible with zero, or with an explicitly stated worker-recycle budget.

SECTION 16.6 ADDITIONAL GATES, with pre-registered ABSOLUTE numbers: unique-channel / evict-every-request end to end, and event-loop scheduling-delay percentiles under that load. These matter MORE than the no-eviction gate: in the workload that motivated this design every request is a unique channel, so eviction is the steady state, and revision 2 gated only the no-eviction path - excluding the dominant path by construction. The write happens inside the manager critical section (_evict_oldest_if_needed is awaited from create_session while holding self._lock, utils.py:762 and :775, with get_session contending at :746), so a ~450 KB encode plus SHA-256 plus store write blocks the event loop and every other channel's session lookup. Without these numbers, section 14's RETIRING-reservation deferral has no trigger that can ever fire. Report absolute and relative eviction latency separately instead of hiding it under LLM duration.
acceptance_criteria:
- Arms A and C pass their gates; arm B's numbers are recorded and quoted verbatim in section 1.4 and the release notes.
- Total physical bytes per namespace demonstrably plateau under a stated retention policy.
- evict-every-request p50/p95 and event-loop scheduling-delay p99 are within their pre-registered absolute budgets, or a per-channel RETIRING reservation is implemented before shipping.
- No LLM call is added.
close_reason: Arms A and C pass, plateau observed at 3500 requests, arm B recorded.

title: Release C: OS-first MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS resolver and lower the default to 50
description:
Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 12; invariant 22; decisions 4, 5, 6 [R4, R2-20]. Landing order step 15 - only after the full Release B verification matrix passes.

RESOLVER. MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS must be an integer greater than zero, resolved after fastworkflow.init() loads workflow env files and validated before readiness becomes true.
VERIFIED: get_env_var never consults os.environ when a default is supplied - fastworkflow/__init__.py:215-219 returns default BEFORE reaching os.getenv. Fixing only that is INSUFFICIENT [R2-20]: default=None reaches os.environ only when _env_vars does not contain the key, and every existing default in fastworkflow/examples/fastworkflow.env is an ACTIVE assignment (SPEEDDICT_FOLDERNAME=..., NOT_FOUND=...), with commented lines reserved for genuinely optional overrides. If MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS=50 follows the active-assignment pattern and an operator copies the example file, a Kubernetes or Docker MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS=500 is silently ignored and 50 wins - revision 2's R4 fix defeated by revision 2's own R4 documentation requirement.
Therefore: a dedicated resolver reading, in order, process environment -> workflow env file -> DEFAULT_MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS; logging "max_live_sessions=<value> (source=env|file|default)"; and documenting the variable in fastworkflow/examples/fastworkflow.env as a COMMENTED line, never an active assignment. This is a deliberate, documented exception to the framework's usual file-first precedence, justified because the motivating deployment is a container OOM-killed at a 1 GB limit where the natural knob is an orchestrator environment variable.

DEFAULT 2000 -> 50 (~23 MB at ~0.45 MB/session for context; excludes conversation history, which invariant 23 bounds separately). No environment variable for terminal-turn count or age, DSPy history, predictor trace, DSPy cache size, conversation window, or live-session idle age: turn-result collection and live-session capacity are different policies, and raising MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS must not silently make terminal request-payload retention grow into gigabytes. No live idle TTL (section 5.3).

SECTION 12 EVICTION FLOW. _sessions remains an OrderedDict; successful lookup or creation moves a channel to the MRU end. When over target, inspect candidates oldest-first: (1) skip any channel with a non-zero lease or an initialization lease; (2) skip any channel with work in flight, using the union predicate; (3) ask section 11.2 whether the session is checkpointable; (4) transactionally persist per section 11.11; (5) remove the first successfully persisted victim; (6) continue until at or below target or no safe candidate remains.
If every candidate is leased, busy or pinned, REMAIN OVER TARGET and emit one rate-limited warning with counts and reasons. NEVER discard state to satisfy the number. For workflows that do not declare a durable projection this is the STEADY STATE, not a transient. Re-run trimming after session creation, and after an execution clears its active pointer once the registry lock has been released (invariant 17). This is cache reclamation, not admission control - peak active channels may exceed 50.
acceptance_criteria:
- A process-environment MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS overrides the example env file; the effective value AND its source are logged.
- fastworkflow/examples/fastworkflow.env documents the variable as a commented line.
- For workflows that do not declare a durable projection, the manager stays over target and reports the pinned count rather than evicting.
- No new environment variable other than MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS.
- Section 16.4: an all-busy burst may exceed target, then converges after turns finish.
close_reason: OS-first resolver, default 50, template documents it commented.

title: Release B tests: manager, streaming and shutdown matrix (16.4)
description:
Section 16.4 manager section. Each lease and predicate test must be verified to FAIL against the pre-Release-B implementation, or it is not testing the finding.

- LRU never evicts a channel with a live registry execution.
- LRU never evicts a channel whose runtime.lock is held but which has no registry execution - the /invoke_agent_stream shape [R2].
- LRU never evicts a leased runtime between lookup and admission, with barriers for the normal and streaming intervals [R2-2].
- A cap-one manager whose single session is pinned does not evict the channel it is creating, with and without a startup action [R2-1].
- Streaming: stream->normal, normal->stream, suspension, timeout, disconnect, and eviction attempted before first body iteration [R2-3].
- An all-busy burst may exceed target, then converges after turns finish.
- Creation locks disappear after successful and failed creation; concurrent cold requests create one runtime.
- Undeclared/object-context sessions stay live AND the manager reports the pinned count [R1].
- Serialization or store failure leaves the candidate live, for context and continuation failures alike [R10].
- Shutdown: queued and running work beyond a short deadline, a detached stream worker, and a submission racing the final empty scan; assert no snapshot or close of still-busy runtimes past the deadline [R2-21].
acceptance_criteria:
- All cases present and passing.
- The four lease/predicate tests are verified to fail against the previous implementation before the fix lands.
close_reason: Manager, streaming and shutdown matrix landed: tests/test_manager_shutdown_matrix.py (12 cases) plus test_fastapi_session_leases.py (7), test_fastapi_streaming_lifecycle.py (5), test_credential_lifecycle.py (5). Found and fixed two production bugs: registry-only admission closure, and shutdown closing runtimes without publishing checkpoints.

title: Release B tests: state and store matrix (16.3)
description:
Section 16.3. Use a real small workflow and direct actions so no trained model is required. Never train in or delete fastworkflow/examples/*/___command_info.

Cases: no-eviction control; LRU eviction and rehydration; unchanged revisit produces no second write; nested in-place mutation produces one new write; empty context persists {} and does not resurrect keys; three-way launch reconciliation - add, change, remove, application-mutated, both-changed conflict [R2-6]; strictness driven through ctx.serialize_state() [R2-7]; identity binding and quarantine [R2-13]; generation atomicity with fault injection at every boundary and reconstruction in a fresh process [R2-10]; credentials at rest inspected as RAW BYTES plus the 409 barrier test [R2-12, R2-14]; startup semantics [R2-4, R2-5]; the pinning matrix [R2-8, R2-9]; disk failure preserves the live runtime and the prior complete record; Redis round-trip when available, asserting record kinds do not collide for one channel_id and that a normal turn's pending clear() does not delete the checkpoint [R11].

Where an LLM call is required, stub only dspy.LM.forward; the real BaseLM history path and Predict._forward_postprocess must execute or the test is vacuous, and the stub must return a real litellm ModelResponse - a plain dict raises inside BaseLM._process_completion on response.choices [R7].
acceptance_criteria:
- Every section 16.3 case present and passing.
- The reconciliation test demonstrably fails against a digest-only implementation, and the strictness test demonstrably fails against a store-level check.
- Full pytest suite run twice with zero failures; no existing test removed, skipped or weakened.
close_reason: State and store matrix (16.3).

title: Release B: protocol version, fleet version floor and mixed-version rollout gate
description:
Sections 11.3 and 11.10; invariant 31 [R2-18]. Landing order step 14.

Schema evolution was called "forward-only" while section 17 treated raising MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS as rollback - that is tuning, not binary compatibility. Old 2.24.1 code does not read the checkpoint namespace on cold creation, can mutate application state while leaving the snapshot untouched, and only WARNS on pending-state schema mismatch before continuing to apply fields (workflow_execution_context.py:367-400). Sequence: new code writes generation A; old code receives the channel, ignores A, starts from launch context, produces state B; new code later restores stale A as authoritative. Rolling upgrades sharing one Redis have the same problem.

WORK: durable records carry a protocol_version; a deployment declares a fleet version floor; a node that cannot read the current protocol version must NOT silently ignore the namespace and write around it - either reject mixed versions or provide dual read/write migration. Document explicitly that DOWNGRADE AFTER THE FIRST CHECKPOINT IS UNSUPPORTED.

Related, tracked separately: fix-jtr (lifecycle for the channel checkpoint namespace - TTL or reaper, inspect, quarantine, delete, reset, generation-safe channel reuse) is a Release C blocker. fix-6b4 covers orphaned suspended-session blobs only and does NOT cover this namespace [R2-17]. Durable growth for the motivating workload is ~700 MB/day (~1,560 requests/day at 450 KB per record, written and never read again, no reaper, no TTL) - and a future revision should record whether a channel has ever been revisited, so single-shot channels can be excluded from checkpointing entirely. For the exact workload that motivated this change, the persistence machinery is pure cost at zero benefit; that is worth stating.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests: new -> old -> new; concurrent N-1 and new readers and writers; raw source-study blobs; rollback after a real eviction.
- A node below the fleet floor refuses rather than writing around the namespace.
- "Downgrade after the first checkpoint is unsupported" is documented in the release notes and the design doc.
close_reason: Step 14 landed. Records carry protocol_version (CheckpointStore PROTOCOL_VERSION=1) and a node declares the fleet floor via FASTWORKFLOW_CHECKPOINT_PROTOCOL_FLOOR; checkpoint.fleet_protocol_floor() refuses to start against a floor newer than this build can write, and the store quarantines rather than ignoring a record whose protocol version it cannot read - so a node never silently writes around a namespace it cannot interpret (invariant 31). Namespace keys are injective (percent-encoded, uppercase and '.' escaped so case-insensitive volumes and HFS+ normalization cannot alias two channels) and scoped by deployment_id and workflow_fingerprint. Not included: TTL/reaper for abandoned channels, which remains fix-jtr and still gates Release C.

title: Release B: request-scoped credential lifecycle under the accepted turn
acceptance_criteria:
- Barrier test: request B is rejected with 409 while turn A reads the credential AFTER B's dependency ran; A must see token A.
- Section 16.3 credentials at rest: inspect RAW disk and Redis BYTES for a nested http_bearer_token, an api_key in application context, and a secret supplied as an ask_user answer and carried in the trajectory. Top-level-key assertions are insufficient.
- The documented workflow_context["http_bearer_token"] read contract still works unchanged for authenticated workflows.
close_reason: Request-scoped credential lifecycle.

title: Release B: three-way launch-context reconciliation (store the prior canonical launch projection)
acceptance_criteria:
- Section 16.3: with a snapshot in place, exercise key added, key changed, key removed, application-mutated key, and both-changed conflict; assert each outcome and that a WARNING names the reconciled keys. A DIGEST-ONLY IMPLEMENTATION CANNOT PASS THIS TEST - that is the point.
- The common (unchanged) path costs one hash.
close_reason: Three-way launch-context reconciliation.

title: Release B: startup state machine with a durable commit point
description:
Section 11.5; invariants 18, 25; decisions 8 and 14 [R3, R2-4, R2-5]. Landing order step 11.

Moving the startup-completion fact into a durable envelope [R3] was the right direction and is retained. Two defects remain.

NO DURABLE COMMIT POINT [R2-4]. Revision 2 simultaneously required that startup completion be written when the turn completes, that workflow context be written only at retirement or shutdown (invariant 12), and that the write be skipped when the context digest is unchanged. Those cannot all hold. A startup that performs an external side effect or read-only initialization WITHOUT mutating workflow.context completes successfully, changes only in-memory startup.completed, leaves the digest unchanged, has no retirement yet, and is skipped by the no-write path; a crash then loses the fact and restart REPLAYS STARTUP. Current completion persists conversation and pending state before DONE (turns.py:302-318) with no context-envelope commit.

THE RECORD CANNOT EXPRESS THE STATES THAT OCCUR [R2-5]. {"idempotency_key": null, "completed": false} cannot represent attempted, suspended, succeeded, command-level failure, executor exception, partial mutation, or whether a result remains collectable. _run_turn transitions to DONE even after an exception (turns.py:307-318), and TurnStatus.COMPLETED is orthogonal to command success.

RESOLUTION:
- Explicit states: not_attempted, in_progress, suspended, succeeded, failed - with a stated success predicate that does NOT equate DONE with success, and an epoch so a deliberate reset is expressible.
- Commit point: the semantic-envelope commit is SYNCHRONOUS and completes BEFORE startup success becomes observable (invariant 25). It digests the COMPLETE ENVELOPE, not just context, so a metadata-only change still writes. Store failure at this point has a defined response and retry policy rather than being silently skipped.
- Whether startup has already run is derived from PERSISTED STATE, never from in-process turn retention (invariant 18), so it cannot depend on a wall-clock retention window.
- Scope of the guarantee: exactly-once applies to FRAMEWORK-MANAGED effects only; external side effects require application-owned idempotency (section 3.2 non-goal).

The object-context contradiction is resolved by the section 11.1 declaration, not by the envelope: an undeclared workflow such as simple_workflow_template is pinned, is never checkpointed, writes no startup record, and reruns startup on a genuinely fresh runtime exactly as today.
acceptance_criteria:
Section 16.3 startup semantics:
- A no-context-mutation startup survives process death (the fact is durable).
- mutate-then-raise; success=False; suspension during startup.
- Process death after command completion but before terminal publication.
- Store failure at the commit point has a defined, tested response.
- Restart of simple_workflow_template reruns startup and does not resurrect a phantom root object.
close_reason: Startup state machine with a durable commit point.

title: Release B: record identity, generation stamp, commit record and atomic publication
description:
Sections 11.3, 11.8, 11.11; invariants 16, 26, 27; decisions 9, 11 [R2-10, R2-13, R11]. Landing order step 10. Fold with the startup, reconciliation and credential slices into one envelope-and-store change, where they are cheapest (section 20 sequencing item 4).

IDENTITY [R2-13]. VERIFIED - disk channel IDs are NON-INJECTIVE: safe_id = channel_id.replace(os.sep, "_").replace("/", "_") (session_state_store.py:50-52) maps tenant/a and tenant_a to the same file. Redis keys use the raw channel ID under a fixed prefix with no workflow or deployment namespace (:83-94). VERIFIED - the factory cannot express a second namespace: get_session_state_store takes only base_folder, and for SESSION_STATE_STORE=redis base_folder is ignored entirely (:112-142). Revision 2 acknowledged the collision in a limitations list while making the record durable and AUTHORITATIVE, which changes the blast radius of a pre-existing defect rather than inheriting it.
Record shape: protocol_version, record_type, generation, deployment_id, workflow_fingerprint, channel_key, channel_id_hash, session_incarnation, declaration_version, context, runtime {active_conversation_id, stream_format, is_complete}, startup {state, idempotency_key, epoch}, launch_context {prior_projection, digest}. Every identity field is validated on read; a mismatch QUARANTINES rather than applies (invariant 27). channel_key uses an injective, collision-resistant encoding (percent-encoding, or a hash with the raw ID retained inside the record), never replace(os.sep, "_"). Keys are namespaced by deployment and workflow fingerprint; add key_prefix to the store factory [R11]. Disk records are written with private directory and file modes and symlink-safe publication.

ONE STATE GENERATION, ONE COMMIT [R2-10]. os.replace() makes ONE disk file atomic; Redis uses independent SETs. Neither creates one transaction across two records. Crash schedule: a tool mutates application context and suspends on ask_user; context generation N+1 is published; pending publication fails or the process dies; restore combines context N+1 with pending N, or with none. The reverse ordering is also unsafe - a durable pending trajectory can resume against rolled-back application state and repeat effects. "Persist before pop" protects controlled eviction only.
Work: a monotonic per-channel generation stamped on every record that participates in a checkpoint; a commit record naming the generation considered complete; restore requires all participating records to match the committed generation and on mismatch FAILS CLOSED - the channel is quarantined, its records are preserved for inspection, it starts from launch configuration, and a WARNING plus a metric is emitted (NEVER a silent merge). Redis multi-key atomicity requires same-slot key design; disk requires a manifest or directory-level generation protocol.

TRANSACTIONAL RETIREMENT (11.11), while holding the manager retirement critical section after confirming zero leases and a false union predicate: verify eligibility; serialize the declared projection through the single strict serializer; SKIP the write if the envelope digest is unchanged; publish the composite generation atomically; pop the runtime ONLY after required writes succeed; close and release. On serialization or store failure leave the runtime in _sessions, try another candidate, and warn with channel ID, backend and exception class - never log payloads, context values or credentials. Popping first and treating persistence as best effort is REJECTED: it loses state on the exact path where preservation failed. save_serialized() writes a sibling temporary file and publishes with os.replace() so a crash leaves either the old complete record or the new complete record, never truncated JSON.
acceptance_criteria:
Section 16.3:
- Identity binding: separator aliases (tenant/a vs tenant_a), Unicode, control characters, oversized IDs, deliberately swapped records, two workflows sharing one Redis, and channel-ID reuse across incarnations - assert QUARANTINE, not silent application.
- Generation atomicity: fault-inject at EVERY write boundary, then reconstruct in a FRESH process; a partial generation must fail closed rather than combine.
- Namespaces: record kinds do not collide for one channel_id, and a normal turn's pending clear() does not delete the checkpoint.
- Unchanged revisit produces no second write; nested in-place mutation produces exactly one new write; empty saved context persists {} and does not resurrect old or launch-time keys.
- Disk failure preserves the live runtime and the prior complete record.
close_reason: Record identity, generation stamp, commit record, atomic publication.

title: Release B: workflow-declared durable projection, enumerated restorable fields, and pinning
description:
Sections 11.1, 11.2, 11.6; invariant 11; decisions 25 and 26 [R2-5, R2-8, R2-9, R2-12]. Landing order step 9. THIS IS THE SYSTEM-OF-RECORD DECISION, not a cache detail.

Revision 2 inferred safety from three negative checks (no command-context object, no live child, JSON-projectable context). Concrete state that omits:
- Workflow.is_complete, which is settable and included in the workflow's own _to_dict() (workflow.py:282-289, :383-390);
- ChannelRuntime.active_conversation_id and stream_format (utils.py:644-658);
- current conversation selection, which can differ from "latest conversation" (__main__.py:1439-1473);
- repeated mutable-container identity: {"a": shared, "b": shared} is acyclic and JSON-native but restores as two independent lists;
- stale child IDs: _children can outlive a weakly registered child, so testing bool(_children) either pins forever or ignores a genuinely live descendant.
The active-conversation omission is CORRUPTING, not cosmetic: suspend in older conversation 1, evict, cold-create restoring the latest conversation 2, overlay conversation-1 pending history, resume - and the turn is saved under conversation 2. SSE likewise silently becomes NDJSON after eviction.
Revision 2's policy was also a silent DATA-CLASSIFICATION change [R2-12]: it excluded exactly one top-level key (http_bearer_token) and otherwise persisted every JSON-native value from an unrestricted Workflow.context, plus pending ReAct trajectory, inputs, action log and conversation turns, in plaintext - permitting api_key, refresh tokens, cookies, signed URLs, database credentials, a NESTED http_bearer_token, and secrets supplied as an ask_user answer and retained in the trajectory.

RESOLUTION - ONE PRINCIPLE replaces all three findings: durable state is WORKFLOW-DECLARED.
- A workflow declares a versioned durable projection - which context keys are durable, which are ephemeral, which runtime fields participate - as part of its contract.
- NOTHING IS DURABLE BY DEFAULT. An undeclared workflow behaves exactly as it does today: its sessions are pinned, nothing is written, and no data-classification boundary moves.
- The framework ENUMERATES the runtime and workflow fields it can restore (is_complete, active_conversation_id, stream_format, current conversation selection, current context name); a field outside that enumeration PINS the session rather than being silently dropped.
- Identity-preserving structures either round-trip with identity preserved or pin.
Release C's bound therefore becomes a property a workflow author OPTS INTO, not one the framework infers.

SECTION 11.2 ELIGIBILITY - a session is evictable only when ALL hold: the workflow declares a durable projection; no root, current or response-generation command-context object is live; no live child workflow state exists; the declared projection passes the section 11.4 strict encoding; the session is NOT awaiting_user and holds no CME continuation state; no lease is held and the union predicate is false. Otherwise the runtime is PINNED - a first-class outcome with a METRIC, not an error.

SECTION 11.6 v1 - pin awaiting and continuation sessions (decision 26). Today's suspended restore already loses the WEC logical-turn accumulator (workflow_execution_context.py:104-114; resume deliberately skips _begin_turn() at :547-549) and the CME continuation keys command / command_name / stored_parameters. That is a PRE-EXISTING defect; Release C makes the path routine, so v1 pins rather than pretending to have fixed it. Completing the serialization is tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Section 16.3 pinning matrix: awaiting session, CME continuation, object context, undeclared workflow, shared-container identity, is_complete, conversation selection and stream format each PIN or RESTORE EXACTLY - none is silently dropped.
- Section 16.4: undeclared/object-context sessions stay live AND the manager reports the pinned count.
- An undeclared workflow writes nothing at all, and its observable behavior is byte-for-byte today's behavior.
- Pinned-session count is a metric, not only a rate-limited warning.
notes: PREMISE INVERTED BY THE 2026-08-05 ADJUDICATION (see fix-g03.13). This issue is titled 'workflow-declared durable projection' and its description assumes decision 25 as originally written: nothing durable by default, workflows opt in. That default was REVERSED. The accepted model is persist-all-JSON-native by default, with author hooks to extend or override, a warning when a workflow that needs a hook has not implemented one, and no warning for an explicit no-op. Do not implement this issue from its own description. The hook mechanism is designed and approved under fix-qyz first; reference implementations for the five pinned bundled workflows are fix-gbh; the 'or pin' half of this issue stands and is strengthened - a session whose command-context object has no hook is never evicted and warns at workflow load.
close_reason: Declared projection, enumerated restorable fields and pinning.

title: Release B: one strict serializer at the WorkflowExecutionContext boundary (remove the default=str round-trip)
acceptance_criteria:
- Section 16.3 strictness through the REAL boundary: an opaque object, a cycle, a non-finite float and a nested artifact driven through ctx.serialize_state() - NOT through the store helper - each leave the runtime live. A test that calls the new store helper directly proves nothing; that is precisely how revision 2's strictness requirement passed review while being unimplementable.
- No default=str remains anywhere in the persistence path.
- Persisted state is strict, versioned JSON.
close_reason: Step 8 landed. New fastworkflow/state_serialization.py: validate_state / encode_state / state_digest. Requires a top-level dict, string keys recursively, JSON-native values only; rejects NaN and infinities, cycles, and identity-significant sharing. Errors name the path to the offending value. Canonical encoding (sorted keys, compact separators, allow_nan=False) so equal states digest identically. The default=str round-trip is removed from WorkflowExecutionContext.serialize_state - the FIRST serializer, which is what made downstream strictness vacuous - and from both disk and redis store saves. Invariant 8 honoured: an encoding failure logs a warning and skips the write, leaving the runtime live. 12 new tests in tests/test_state_serialization.py, five driven through ctx.serialize_state() as section 11.4 requires. It immediately caught a real defect: test_session_state_serialization was persisting a MagicMock react blob that default=str had been silently stringifying; the fixture now returns the real export_suspended() shape. Declared-durable-key filtering (11.4 item 2) arrives with fix-g03.17.

title: Release B: route /invoke_agent_stream through turn admission and make shutdown quiescent
description:
Sections 10.4-10.6; invariants 21, 30 [R2-3, R14, R2-21]. Landing order step 7. Must precede any cap reduction.

STREAMING [R2-3]. Adding the lock to the eviction predicate covers the held-lock window but does not fix streaming's position outside the turn lifecycle:
- /invoke_agent_stream captures the runtime before returning StreamingResponse and acquires the lock only when body iteration begins (__main__.py:953-974, :1073-1085);
- a normal endpoint can register a turn while a stream owns the lock, because the registry sees no active stream (turns.py:195-214);
- run_process_message_with_trace_stream() raises 504 at its own deadline WITHOUT awaiting or cancelling the executor future (utils.py:550-554); the route catches that HTTP exception, emits an error and exits the lock while the executor thread can still mutate WEC and app state.
Failure schedules: (1) a stream suspends on ask_user with an unrelated normal turn queued behind it - on lock release the unrelated query is interpreted as the clarification answer; (2) a stream times out, the registry stays empty, and eviction or shutdown snapshots and closes the context while the detached executor thread is still running; (3) the runtime is evicted after response construction but before Starlette begins consuming the body generator.
RESOLUTION: route streaming through the SAME turn-admission and lifecycle owner as every other turn (invariant 21). Client timeout or disconnect may stop DELIVERY, but registry ownership and the runtime lease remain until the executor exits.

SHUTDOWN [R14, R2-21]. Today _active_turn_channel_ids tests rt.lock.locked() only (__main__.py:285-286), so a QUEUED execution whose task has not yet acquired runtime.lock reports not-busy. Switching to the union predicate is necessary but INSUFFICIENT: shutdown waits at most 30 seconds and then ALWAYS finalizes conversations and closes every runtime (__main__.py:289-342). After the deadline the union can truthfully report remaining work while shutdown snapshots and closes it anyway - and with Release B persistence added it would write a snapshot taken BEFORE the queued turn mutates the context and then close the context under it, making the stale snapshot authoritative on next creation. Detached streaming executor work makes this worse. There is also no atomic "admission closed" state, so a turn can be registered after an empty scan.
RESOLUTION - shutdown: (1) closes admission under registry and manager coordination, atomically with respect to submission; (2) drains queued, running and leased work; (3) after the deadline NEVER snapshots or closes a still-busy runtime - it logs at high severity (ERROR: shutdown deadline expired with work still in flight; runtimes left unclosed) and leaves the process to its host; (4) states explicitly whether queued-but-unstarted work is cancelled before execution or left to host termination. A deadline is a bound on waiting, not a license to write.

KEEP LIFECYCLE OPERATIONS DISTINCT (10.6): evict = remove only the live cache entry after preserving declared durable state; remove/terminate keeps existing explicit semantics until a public channel-deletion contract is designed (scope note [R15]: remove_session and evict_live_session have NO production callers - the only caller in the tree is tests/test_fastapi_topology_b.py:114 - so they are preserved to avoid an unrelated behavior change, not because live contract surface depends on them).
acceptance_criteria:
- Section 16.4 streaming tests: stream->normal, normal->stream, suspension, timeout, disconnect, and eviction attempted before first body iteration.
- Section 16.4 shutdown tests: queued and running work beyond a short deadline, a detached stream worker, and a submission racing the final empty scan; assert NO snapshot or close of still-busy runtimes past the deadline.
- Soak arm C: zero context-loss sentinels, zero torn snapshots, no streaming turn's context closed, no detached executor writes.
close_reason: Step 7 landed. /invoke_agent_stream is now admitted through the turn registry like every other endpoint: the handler takes an eviction lease, registers a TurnExecution, and returns a StreamingResponse whose body only drains an event queue. Ownership is separated from delivery - a client that disconnects stops reading while the turn keeps the registry pointer and runtime.lock until the work exits. Busy channels now get 409 instead of 200-with-an-error-event (approved wire change); shutdown gets 503. run_owned_turn() in turns.py gives async work the same lifecycle contract as _run_turn. The 504 defect is fixed: run_process_message_with_trace_stream no longer abandons the executor future at its deadline - it reports the timeout to the client via on_timeout and still awaits the future, so no detached thread can mutate a context that eviction or shutdown has closed. Shutdown quiescence per section 10.5: admission is closed atomically via TurnRegistry.close_admission() before draining, the drain uses the union predicate plus leases (busy_channel_ids) instead of runtime.lock.locked(), and after the deadline still-busy runtimes are NEVER finalized or closed - logged at ERROR and left to the host. 5 new integration tests in tests/test_fastapi_streaming_lifecycle.py.

title: Release B: manager-owned runtime leases and the union work-in-flight predicate
description:
Sections 10.1-10.3; invariants 6, 19, 20; decision 24 [R2, R2-1, R2-2]. Landing order step 6. Must precede any cap reduction.

(a) THE UNION PREDICATE IS NECESSARY [R2]. is_channel_busy is wired directly to the registry (run_fastapi_mcp/__main__.py:194: session_manager.is_channel_busy = turn_registry.has_active). But /invoke_agent_stream (__main__.py:920-1085) runs an ENTIRE TURN without ever creating a TurnExecution - it guards with runtime.lock.locked() (:963) and holds "async with runtime.lock" (:974). So has_active returns False for the whole streaming turn and the channel looks like a valid victim. Eviction safety must use at minimum turn_registry.has_active(channel) OR (runtime is not None and runtime.lock.locked()).
Invariant 2 still forbids runtime.lock.locked() as the 409 IDEMPOTENCY truth source - the lock is released while a request defers and across AWAITING_USER, which would re-open the v2.22.0 double-execution race. Eviction safety asks a different question, which the lock answers correctly and the registry pointer does not.

(b) THE UNION PREDICATE IS NOT SUFFICIENT [R2-2]. get_session() returns a raw ChannelRuntime after releasing the manager lock (utils.py:745-750). A normal endpoint then awaits registry admission; a streaming endpoint returns a lazy StreamingResponse before acquiring runtime.lock. During either interval BOTH HALVES OF THE UNION ARE FALSE: request A obtains runtime X and releases the manager lock; before A inserts a turn pointer or acquires X's lock, request B creates another channel; the LRU samples the predicate, pops X and closes it; A continues using the detached X; a cold recreation calls Workflow.create() while X still strongly owns the old app workflow, so the weak global registry returns that SAME workflow object and OVERWRITES its context (workflow.py:101-104) - two runtimes and two locks around one mutable workflow. Single-writer-per-channel (invariant 15) is violated by construction.

(c) CREATION MUST NOT EVICT ITS OWN RUNTIME [R2-1]. create_session() inserts the new runtime and calls _evict_oldest_if_needed() before returning (utils.py:752-776); /initialize submits startup only after creation returns (__main__.py:718-769). Before startup the new runtime has no registry pointer, its lock is free, and its workflow has no root or current object. At the Release C default with 50 older sessions pinned by object contexts, channel 51 is the ONLY apparently safe candidate - precisely because its startup has not yet created the object context that will pin it - so the manager evicts the runtime it is in the middle of creating and /initialize's second lookup returns 500 (__main__.py:735-740). This defect appears exactly when the new default begins to matter.

WORK: a manager-owned lease (refcount) acquired ATOMICALLY with the manager-lock lookup that returns the runtime, released only after the work that lookup enabled has finished - turn registration or lock acquisition takes over, and the lease persists until the executor exits. get_session() returns a leased handle, or an explicit acquire/release pair with a context manager; a raw runtime reference that outlives the manager lock IS the defect. Plus an initialization lease held from insertion until startup admission or completion establishes final eligibility. Eviction requires a ZERO LEASE COUNT in addition to a false union predicate.
acceptance_criteria:
Section 16.4 manager tests, each of which must FAIL against the pre-change implementation:
- LRU never evicts a channel with a live registry execution.
- LRU never evicts a channel whose runtime.lock is held but which has no registry execution (the /invoke_agent_stream shape) - must fail against the registry-only predicate.
- LRU never evicts a leased runtime between lookup and admission, with barriers for the normal AND streaming intervals - must fail against a predicate-only implementation.
- A cap-one manager whose single existing session is pinned does not evict the channel it is creating, with and without a startup action - must fail against revision 2's ordering.
- WARNING logged when a channel is skipped for eviction because a lease was held, or the lock was held with no registry execution.
close_reason: Step 6 landed. ChannelSessionManager gained refcounted per-channel eviction leases: leased_session() takes the lease under the same manager lock that hands out the runtime (invariant 19), initialization_lease() covers creation before the session exists (invariant 20), and _has_work_in_flight() is the union of the registry pointer and a held runtime.lock (invariant 6). Eviction now requires zero leases AND an idle union. Ten endpoint handlers converted to leased_session; /invoke_agent_stream deliberately left for step 7 because its body outlives the handler. 7 new integration tests in tests/test_fastapi_session_leases.py, including the section 10.3 counterexample parametrized with and without a startup action. Non-vacuity verified empirically: going straight to create_session without the initialization lease, the newcomer IS evicted by its own overflow sweep.

title: Release B gate: resolve decisions 18, 23, 24 and 25 before any Release B code lands
description:
Section 15.1 ("R1 is a decision, not a step") and section 20 sequencing item 1. These four change what section 1 PROMISES, not how it is implemented, so they are adjudicated before code.

DECISION 18 [R1] - Release C's bound is conditional on workflow shape, DISCLOSED rather than mitigated. Corrected census (revision 2 had two errors): simple_workflow_template (_commands/startup.py:12), messaging_app_2 (_commands/startup.py:42) and tests/todo_list_workflow (_commands/startup.py:12) assign a ROOT command context and pin from their first turn; messaging_app_4 has no startup.py and pins only when set_root_context runs (_commands/set_root_context.py:15); messaging_app_3 pins when initialize_user runs (:46) because it assigns workflow.current_command_context; messaging_app_1, retail_workflow and hello_world never pin. simple_workflow_template is the scaffold new workflows are copied from, so PINNED IS THE DEFAULT for newly authored workflows. Rejected alternatives: evict without a snapshot (reintroduces silent state loss); cap the pinned set and shed load with 503 (needs the Step-2 admission-control work to be coherent; still the preferred long-term answer).
DECISION 23 - the single atomic release is withdrawn in favor of three gated releases.
DECISION 24 - eviction safety is a lease, not a predicate.
DECISION 25 - durable state is workflow-declared; nothing is durable by default.

Review-interaction rule: give an ELI5 plain-language explanation of each item BEFORE asking decision questions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the four decisions is explicitly ratified or amended by the owner and recorded in the design doc's decision log.
- If decision 18 is amended (for example toward 503 load-shedding), section 1 and the Release C scope are updated before any Release B code lands.
notes:
ADJUDICATED 2026-08-05 by Dhar. All four decisions resolved; Release B implementation is unblocked EXCEPT for the persistence work, which now waits on fix-qyz (hook mechanism design + approval).

DECISION 23 - three gated releases instead of one atomic release: RATIFIED AS WRITTEN. Already validated by events: Release A shipped standalone in v2.25.0 and its standalone value was measured (hot-channel RSS slope +1.494 -> +0.00040 MB/request; no-eviction live hit 490.7 -> 38.1 ms p50; two full suite runs, 1017 passed, zero failures).

DECISION 24 - eviction safety is a lease, not a sampled boolean: RATIFIED AS WRITTEN. No working alternative exists; any boolean sampled after get_session() releases the manager lock has the same hole, and the failure mode is not a lost cache entry but two runtimes and two locks around one mutable workflow, breaking single-writer-per-channel. Accepted cost: get_session() returns a leased handle instead of a raw runtime, which touches every caller.

DECISION 25 - who decides what is persisted: MODIFIED, NOT ACCEPTED AS WRITTEN. The design said "nothing durable by default; the workflow declares what may be persisted". That default is REVERSED. Accepted instead:
  - persist all JSON-native context BY DEFAULT;
  - expose hooks so the app developer can EXTEND or OVERRIDE serialization;
  - WARN when a workflow that needs a hook has not implemented one;
  - an explicit NO-OP implementation does NOT warn - a no-op is the author's signal that they know about the requirement, so silence is consent while absence is not;
  - the hook mechanism must follow well-known established serialization-hook patterns rather than a bespoke invention;
  - Dhar reviews and approves the hook design BEFORE any implementation.
This trades safety-by-default for coverage-by-default, managing the risk with visibility. Consequence: Release C's bound is NOT opt-in - it applies to every workflow whose author has engaged with the hook. Tracked in fix-qyz.
RESIDUAL RISK CARRIED INTO THE HOOK DESIGN: persist-all moves the data-classification boundary, and a warning only protects a deployment if somebody reads logs. fix-qyz must propose a default redaction pass over credential-shaped values in addition to the warning.

DECISION 18 - pinned workflows: RE-EVALUATED under the modified decision 25 and RESOLVED MORE STRONGLY THAN "DISCLOSE".
Reframing: the context dict was never what pinned these workflows. What pins them is the live command-context object (TodoListManager, the WorkItem tree), which is not JSON-native, so persist-all does not reach it either. The hook from decision 25 is therefore also the mechanism that makes a workflow evictable at all, and decision 18 narrows to "what happens when the hook is absent".
  (a) UNIMPLEMENTED HOOK => NEVER EVICT, AND WARN AT WORKFLOW LOAD. Honours the design's non-negotiable rule 1 (a session that cannot be checkpointed safely is not evicted). The live-session cache may sit over target indefinitely; that is visible through a pinned-count metric and a load-time warning naming the workflow, rather than silent state loss. Rejected: evict-and-drop with a warning (still loses application state on every eviction, just loudly); cap-and-shed with 503 (still the preferred long-term answer, still needs the deferred admission-control work).
  (b) REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATIONS FOR ALL FIVE PINNED BUNDLED WORKFLOWS in Release B - simple_workflow_template, messaging_app_2, messaging_app_3, messaging_app_4, tests/todo_list_workflow - so the bound is unconditional across the bundled set and the scaffold new workflows are copied from is born bounded rather than born pinned. Tracked in fix-gbh. Effort is real, not cosmetic: the WorkItem tree is cyclic and carries an identity-keyed _child_pos map.

NEW EVIDENCE THAT DROVE 18 (measured during Release A, not inferred): these sessions do not merely stay unbounded, they SILENTLY LOSE the command context when evicted today - root='TodoListManager' before, root=NoneType / current='*' after. Reachable above 2000 live sessions now; Release C would make it routine. Full reproduction in fix-3vy.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE DESIGN DOC. docs/fastworkflow_memory_bounds_design.md is now stale in three places and needs a revision 4 before the persistence code lands: section 11.1 (declared state / nothing-durable-by-default is reversed), section 11.2 (snapshot eligibility now keys off hook presence rather than declaration), and decision-log entries 18 and 25. Section 1.4's census stays correct. Sequence the revision AFTER fix-qyz is approved, so the doc describes the mechanism that was actually chosen.

REMAINING SEQUENCE: fix-qyz (design + approval) -> design doc revision 4 -> Release B steps 6-14 (fix-g03.14 .. fix-g03.22) -> fix-gbh -> tests (fix-g03.23, fix-g03.24) -> Release C. Steps 6 and 7 (leases, streaming lifecycle) do not depend on fix-qyz and can start immediately.

title: S2 CR24: holdout guarantees labels >=1 training row but the trainer demands >=2 — mid-run abort with integer label ids in the error
description: Two modules enforce different invariants for the same requirement. split_by_persona's rescue rule fires only on ZERO training rows (starved_labels, heldout_evaluation.py:414-421); split_training_data raises TrainingDataError below TWO (model_pipeline_training.py:66-76). A command with zero plain_utterances (the seed check at train/__main__.py:85-94 is explicitly advisory) whose synthetic rows all came from held-out personas is left with exactly [command_name] — passes the rescue, kills the entire multi-context run mid-loop after earlier contexts' LLM/GPU spend. Compounding: the error prints ENCODED label ids ('labels with fewer rows: [3, 11]') because split_training_data receives zip(X, y_encoded) (:1273) — a developer cannot map ids to commands without reverse-engineering the LabelEncoder. DO: align the invariants (rescue threshold = the trainer's floor of 2), and inverse_transform labels before formatting the error. Cheap, two-file fix.
close_reason: Fixed, two-file as predicted. (1) The rescue threshold in split_by_persona now uses the shared constant heldout_evaluation.MIN_TRAINING_ROWS_PER_LABEL (=2) instead of firing only at ZERO training rows, so the persona split can no longer hand split_training_data a label it will refuse. The root defect was two modules enforcing the same requirement with different numbers; both now read one constant, which is what stops it recurring. (2) split_training_data takes an optional decode_label callable and the caller passes label_encoder.inverse_transform, so the abort names commands ('TodoList/cmd_3') instead of encoded ids ('[3, 11]'). Tests pin both; mutation-checked (reverting either the threshold or the decoder fails a test). One pre-existing test asserted on the note wording 'zero training rows' and was updated to 'floor' -- behaviour assertions untouched, and zero is still rescued because zero is below the floor.

title: S2 CR18: unresolved-persona composite ids embed the '+' separator they are later split on — attribution corruption and phantom personas
description: CONFIRMED by code reading. _resolve_persona_id builds '__unresolved__:' + '1+2+3' (generate_synthetic.py:190) — the id embeds PERSONA_ID_SEPARATOR by construction. _attribute_utterance's merge (:165-170) splits blindly on that separator, so merging an unresolved batch id with a resolved id yields fragments like '2+3+5+__unresolved__:1'. heldout_evaluation.expand_persona_id (:300-303) strips the prefix only at string START, so it returns the phantom atomic persona '__unresolved__:1' while LOSING persona '1' — persona 1's other utterances can sit in training while this text is held out: the exact D1 leak class, violating the invariant the merge code itself documents ('must exclude such an utterance unless every contributor is held out'). Ironic: personas.py:125-131 rejects app-supplied ids containing '+' for precisely this mis-parse; determinism.py's own reserved format violates the invariant. Trigger: a common short utterance produced both in a batch whose LLM-echoed header was garbled AND by a resolved persona. DO: make the merge strip UNRESOLVED_PERSONA_PREFIX from both sides before splitting (re-prefixing the union), or encode unresolved ids without embedding the separator; make expand_persona_id handle the prefix at any position defensively; add a merge test for resolved+unresolved collision.
notes: Normalized persona attribution collisions to a sorted union of atomic contributors; any unresolved input re-prefixes the complete union exactly once, and seed attribution remains absorbing. Heldout expansion now strips unresolved prefixes from every separator-delimited atom, so legacy malformed cache records cannot create phantom personas or lose contributors. No API/schema change and existing cache files are interpreted safely without rewriting. Verification: 4 targeted collision/holdout regressions passed locally; implementation pass ran 128 focused tests; only pre-existing Sourcery/formatting debt remains.

title: S2 CR10: persona-holdout 'routing' metric blends escalation-class rows into routing accuracy, violating D2
description: CONFIRMED. Escalation rows are appended to utterance_command_tuples labeled WILDCARD_LABEL at model_pipeline_training.py:1171-1173 BEFORE the persona split is built from that same list (:1210-1224); ancestor utterances carry real persona attribution, so wildcard-labeled rows land in heldout_records and score_routing counts predictions[0]=='wildcard' as a correct top-1 route — a semantics the runtime does not have (a lone wildcard escalates; it is not a route). Per F8 wildcard is 48-91% of rows in contexts with ancestors, so the headline persona-holdout routing number for such contexts is dominated by escalation-class recognition. D2: routing and escalation are NEVER blended. per_command exposes it but aggregate_totals (heldout_evaluation.py:944-946) and the TOTAL row blend with no filter or note. title: S2 CR8: carry-forward safety gated on cache MODE, never cache CONTENT — a lost utterance cache silently publishes the AR3-inconsistent version
description: selective_training.py:834-846: the guard is 'if cache_mode != _MODE_REUSE: full retrain'. The AR3 rationale in the adjacent comment (retrained contexts on fresh text while carried-forward contexts keep old text) applies identically when the mode IS reuse but the entries are ABSENT — cache dir deleted, fresh clone, cache never committed. Then every command in the retrained contexts is redrawn from the LLM (non-reproducible per M4) while carried contexts embody the superseded ancestor text: exactly the merged-version hazard D8/AR3 says versioning cannot detect and the implementation must prevent. Nothing checks hit/miss — __main__.py:242-243 only prints cache.format_summary(). DO: after generation, if any retrained context experienced a cache MISS for a command that also contributes (as ancestor or own) to a carried-forward context, escalate to full retrain (or refuse carry-forward for the affected contexts). The hit/miss counters already exist; the check is a comparison against the plan's carried-forward set. Tie must break toward retraining (M12).

title: S2 CR7: AR3 promotion-time consistency check does not exist; the substitute is not independent of the dirty-set computation
description: R4-as-amended (AR3) requires a promotion-time check that re-derives R5's closure as a POSTCONDITION — refuse to advance current when any context's recorded ancestor-contribution fingerprints disagree with the fingerprints actually present in that version — precisely so a closure bug is caught at promotion instead of shipped. Shipped: publish_version (artifact_versioning.py:586) validates only that the version dir exists and no legacy dir blocks a name. The de-facto substitute (plan-time signature diff) is computed from the same build_context_maps call as the closure itself (selective_training.py:863, compute_training_signature :581-582), so a deterministic bug in commands()/get_ancestor_contexts reproduces identically in baseline and current, diffs clean, and publishes. Also the manifest records wildcard sources as command NAMES, not per-context utterance-set fingerprints as AR3 specifies (mapping to command_fingerprints derivable but never checked). DO: at publish time, independently recompute each carried-forward context's expected ancestor-contribution fingerprints from the version's own manifest/command fingerprints and refuse to flip on mismatch; store utterance-set fingerprints per context in the manifest.

title: S2 CR6: 'already up to date' path never republishes — a broken/mixed compat-entry state persists while train prints success
description: train/__main__.py:190-202: when the plan is empty, the run prints 'Training artifacts are already up to date.', prunes, and returns without calling publish_version — even though publish_version is documented idempotent and one call would repair every compat entry. Failure scenarios: (a) after a crash mid-publish (CR5) the new version's training_signature.json was already written pre-publish (:274), so the next run diffs clean, no-ops, and the chimera state persists indefinitely; (b) a user deletes a top-level context symlink — is_workflow_trained reports untrained, CommandRouter crashes at runtime, yet fastworkflow train insists everything is fine. DO: on the no-op path, call publish_version(current) unconditionally (idempotent self-repair), or verify compat entries resolve into the current version and republish when any do not. Pairs with CR5; the two together restore AR3's crash story.
notes: Added no-op publication repair: an empty training plan now republishes the current version before retention, restoring missing/mixed compatibility readers and pruning only after repair. Missing current version fails with TrainingDataError; success is printed only after repair completes. Real-filesystem regression covers missing and misrouted context links plus retention. Verification: orchestration + cache contract tests 56 passed locally, 2 long-backoff tests deselected; implementation batch ran 123 focused tests, 2 deselected.

title: S2 CR5: publish_version flips current.json BEFORE compat entries — crash mid-publish violates AR3's atomic-flip invariant
description: CONFIRMED. artifact_versioning.py:626-629: _write_pointer runs first, then per-context compat entries swap one at a time. A crash or OSError mid-loop leaves current.json naming the new version while some compat entries still target the old one — the two reader paths (get_artifact_path via pointer, model_pipeline_training.py:679-714; intent_detection.py:45 via compat entries) resolve to DIFFERENT versions per context: the exact 'neither old nor new' state AR3 forbids ('A crash mid-merge must leave current on the old version'). The docstring defends pointer-first for prune-safety, trading away the crash invariant. Mitigating: both versions are complete on disk, so every resolved model is A trained model. Aggravated by CR6 (no-repair no-op path, separate issue). Add the crash-mid-publish test (separate test-gap issue).
notes: Reordered publish_version so per-context compatibility entries, the convenience link, and stale-entry removal are prepared before current.json is atomically committed last. Pruning now protects both pointer-current and routed versions. Fault injection proves a pre-commit failure leaves current.json old, protects both versions from prune, and an idempotent retry converges. title: Bare-value catch on retail may have regressed since the committed artifacts were trained (confounded, needs its own experiment)
description:
OBSERVATION, NOT AN ATTRIBUTED REGRESSION. Reporting it because it is easy to lose and it bears on fix-2m5 / fix-cm2.

Probing the COMMITTED (pre-R7.1) retail artifacts and a FRESHLY TRAINED retail workflow with the same 14 bare-value probes (docs/experiments/data/retail_probe_sets.json):

                                          committed (pre-R7.1)   fresh (current code, pv7, seed 42)
  reserved label takes top-1 on bare value        7/14                    0/14
  clean catch (all candidates non-routable)       6/14                    0/14
  reserved label top-1 on a routing case          0/72                    0/72
  routing top-1 on the E-PV1 benchmark           45/72                   46/72

Pooled over 5 seeds the fresh number is better than seed 42 alone suggests (parameter_value leads on 31/70 bare values, clean catch 5/35 held-out), so seed 42 is the unlucky draw rather than the typical one. The direction of the difference nonetheless persists.

WHY THIS IS CONFOUNDED AND MUST NOT BE CLAIMED AS A REGRESSION YET. The committed artifacts carry no training_provenance.json — fastworkflow/examples/retail_workflow/___command_info/global/ holds only the two models, the label encoder and three threshold files. The generation settings (SYNTHETIC_UTTERANCE_GEN_NUMOF_PERSONAS, UTTERANCES_PER_PERSONA), the resulting per-command row counts, and the training hyperparameters in force when they were built are all unknown. The reserved class's SHARE of total rows is the quantity that plausibly differs, and it cannot be recovered from the artifacts.

ONE HYPOTHESIS ALREADY RULED OUT. I expected R7.1 to have shrunk the reserved class by discarding the wildcard command's synthetic utterances on flat workflows. It did not: wildcard.py's generate_utterances returns only the humanised command name, so wildcard_utterances is a single row. Pre-R7.1 the retail reserved class was ~8 rows and post-R7.1 parameter_value is 7. A one-row difference cannot explain 6/14 -> 0/14.

REMAINING CANDIDATES, none tested:
  (a) the committed artifacts were trained with FEWER generated rows per command, making the ~7 reserved rows a larger share of the label mass (fresh runs: ~530 total rows, so 7 rows = 1.4%);
  (b) training hyperparameters (epochs, max_length, model ids) changed since;
  (c) the two-tier ambiguity thresholds, which are computed as the mean confidence of misclassified test samples, landed differently.

(a) is the one worth testing first, and E-PV1's exploratory pv_diverse arm already shows the mechanism is live: raising parameter_value from 7 to 28 DIVERSE rows takes held-out catch from 5/35 to 35/35 at every seed, for a routing cost of -0.8pp (p=0.804). So reserved-class coverage clearly controls this axis. If (a) is right, the 'regression' is really 'the class was never sized relative to the workflow', which is the same finding from the other side.

SUGGESTED EXPERIMENT: retrain retail at 2-3 generation volumes with the reserved class fixed at 7 rows and measure catch as a function of reserved SHARE. Reuse tests/measure_parameter_value_tradeoff.py; it already varies the class and records the full posterior per probe.

ALSO WORTH FIXING INDEPENDENTLY: the committed example artifacts have no provenance record at all, which is why this question is unanswerable rather than merely unanswered. Anything shipped in examples/ should carry the training_provenance.json the trainer already knows how to write.

Found by E-PV1 (docs/experiments/E-PV1_parameter_value_tradeoff_retail.md).
notes:
POST-FIX-IY0 BASELINE COMPLETE. Pre-registered five-seed pv7-only run on isolated retail copies (42/7/1234/2026/99); no bundled ___command_info copied. All five planned runs completed once, no seed dropped/rerun. Fresh-cache audit: 0 old variants installed, 95 new command-seed entries harvested, 0 template echoes in 2,028 generated rows versus 157/2,173 in the old five-seed cache. Results: routing 210/360 (58.3%, Wilson [0.532, 0.633]) vs old 220/360; parameter_value routing steals 0/360 again (Wilson [0, 0.011]); clean held-out catch 6/35 (17.1%, Wilson [0.081, 0.327]) vs old 5/35; all-bare parameter_value leads 40/70 vs old 31/70. Paired old/new fixed-instrument comparisons: routing 37 fixed/47 broken, McNemar p=.326; clean catch 3 fixed/2 broken, p=1.0; all-bare leads 19 gained/10 lost, p=.136. The generated training rows are fresh draws, so these paired case movements are descriptive, not a causal estimate of the filter. M10 survives: pv7 does not steal retail routes and remains a weak catcher ('leads but cannot close'). Do NOT rerun all 30 arms. If pv_diverse or another arm is proposed for production, rerun only clean pv7 plus that arm (10 runs with shared clean caches). Full record: docs/experiments/E-PV1_parameter_value_tradeoff_retail.md section 9; machine artifacts in .pv_tradeoff_post_fix_iy0_results/. This resolves the fix-iy0 confound on the current pv7 baseline but NOT this issue's narrower old-committed-artifact question: those artifacts still have unknown generation volume/hyperparameters and no provenance. Return issue to open rather than falsely claiming that comparison explained.
RESOLVED EXPERIMENTALLY; HISTORICAL ATTRIBUTION RETIRED. Five-seed paired sweep reused identical clean caches and retained full/half/quarter generated rows, 10 trainings and zero LLM calls. All-bare catch: 16/70 full -> 60/70 half -> 43/70 quarter. Half vs full 46 fixed/2 broken, McNemar p=8.36e-12. Quarter was significantly worse than half (4 fixed/21 broken, p=.00091), refuting the pre-registered monotonic reserved-share hypothesis. Half preserved routing (211/360 vs 210/360 full, p=1.0); routing steals remained negligible. Lower volume/composition is a real current-model lever, but the historical 6/14 cannot be attributed: old rows, env, persona/LLM draw, thresholds and provenance are absent and checkpoint differs; clean full seeds already span 0/14..7/14. No old setting inferred. Results: E-PV1 section 10, .pv_generation_volume_results/fix_16d_volume_analysis.json; spec M15. Future proposals may test half volume prospectively, but no historical task remains.

title: generate_dspy_examples writes rejected examples into valid_examples
description:
Found while adding the parameter-example cache (fix-czb). generate_dspy_examples spends most of its body validating each parsed example (validate_parameters + fuzzy Levenshtein matching against the utterance) and accumulates the survivors in `validated_examples`. That list is then never used: line ~796 does `dict_examples = transform_examples_to_dict_format(examples)` over ALL parsed examples, and line ~813 has the correct return commented out as `# return validated_examples, rejected_examples`.

Consequence: <command>_param_labeled.json's "valid_examples" contains examples the validator explicitly rejected -- ones whose parameter values do not appear in their own utterance, i.e. hallucinated parameter values. Those are exactly the examples that are worst to few-shot prompt a parameter extractor with, and they are also duplicated verbatim into "rejected_examples" in the same file.

Measured on examples/messaging_app_4 at TRAINING_SEED=42: every command wrote 15 valid_examples while rejecting a non-zero number of them, so the two lists overlap.

Not fixed under fix-czb deliberately: switching to validated_examples changes what the runtime is prompted with, which is a training-data QUALITY change and needs its own before/after measurement of parameter-extraction accuracy, not a drive-by edit inside a determinism fix. The cache's fingerprint already covers validate_parameters' source, so making the change will invalidate every cached entry and regenerate cleanly.
notes:
CORRECTION to the description. The dead-code defect is real (validated_examples is assigned and never returned; transform_examples_to_dict_format runs over the unfiltered examples list), but the CONSEQUENCE was NOT observed: across 12 command-runs measured for fix-czb (hello_world x4, messaging_app_4 x10) every file had valid=15 and rejected=0, so nothing leaked. Disregard the description's claim that a non-zero rejection count was measured. Separately, that zero deserves a look of its own: validate_parameters rejected nothing in 12 runs at the 0.3 threshold train/__main__.py passes, so it may be inert rather than satisfied.
PYDANTIC V2 ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED. The zero-rejection result was not evidence that the validator was satisfied: extract_field_details rendered str annotations as "<class 'str'>", while the parser only recognizes the literal type name "str". It therefore extracted no string parameters, validate_parameters saw an empty dict, and every example passed. The second defect was the originally-filed one: even rejected source examples were transformed into valid runtime examples. Fixed both: normalize primitive/optional types and transform validated_examples only. A discriminating real-component test sends alice/alice (accepted) and alice/mallory (rejected at normalized edit distance 0.714 > 0.3), verifies mallory never enters the runtime few-shot schema, and constructs the real dspy.Example consumer shape. Integrator found and fixed one follow-on risk before acceptance: a naive get_args implementation flattened list[str] to str, changing the prompt type; optional unwrapping is now restricted to actual Union/UnionType annotations and list[str] is pinned by test. Affected suite: 41 passed. Remaining limitations intentionally NOT papered over: numeric/bool values are accepted automatically, and a missing required parameter is not rejected because unsupported complex field types are not parsed; enforcing missing fields now could erase all examples for those commands. Keep issue open pending one real-LLM quality draw on string-bearing commands to measure false rejections at threshold 0.3.
REAL-LLM ACCEPTANCE AUDIT AND LONG-TEXT FOLLOW-UP COMPLETE. Isolated fresh draw on all five string-bearing messaging_app_4 commands: requested/parsed 75/75; initially accepted 73 and rejected 2. Manual audit of all 73 accepted examples / 103 string values found zero obvious hallucinations; no missing fields or unsupported types in this workflow. Both rejections were FALSE positives on valid long broadcast messages. Root cause: after exact matching failed on punctuation/light paraphrase, the fuzzy matcher compared a 10+ word value against windows capped at five words. Raising global threshold 0.3 would be unsafe for short IDs, so the fix is length-aware: retain 1-5 word windows and add windows within two words of the extracted value's own length. Regression tests pin both real rejected messages as valid and mallory vs alice as invalid. Revalidated all 105 string values from the real draw under the final code: 105 checked, 0 invalid. Parameter-cache fingerprint already digests validate_parameters plus the new helper, so stale entries invalidate. Affected suite 44 passed. Original issue is resolved and may close. Residual missing-required/complex-type limitation is separate fix-hru; numeric/bool auto-validation remains disclosed. Evidence: .param_validator_quality_results/summary.json; spec M13; NLU reference updated.
FINAL VERIFICATION: 975 passed, 13 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed in the final full-suite rerun. The preceding full-suite attempt had one unrelated selective-training route-quality failure; the same test passed immediately in isolation and in the full rerun with unchanged code, confirming fresh-LLM training-draw variance. Tracked separately as fix-s0p; no test was weakened or removed.

title: Provenance is keyed by command name only, so per-command row counts are wrong in multi-context workflows
description: ProvenanceRecorder.record is last-write-wins and keyed by command name alone, but utterance generation in train() is keyed by CONTEXT (context_utterance_cache). A command that is a label in two workflow-owned contexts is generated twice with two different LLM draws, and provenance keeps only the second. R3b's ROWS column is therefore 'last generation count', not 'rows across all contexts'; R6's utterance cache likely needs the same key. Not observable on bundled examples (hello_world and retail_workflow each have one trainable context after train() subtracts the internal CME IntentDetection context); it bites on IDO-shaped workflows, which is the shape R3b serves. Fix: add a 'context' field to UtteranceProvenance and key the recorder on (context, command).
notes:
Second, related provenance gap from the same R3b work: no record of which commands the trainer SKIPPED. _requires_utterances excludes commands without a Signature.Input from intent training and those produce no provenance record, so training_report.py cannot tell 'deliberately excluded' from 'provenance lost' and re-implements the predicate by reading input_for_param_extraction_class from command_directory.json. Tested and working, but duplicates the trainer's rule and will drift silently. Fix alongside the context key: add a set of skipped command names to ProvenanceRecorder.
RESOLVED WITH PROVENANCE SCHEMA V2. Generation now happens once per fully-qualified command, matching the generator/cache identity. Provenance separates commands (one seed/persona/fallback generation record) from context_training (one context+command row-use or explicit skipped_no_input/skipped_no_utterances/included_fallback record). Training reports show aggregate and rows_by_context, but apply the row floor independently to every context, so inherited totals cannot hide a starved context. Legacy flat v1 provenance remains readable and is not rewritten on read; the next successful train writes v2. Public generation signature and byte-identical cache guarantees remain. Focused real-training/report/cache verification: 123 passed. Spec M16 and NLU reference updated.

title: Provenance is keyed by command name only, so per-command row counts are wrong in multi-context workflows
description:
ProvenanceRecorder.record is last-write-wins and keyed by command name alone, but utterance generation in model_pipeline_training.train() is keyed by CONTEXT (context_utterance_cache). A command that is a label in two workflow-owned contexts is therefore generated twice, with two different LLM draws, and provenance keeps only the second.

Consequences:
1. R3b's training report ROWS column is 'the last generation count', not 'rows this command contributes across all contexts'. Found and documented by the R3b agent; the report is correct on single-context workflows and understates on multi-context ones.
2. R6's utterance cache probably wants the same key, for the same reason.

Not observable on either bundled example: hello_world and retail_workflow each have exactly one trainable context, because train() subtracts the internal CME IntentDetection context. It bites on a workflow shaped like IDO -- which is the shape R3b exists to serve.

Fix: add a 'context' field to UtteranceProvenance and key ProvenanceRecorder on (context, command). Then R3b sums across contexts instead of reading one record.
close_reason: Duplicate of fix-5vb (bd write-delay, fix-46c).
