title: No out-of-scope rejection: irrelevant utterances route confidently to real commands
description:
There is NO out-of-scope rejection in intent detection. Irrelevant utterances route confidently and silently to real commands. Found while verifying that the fix-551.11 root-context ruling does not regress out-of-scope handling; the verification showed the handling does not exist to begin with.

MEASURED, against the already-trained fastworkflow/examples/retail_workflow 'global'
context (20 labels, no ancestors), calling CommandRouter.predict directly:

  'book me a flight to Tokyo'               -> ROUTES to IntentDetection/what_can_i_do
  'please summarise the french revolution'  -> ROUTES to IntentDetection/reset_context
  'what is the weather in Paris'            -> ambiguous (k=3)
  'who won the world cup in 2018'           -> ambiguous (k=3)
  'tell me a joke about penguins'           -> ambiguous (k=3)
  'what is the capital of Australia'        -> ambiguous (k=3)

2 of 6 clearly out-of-domain utterances produced a SINGLE confident prediction, which
intent_detection.py:182 routes without prompting. A retail agent asked to summarise the
French revolution resets its context.

WHY: the only rejection mechanism is the ambiguity threshold in CommandRouter.predict
(model_pipeline_training.py:321-334) -- confidence above threshold returns one label and
routes; below returns topk and prompts. The trained thresholds for retail are:
  tiny_ambiguous_threshold  = 0.2395
  large_ambiguous_threshold = 0.3392
So anything clearing ~24-34% confidence executes. Those thresholds are not calibrated;
they are computed at :1174-1190 as the MEAN CONFIDENCE OF MISCLASSIFIED TEST SAMPLES,
which is a descriptive statistic of the training run, not a decision boundary.

WHAT 'wildcard' IS AND IS NOT: measurement confirms wildcard is an ESCALATION signal, not
an out-of-scope sink. In the same run it was predicted for 3 of 4 bare values ('france',
'id=3636', '/path/to/my/object') and for 0 of 6 out-of-scope prose utterances. In a
context WITH ancestors it is trained on ancestor-command utterances, which are in scope
for a parent -- also not out-of-scope. Nothing in the system is trained to recognise
"this belongs to no command anywhere".

NOT A REGRESSION FROM fix-551.11. The seven bare-value placeholders move verbatim from
wildcard to parameter_value; both are non-routable, both resolve to command_name=None,
and in a root context both terminate the parent walk at you_misunderstood. Behaviour is
identical. This issue is the pre-existing hole that ruling exposed.

POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS (needs design, do not implement blind)
  1. A genuine out-of-scope negative class trained on out-of-domain utterances, distinct
     from both wildcard (escalate) and parameter_value (bare value). This is the direct
     fix and is a natural extension of R7's label taxonomy.
  2. Calibrate the ambiguity threshold as a real operating point (e.g. chosen on the R1a
     held-out set at a target false-accept rate) instead of the mean confidence of failed
     test rows. Requires fix-551.5 to land first.
  3. A maximum-softmax-probability floor below which nothing routes regardless of the
     learned threshold, as a cheap immediate guard.

Reproduce with the probe recorded in this issue's discussion; it needs no training run,
only the committed retail artifacts.
notes:
--- DESIGN PROPOSAL DELIVERED: docs/out_of_scope_rejection_design.md (2026-08-02) ---
Design only, per instruction. No production code changed, no training run, no tests added.
All measurement read-only against the COMMITTED ___command_info artifacts for
examples/retail_workflow and examples/hello_world. Throwaway probes in /tmp/fix-d28-probe/.

RE-MEASURED AT LARGER n. In-scope set = the 72-case hand-written seed-disjoint benchmark at
docs/experiments/data/retail_intent_benchmark.json (0 seed leaks). Out-of-scope set = 50
utterances across 7 categories, 15 of them near-domain ("what are your store opening hours",
"do you price match", "is my data being sold to advertisers").

  out-of-scope routed confidently: 20/50 = 40%  95% CI [28%, 54%]
  in-scope routed confidently:     63/72 = 88%
  in-scope benchmark top-1:        45/72 = 62.5%   in-list: 51/72 = 70.8%
  out-of-scope predicted wildcard:  0/50

This issue's 2-of-6 figure generalises. The mechanism half of the issue is confirmed.

*** THE SEVERITY HALF NEEDS CORRECTING: BLAST RADIUS ***
"Routes confidently and silently to real commands" is true of the routing but not of the
consequence. Classifying the 20 confident mis-routes by what actually executes:
  12/20 -> CME meta-commands (what_can_i_do x6, what_is_current_context x3,
           reset_context x2, go_up x1). These execute immediately with NO parameter stage
           (_commands/wildcard.py:77-89) but are read-only or navigational.
   2/20 -> list_all_product_types, a zero-field Input, so it executes: a read.
   6/20 -> app commands with >=1 required field (get_user_details x2, calculate,
           modify_pending_order_payment, modify_pending_order_items,
           transfer_to_human_agents). The utterance carries no extractable value, so
           validate_parameters (utils/signatures.py:337-340) reports NOT_FOUND and the turn
           becomes a parameter prompt, NOT an execution.
ZERO of 50 out-of-scope utterances cause a state mutation. The modal outcome is
what_can_i_do (10/50 overall, 6/20 confident) -- i.e. the capability list, which is close to
the CORRECT out-of-scope response, arrived at by accident.
=> Recommend reclassifying p1 -> p2: UX / trajectory-quality defect, not a safety defect.
   The one thing that would reverse this: a workflow with a ZERO-PARAMETER MUTATING command
   reachable from a root context. Retail has none. Unsurveyed for user workflows.

*** THE DECISION-RELEVANT ANSWER: CONFIDENCE DOES NOT SEPARATE ***
AUC (P(in-scope scores higher than out-of-scope); 0.5 = chance):
  classifier max softmax prob   retail 0.788   hello_world 0.533
  classifier top1-top2 margin   retail 0.772   hello_world 0.571
  normalised entropy (smaller probe) retail 0.718  hello_world 0.495
  max cosine to seed-embedding bank  retail 0.911   hello_world 0.604
Only 15/72 in-scope cases score above the highest out-of-scope confidence (0.7152, "what is
your carbon footprint policy"). The zero-false-positive operating point on max_prob rejects
just 9/50 = 18%, barely above what the shipped 0.2395 threshold already achieves.
=> A THRESHOLD-ONLY FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE. Direction 2/3 in this issue (calibrate the
   threshold / add a max-softmax floor) is worth doing for its OWN reason -- the thresholds
   really are the mean confidence of misclassified test rows, not an operating point -- but
   it must NOT be sold as out-of-scope rejection. It buys 18%.

*** RECOMMENDATION: NOT direction 1 (negative class) FIRST ***
1. Reclassify to p2 (above).
2. Adopt the SOFT ACTION now, no detector needed: at the command_name-is-None fall-through
   in _commands/wildcard.py:109 -- already commented "# out of scope commands" -- answer
   with the capability list framed as a non-answer instead of the misunderstanding loop.
3. Prototype an OPEN-SET GATE (max cosine to a per-context seed-embedding bank) behind an
   opt-in flag defaulted OFF. Measured on retail: AUC 0.911; 26/50 = 52% detection at 1/72
   false positives; leave-one-out 1/72 = 1.4% FP with 34% detection.
   Reuses cache_matching.get_embedding, the same DistilBERT [CLS] vector cache_match already
   computes on the intent-detection hot path.

WHY NOT THE NEGATIVE CLASS (direction 1) YET -- three reasons:
  a) fix-2m5. Reserved classes compete with real commands for probability mass, and that is
     open and unfixed. A broad negative class competes harder than the 7-row
     parameter_value class does. The open-set gate adds NO class: it sits outside the
     softmax and cannot change the parameter_value/real-command balance at all.
  b) The negatives would have to be carved out of the region the CME meta-commands occupy.
     Measured: a seed bank built from the CME meta-commands ALONE gives AUC 0.348 -- BELOW
     0.5, i.e. INVERTED. Out-of-scope prose is closer to "what can you do? / now what? /
     where am I?" than genuine in-scope retail requests are. A negative class would
     cannibalise what_can_i_do, which is the command producing the best out-of-scope
     response today.
  c) The definition does not compose. In a context WITH ancestors, "out of scope" is the
     complement of the union over the whole ancestor chain, which is not knowable where the
     per-context classifier is trained. Either the label means different things in root and
     non-root contexts -- the exact defect F6/R7.1 just removed from wildcard -- or the
     decision is deferred to the end of the parent walk, at which point it is not a label.

*** WILDCARD CLAIM RE-VERIFIED AND STRENGTHENED ***
0 of 76 out-of-scope prose utterances predicted wildcard across both workflows (0/50 retail,
0/26 hello_world); 11 of 12 bare values did. spec section 11 M1/M2 holds. "Just put wildcard
back" is not an option.

*** ALSO FOUND ***
- hello_world is unusable as a test bed: 4 of its 6 non-reserved labels are CME
  meta-commands, its seed bank is 3 app utterances vs 24 meta-command ones, all 26
  out-of-scope utterances land on meta-commands, and all 3 held-out add_two_numbers
  paraphrases were predicted go_up. That last is an instance of the cross-run flakiness
  already recorded on fix-2m5, not a new defect. Acceptance measurement must use
  retail_workflow or larger.
- The fuzzy Levenshtein pre-match at intent_detection.py:166 (threshold 0.3) fired on 0 of
  95 probe utterances. Not a contributor; no proposal needs to touch it.
- FALSE-POSITIVE ASYMMETRY IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. Rejecting a valid utterance is a dead
  end; a misroute is recoverable. Forcing zero observed FP costs 18 points of detection
  (52% -> 34%), and 0/72 still leaves a rule-of-three 95% upper bound of 4.2%. So a HARD
  refusal is unshippable at any detection rate. The gate's action must be soft (answer with
  the capability list, leave the turn open), which collapses the FP cost to one wasted turn.
- Measurement must extend heldout_evaluation.py: a third BenchmarkCase kind "out_of_scope",
  score_out_of_scope(), and a false_rejection_rate over the EXISTING routing cases, reported
  as two numbers never blended (decision D2 precedent). Where the negative cases come from
  is itself a design problem -- see section 5.2 of the doc.
- CAUTION: every number above is from ONE training run against a 20.6% verdict-churn noise
  floor (spec section 2, and M4: training is not reproducible at a fixed seed). This is a
  feasibility probe, not an acceptance measurement.
- SEQUENCING: docs/experiments/data/ already holds a retail benchmark and probe sets for an
  in-flight E-PV1 parameter_value experiment. Both want to touch retail's label space and
  benchmark. Do not run them against the same artifacts concurrently.

--- CORRECTION (same session): what the ambiguous 60% actually see in a ROOT context ---
By code trace, not runtime capture. The three-option "The command is ambiguous. Please
choose..." message that intent_detection.py builds is NOT what a root-context user sees on
that turn. intent_detection returns command_name=None with error_msg set; _commands/
wildcard.py:99-124 enters the parent walk; retail's context_inheritance_model.json is empty
so is_command_context_for_response_generation_root is true and the walk body never runs;
control reaches line 111 -- already commented "# out of scope commands" -- and executes
ErrorCorrection/you_misunderstood, which prints the FULL command list ("Please select the
correct command name from the list below: ... or type 'abort' to cancel"). The stored
three-option message only surfaces on a later INTENT_MISUNDERSTANDING_CLARIFICATION turn.

Two consequences:
- The status-quo damage is lower again than the blast-radius note above already said: the
  60% non-confident out-of-scope utterances already get a capability list. What is wrong is
  the WORDING, which presupposes that one of the listed commands is what the user meant.
- The recommended "soft action" (piece 2) is therefore a wording change in
  you_misunderstood.py, not a new code path. Cheaper than scoped, and it is also exactly the
  response an armed detector would need, so building it first de-risks piece 3.

This is the one claim in the design doc that is code-trace only; a single integration test
would settle it and the doc makes that the first task under section 7.1.
VERIFIED BY THE INTEGRATOR — the one claim the design flagged as unverified (code trace, not a live transcript) holds end to end:
1. wildcard.py lines 99-121: when command_name is None after the parent walk and the stage is INTENT_DETECTION, control reaches the line already commented '# out of scope commands' and dispatches ErrorCorrection/you_misunderstood.
2. retail's context_inheritance_model.json is literally '{}', so the walk body never executes for a root context and that dispatch is reached immediately.
3. you_misunderstood.py builds the union of the CME IntentDetection commands and the current context's commands and prints all of them. So the non-confident majority already receives a FULL capability list, not the three-way ambiguity prompt.

The defect is therefore the wording, and it is precise: the response reads 'Please select the correct command name from the list below: ... or type abort to cancel'. For a genuinely out-of-scope utterance that presupposes one of the listed commands is what the user meant, which is false, and it offers abort as the only alternative. This is a single-string change in you_misunderstood.py with no new code path, and it is separable from the gate design. NOT implemented, because this issue was scoped to design only.

CAVEAT ON THE RETAIL EVIDENCE, found while verifying: the committed retail artifacts under examples/retail_workflow/___command_info contain the label wildcard 11 times and parameter_value zero times. They predate the R7.1 wildcard/parameter_value split, so the probes ran against the OLD single-overloaded-label model. This does not undermine the AUC findings, which are about the confidence distribution rather than label names, and it explains the reported '11 of 12 bare values predicted wildcard' -- under current code those should route to parameter_value. Any label-specific claim in the design doc should be re-checked against freshly trained artifacts before it is relied on.

PRIORITY LOWERED p1 -> p2 on the blast-radius evidence: 0 of 50 out-of-scope utterances cause a state mutation. 12 of the 20 confident mis-routes land on read-only CME meta-commands, 2 on a zero-field catalogue read, and 6 are stopped at the parameter-extraction prompt because the utterance carries no extractable value. The modal outcome is what_can_i_do, i.e. the capability list -- close to the correct out-of-scope response, arrived at by accident. This is a UX defect, not a safety one. The one thing that reverses this judgement is a zero-parameter MUTATING command reachable from a root context; retail has none, user workflows are unsurveyed.
WORDING FIX SHIPPED (approved 2026-08-02). ErrorCorrection/you_misunderstood no longer says 'Please select the correct command', which falsely presupposed that an out-of-scope request matched one listed command. It now says the framework could not determine a match, asks the user to enter a command name only if one applies, and explicitly offers rephrasing or aborting. No routing or detector behavior changed. Added tests/test_you_misunderstood_command.py using the real todo_list workflow and CME child workflow; it asserts neutral wording, the old presupposition is absent, and every structured valid_command_name remains visible. Targeted test: 1 passed. The broader fix-d28 remains open because this is a soft fallback UX improvement, not out-of-scope detection.
--- 2026-08-02 CURRENT-TREE CORRECTION + MEASUREMENT SLICE ---
A targeted runtime audit found that the design proposal was not implementation-ready. The proposed gate at wildcard.py's end-of-parent-walk fall-through cannot see the measured 40% confident misroutes: a single classifier label skips the walk and reaches immediate CME execution or parameter extraction. A live isolated retail turn also disproved the document's §1.3 trace: 'what is the weather in Paris' returned the ambiguity error immediately with stage INTENT_AMBIGUITY_CLARIFICATION; it did not reach you_misunderstood on the first turn.

Appended Amendment A1 to docs/out_of_scope_rejection_design.md. The corrected minimal future contract validates only a lone ROUTABLE classifier commitment inside INTENT_DETECTION before assigning command_name. Rejection leaves command_name unset so the existing parent walk tries each ancestor; exact/fuzzy/user-correction-cache routes, top-k ambiguity, wildcard/parameter_value, and PARAMETER_EXTRACTION remain outside the first slice. This catches the measured mechanism without reordering wildcard.py or suppressing escalation.

Runtime arming is intentionally NOT implemented: current evidence is 72 routing + 50 OOS cases, committed retail artifacts predate the R7.1 label split, no second realistic workflow generalises the result, and no paired post-split replicate exists. These do not meet the design's >=200 routing / >=100 OOS / two-run acceptance bar.

Implemented measurement plumbing only:
- BenchmarkCase supports kind='out_of_scope' with required category/near_domain metadata.
- Added score_out_of_scope and score_false_rejection as separate metrics, plus structural validation that explicitly does not pretend command metadata can prove semantic out-of-scope status.
- Added docs/experiments/data/retail_out_of_scope_benchmark.json containing the exact 50 feasibility cases (15/50 near-domain), explicitly marked below acceptance size/mix.
- Updated docs/intent_benchmark_format.md and integration tests.

Fresh read-only replication against the exact new 50-case file and 72 routing cases matched the prior probe: baseline confident OOS routes 20/50 (40%, Wilson 95% CI 28-54%); seed-bank AUC 0.911; at t=0.5715, detection 17/50 (34%, CI 22-48%) with 0/72 observed false rejections; at t=0.6146, detection 26/50 (52%, CI 39-65%) with 1/72 false rejection. This remains feasibility evidence only.

Verification: benchmark loader reports 50 cases / 15 near-domain; targeted pytest tests/test_heldout_evaluation.py tests/test_you_misunderstood_command.py: 50 passed. Full suite launched separately.
Verification completed after the measurement-report fields were added: full local suite passed 999 passed, 13 skipped, 58 warnings in 926.41s (0 failures). Targeted out-of-scope evaluator + fallback tests remained 50 passed.
--- 2026-08-02 ADVERSARIAL FOLLOW-UP (A2): OPTION C NO-GO ---
Independent adversarial review confirmed the no-go and found additional evidence defects beyond A1:
- The measured model directories are gitignored local legacy artifacts, not committed or reconstructible from 23dbe35. The exact weights/training inputs have no manifest.
- R7.1 can change AUC because the candidate vectors come from the fine-tuned DistilBERT body; pre-split AUC is not invariant to a label-space retrain.
- The probe's 117-row bank is specifically literal plain_utterances, not the full training manifold.
- Candidate thresholds were fitted and reported on the same 72/50 cases; leave-one-out reused all negatives. Acceptance needs disjoint calibration and locked evaluation corpora, k>=5 paired versioned builds, and application/CME plus near/far strata.
- CommandRouter-only scoring cannot prove the final runtime response. The next detector-related slice must be shadow-only at the full runtime path, recording route origin, contexts visited, similarities, actual command/stage/response, and latency without changing routing.
- A direct rephrase in INTENT_MISUNDERSTANDING_CLARIFICATION does not rerun classification; it defaults to what_can_i_do. The fallback had advertised a recovery path that does not exist.

Appended design Amendment A2, which supersedes A1's next-step recommendation and requires runtime shadow evidence on fresh immutable post-split artifacts before any gate decision. Updated benchmark docs accordingly.

Corrected the fallback affordance to the behavior the state machine really supports: "type 'abort' to cancel, then rephrase your request." Extended the real-workflow integration test to prove abort resets NLU_Pipeline_Stage from INTENT_MISUNDERSTANDING_CLARIFICATION to INTENT_DETECTION, so the following turn can actually be reclassified. Verification after this correction: targeted fallback test 1 passed; no new linter diagnostics. The earlier evaluator+fallback run remains 50 passed and the full pre-A2 regression run was 999 passed / 13 skipped / 0 failed.
--- 2026-08-02 AMENDMENT A3: PROOF-CARRYING SELECTIVE EXECUTION ---
Updated docs/out_of_scope_rejection_design.md with Amendment A3 based on the outside-the-box review. The issue explicitly remains OPEN; no satisfactory detector or enforcing gate exists.

A3 records fresh read-only evidence that variants of the current embedding gate are inadequate on confident commitments: global cosine AUC 0.902 and predicted-command cosine AUC 0.885 both catch only 4/20 confident OOS routes at zero observed false rejection; nearest-seed/classifier disagreement catches 7/20 but falsely rejects 7/63 valid commitments; similarity margin AUC is 0.793. The current fine-tuned-CLS/plain-utterance gate is retired as the presumptive solution and retained only as a baseline.

The new candidate direction reframes routing as proof-carrying selective execution: a classifier proposes; a separate frozen pairwise verifier evaluates an utterance against a versioned command capability card; conformal calibration controls marginal false abstention narrowly; deterministic risk policy requires confirmation for implicit navigation/write/external/unknown-effect routes; CME control-plane intents are evaluated separately; negative corrections can veto repeated wrong mappings; and outlier exposure is a separate ablation without a competing OOS label.

A3 defines capability-card contents, feedback invalidation/privacy requirements, a shadow-only experiment ladder with disjoint train/calibration/locked-eval data and k>=5 paired builds, runtime/recovery/latency metrics, and explicit kill criteria. The risk firewall and semantic verifier must be measured separately. If no semantic candidate clears the bar, the honest partial solution is the deterministic risk firewall plus neutral fallback, not a weak detector.

title: AR6: R7.2's Exception wildcard-share figures do not reconcile — do not cite
description:
FOUND BY the adversarial review (bd fix-551.1, finding AR6).

The spec's R7.2 and the bd issue fix-551.12 both quote a measured effect on the IDO workflow's 'Exception' context: 2352 ancestor utterances -> 170, an 88% -> 27% wildcard share. Those numbers do not reconcile with F8's 'Exception' row (42 own rows / 312 wildcard / 88%) under any single definition of 'row':

- 88% before implies roughly 321 own rows
- 27% after implies roughly 460 own rows
- seeds/command did not change between the two runs, so own rows cannot have grown

At least one of the three figures is computed over a different denominator (deduplicated vs raw, pre- vs post-subtraction of the context's own utterances at model_pipeline_training.py:872-873, or per-context vs per-run).

ACTION: treat the '2352 -> 170' and '88% -> 27%' figures as NOT CITABLE until re-derived from the raw run data with the denominator stated. The COVERAGE claim in the same sentence — that all 33 ancestor intents remained represented — is unaffected and stands, since it is a count of distinct labels rather than a share.

This does not block implementing R7.2 (fix-551.12), whose justification is the 44% training-time reduction (D3), not these figures. It blocks quoting them in any doc or commit message.
notes: RESOLVED BY EXPLICIT RETRACTION, not guessed correction. F8's 42 own / 312 wildcard / 88% is internally consistent. R7.2's 2352->170 and 88%->27% cannot share one denominator: rounded 88% implies 306-336 own rows; rounded 27% implies 449-471, no overlap. With F8's 42 own rows, 170 wildcard rows is 80.2%, not 27%. Current/pinned code exposes raw ancestor rows, deduplicated wildcard-label rows, budget-selected rows and local tuples, so denominator mixing plausibly explains 2352/312/170 but not 27%. No IDO workflow, train_ido.py, report or artifacts remain to recover the original denominator. docs/intent_training_improvements_spec.md now retracts all Exception transformations and the unreproducible count of 33 while retaining the algorithmic round-robin coverage guarantee. Deterministic reproducer and output: .fix-lfz-results/. Confidence 99% mathematical incompatibility, 95% evidence unrecoverable.

title: F13: tell developers that seed count is the dominant input
description:
ADDRESSES F13 (S2). The IDO curve, holding everything else constant:

  3.2 seeds/command -> 46.2% routing top-1
  8.0 seeds/command -> 70.4%
  9.3 seeds/command -> 73.8%

Seed count is the single largest lever measured in this entire exercise — larger than the wildcard cap, larger than anything in the training loop. NOTHING in the docs or the training output tells a developer that this is where their effort belongs, or that returns flatten past roughly eight seeds.

DO:
- Surface the guidance in the training output itself (the R3b per-command table is the natural place: a command with 3 seeds should be visibly flagged).
- Document it wherever plain_utterances / seed authoring is explained.
- State the flattening point (~8 seeds) as an observation from one workflow, not a universal constant — the curve came from IDO alone.

DEPENDS ON R3b, which creates the per-command surface this guidance attaches to.

DOCS DISCIPLINE: consult the fastworkflow-docs-and-positioning skill before editing README/CLAUDE.md — there are authoritative-doc rules and a known doc-rot hazard in this repo.
notes: F13 SHIPPED. The convergence skill now names hand-written seed utterances per command (Signature.plain_utterances) as the DOMINANT input to intent-detection quality, ranked above the generation dials developers were previously left to guess at.
close_reason: Shipped and integrated; see notes

title: R9a: allow app-supplied or domain-conditioned personas
description:
ADDRESSES F12 (S3). Personas are drawn at random from PersonaHub with no conditioning on the application domain (generate_synthetic.py:43). For an identity-governance workflow, most sampled personas have no relationship to the vocabulary users actually employ.

The spec's assessment: allowing an app-supplied persona set is PLAUSIBLY A LARGER GENERALISATION LEVER THAN ANYTHING IN THE TRAINING LOOP. That is a hypothesis, not a result — it has not been measured, and it must be tested against the R1 benchmark with a paired test like every other accuracy claim in this epic.

DO (spec R9): allow an app-supplied persona list or domain conditioning.

INTERACTS WITH R2 and R6: persona IDs are part of the provenance record and part of the utterance-cache fingerprint, so an app-supplied set must flow through both.
notes:
R9a INTEGRATED into generate_synthetic.py: personas.json (or SYNTHETIC_UTTERANCE_GEN_PERSONA_FILE) discovered per workflow; resolve_personas replaces the direct select_persona_indices call; the datasets-availability guard now also consults persona_source_needs_corpus, so an app-supplied persona set needs neither the PersonaHub download nor the optional dependency; the cache fingerprint gains a persona label that is None for the default draw, so no existing workflow's cached utterances were invalidated by this landing.

One correction applied during integration. The delivered patch set provenance.generator_config['persona_source'] on the generation path, which sits AFTER the R6 cache lookup. A cache hit returns early, so the field was present on a run that generated and absent on a run that reused, and two runs at the same seed produced different provenance -- defeating the byte-comparison R6 exists to enable. Caught by test_provenance_is_byte_identical. Now recorded before the cache is consulted, via a new corpus-free personas.active_persona_source_name(), which is deliberately distinct from active_persona_source_label(): the label is a cache key (absent for the default draw, changes with persona CONTENT), the name is a run description (always present, does NOT change with content).

NOT MEASURED, and deliberately so: no effect of domain-conditioned personas is claimed. The persona holdout that R1 scores is generated BY the persona source under test, so the two arms are not scored on the same instrument and no number of repeats fixes that confound. Establishing an effect needs a fixed hand-authored intent_benchmark.json on a real-domain workflow; the delivered power analysis puts a +5pp effect at 18 paired runs.
R9a SHIPPED. Personas can now come from an app-supplied personas.json or a domain-conditioned source instead of the default PersonaHub draw, resolved through resolve_personas(). Integrated into generate_synthetic.py in five places. Two non-obvious parts: the persona label is in the R6 cache fingerprint, so a workflow that adds a personas.json stops being served utterances written by the generic personas it just replaced; and the `datasets` availability guard consults persona_source_needs_corpus(), so an app-supplied persona set requires neither the PersonaHub download nor the optional dependency. Fixed my own integration defect here: persona_source was written to provenance only on the generation path, so a cache HIT omitted it and broke byte-identity -- now written before the cache branch.
close_reason: Shipped and integrated; see notes

title: R8: re-point the convergence skill at in-package evaluation once R1 lands
description:
ADDRESSES R8 (decision D7). The skill ALREADY EXISTS at .claude/skills/fastworkflow-intent-training-convergence/SKILL.md, written against the app-side IDO harness because the package offered nothing to measure with. This issue is the follow-up: once R1 ships in-package held-out evaluation and R4 ships versioned artifacts, the skill must point at package commands instead of the external harness.

WHY A SKILL AND NOT A CLI FLAG (D7): the loop is a judgement-bearing protocol — estimate the noise floor, increase sample size, test paired, decide whether to continue — and it composes with the existing house methodology skills rather than duplicating them. A CLI subcommand would hard-code statistical policy. Rejected accordingly.

THE SKILL MUST (spec R8): establish the noise floor by REPEATED IDENTICAL RUNS before attributing anything to a change; grow utterance sample size progressively; test paired with exact McNemar; and stop when the per-step gain drops below the floor. It defers all statistics conventions to the fastworkflow-proof-and-analysis-toolkit skill.

DO HERE:
- Replace references to the external harness (tests/eval_intent_benchmark.py, tests/compare_runs.py) with the in-package equivalents from R1 and R4.
- Verify the ~20.6% churn figure still holds AFTER R2 seeds the pipeline — determinism should collapse the floor substantially, and the skill's central number becomes wrong if it does. Re-measure rather than assuming either way.

DEPENDS ON R1b (the metric the loop reads) and R4 (paired scoring of two versions on identical cases).
notes: R8 SHIPPED. The convergence skill is re-pointed at in-package evaluation: heldout_evaluation.py running automatically at the end of `fastworkflow train` and writing ___command_info/heldout_evaluation.json, replacing the app-side tests/eval_intent_benchmark.py it used to send developers to. Refreshed again at the end of wave 3, because the skill had accumulated stale warnings that were now actively misleading -- it still told readers the benchmark validators never run (fixed, fix-eia), that utterance reuse was 'built but switched off' (now installed by train_workflow), and that four modules had no call site (three now do). Replaced the prose warning with a wired/not-wired table, and added the two traps a table cannot express: a module-level handle can be imported without ever being installed, and the determinism suites install those handles themselves so they pass either way.

title: R7.3: class weighting for imbalanced per-context label spaces
description:
ADDRESSES F9 (S3). Independent of `wildcard`: per-context label spaces range from 4 to 23 commands on IDO, and the loss is unweighted with no sampler.

Capping the ancestor class (R7.2) is a blunt special case of this general fix. Class weighting subsumes it and additionally handles imbalance AMONG REAL COMMANDS, which capping does nothing for.

DEPENDS ON R7.2 — implement the cap first (it is the measured, cost-justified change), then generalise, so the two effects can be attributed separately.

ACCEPTANCE: both axes measured (R1) plus a paired test. Same bar as R7.2.
notes:
NOT STARTED (wave 2). Note previously recorded here was lost to a concurrent-bd-writer race during the parallel wave; the authoritative record is docs/intent_training_improvements_spec.md (F9 for the finding, R7.3 for the requirement, sec.10 for the review findings that touched it). Pointing at the spec rather than re-copying, so the two cannot drift.

Sequencing: class weighting must be decided AFTER fix-551.11 (wildcard split) and fix-551.12 (cap), because both change the per-context class balance this issue is meant to correct. Weighting a distribution that is about to change would be measuring the wrong thing.

--- WAVE 2 MEASUREMENT: NEGATIVE RESULT. RECOMMENDATION IS NOT TO SHIP. ---
(agent, 2026-08-02)

AR8 flagged that this issue rests on a structural fact (no weighting exists) with no
measured accuracy benefit, and would read more honestly with an explicit exploratory
disclaimer. It has now been measured, and the answer is that class weighting does
nothing here.

PROTOCOL: tests/measure_class_balance.py. examples/hello_world, 10 TRAINING_SEED
values x 6 configurations = 60 trainings. Every configuration at a seed trains on
BYTE-IDENTICAL utterances (the harness caches _get_utterances to disk and replays it),
which removes the M4 confound and makes the comparison genuinely paired. 12 probes per
run (the 4 from fix-2m5 plus 8 further phrasings) and 7 HELD-OUT bare values -- held
out on purpose: probing with the seven training literals measures memorisation, and
any config that removes a literal scores zero on it by construction.
The whole 60-run sweep was repeated end to end and reproduced CELL FOR CELL.

RESULT -- paired exact McNemar against the unweighted control:

  config          axis            fixed broken     p
  balanced        fix-2m5 probes      1      1  1.000
  balanced        all routing         3      5  0.727
  balanced        bare-value          2      6  0.289
  balanced_real   fix-2m5 probes      1      3  0.625
  balanced_real   all routing         2      8  0.109
  balanced_real   bare-value          0      7  0.016
  reserved w=0.5  fix-2m5 probes      1      1  1.000
  reserved w=0.5  all routing         1      4  0.375
  reserved w=0.5  bare-value          3      4  1.000
  reserved w=0.25 fix-2m5 probes      1      3  0.625
  reserved w=0.25 all routing         1      8  0.039
  reserved w=0.25 bare-value          2      2  1.000

NO configuration improved ANY axis. The only two nominally significant results are
REGRESSIONS, and neither survives Holm correction across the twelve comparisons
(0.016 x 12 = 0.19). Totals: control 33/40 on the fix-2m5 probes, 42/80 extra,
57/70 bare-value; no weighted config beat it on more than one axis at a time.

Note the DIRECTION textbook balancing pushes: parameter_value is the SMALLEST class
in this label space (7 rows against 24-39), so sklearn-style inverse-frequency
weighting up-weights by 3.67x the class that is already out-competing the real
commands. 'balanced' is not a safe default here.

Also notable: multiplying the reserved class's loss weight over a 15x range
(3.67x under 'balanced' down to 0.25x) produced no distinguishable difference, while
removing rows from the same class produced p = 0.001. Whatever governs this decision
boundary, it is not the class's loss weight.

SHIPPED AS: fastworkflow/train/class_balance.py implements 'none' (default,
byte-identical to today), 'balanced', 'balanced_real', and an orthogonal
RESERVED_CLASS_WEIGHT multiplier, plus class_weight_tensor/weighted_cross_entropy.
The code exists so the next person can re-test rather than re-litigate.
RECOMMENDATION: do not integrate the loss-weighting hook into the trainer's two
training loops. An off-by-default hook is still two seams in a hot loop for zero
measured benefit. The integration patch marks it optional and advises against it.
R7.3 MEASURED AND NOT SHIPPED — negative result. Three weighting schemes (none / balanced / balanced_real) crossed with a reserved-class weight multiplier, 5 seeds each, PAIRED on byte-identical training data (only possible because R6's utterance cache landed first; without it section 11's 0/5 reproducibility finding would swamp the comparison). Routing 41/60 vs 40/60 vs 39/60; bare-value catch 43/50 vs 44/50 vs 43/50. Exact McNemar on the paired verdicts: p = 0.72, 1.00, 0.51. Indistinguishable from noise on both axes, and smaller than the ~20% verdict churn.

The weighting computation stays in fastworkflow/train/class_balance.py, tested down to the gradient level (down-weighting a class demonstrably shrinks its share of the gradient), so a future workflow with genuinely severe imbalance can turn it on. It is simply not enabled by default, because there is no evidence it helps.

Bound on the claim, stated honestly: ~60 routing verdicts per config rules out a LARGE effect, not a small one. A tighter bound needs an evaluation set well beyond 38 samples, which is a bigger job than this issue.

title: Step 2 integration tests: long turn recoverable via polling + saturation
description: Integration tests building on the long-running command harness from fix-85g.8. Assert: (1) a long turn (sleep >> wait_seconds) is fully recoverable via repeated GET /turns/{turn_key} across many polls until exec_state=DONE with the correct result; (2) streaming and polling read the SAME record (non-destructive buffer); (3) GET /turns auth scoping rejects a turn_key not owned by the JWT; (4) saturation returns 429 rather than hanging/exhausting threads; (5) terminal results are TTL-evicted (registry does not grow unbounded).

title: Step 2: sized executor + global backpressure (429) + TTL eviction of terminal executions
description: Step 2. (a) Dedicated sized executor (loop.set_default_executor or a private pool) separate from the default pool so turns do not exhaust threads. (b) Global semaphore/queue bounding concurrency across channels (per-channel single-flight only bounds to active-channel count — §7.8); return 429/queued when saturated rather than exhausting threads. (c) TTL eviction of terminal DONE/LOST registry entries (TurnRegistry.evict_terminal) so the registry does not grow unbounded.

title: Step 2: non-destructive per-execution trace replay buffer

Replace the destructive get_nowait trace drain (utils.py:487/507/532/538/566) with a per-execution trace replay buffer that supports read-by-offset, so a poller (GET /turns) and a streamer (GET /turns/{turn_key}/events, SSE/NDJSON) can BOTH read the same record without consuming it. _run_turn appends to this buffer.

title: Step 2: GET /turns/{turn_key} (auth-scoped) + real 202 deferred responses
description: §5.2 + Step 2. Add GET /turns/{turn_key} -> 200 {turn_key, exec_state, status?, result?, error?, traces?}. Transport 200 = 'execution state read successfully'; the turn OUTCOME lives in TurnStatus — do NOT map a failed turn to HTTP 5xx. Make the deferred path return a real 202 {turn_key, exec_state:'running'} (200 = finished in window). Auth scoping: GET /turns/{turn_key} MUST verify the JWT channel/user owns turn_key (key is unguessable but must not be sole authz). MCP exposure decision per §5.3 is resolved here (deferred item 4).

title: Full test suite wipes example workflows' trained ___command_info (breaks FastAPI service tests)
description:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED. The module-scoped fixture trained_hello_world in tests/test_train_modern_stack.py operates on the REAL example dir (HELLO_WORLD_PATH = fastworkflow/examples/hello_world) and calls _cleanup() which runs shutil.rmtree(<workflow>/___command_info) at BOTH fixture setup (line ~124) and teardown (line ~131). It only skips (leaving artifacts intact) when datasets is missing OR no real LITELLM_API_KEY_SYNDATA_GEN is available; in local dev both are present (datasets installed + real keys overlaid from ./env/.env + ./passwords/.env via _resolve_env_vars), so the fixture ACTIVATES and wipes the real example's trained ___command_info. ORDERING: in a full run, test_fastapi_service.py (f) runs before test_train_modern_stack.py (t), so the 4 model-dependent FastAPI tests pass in the SAME run, but test_train_modern_stack's TEARDOWN deletes ___command_info at the end -> the NEXT full-suite run finds threshold.json gone and those 4 fail (FileNotFoundError: .../___command_info/global/threshold.json). This matches observed behavior across the v2.21.5 run (4 passed, model wiped at teardown) and the v2.21.6 run (4 failed, model already gone). 

The 4 affected tests: test_initialize_with_startup_command_in_request, test_invoke_assistant_endpoint, test_session_not_found_errors, test_concurrent_request_handling. They implicitly depend on a pre-trained real example, while test_train_modern_stack assumes it may freely delete it -> hidden inter-test dependency. 

RECOMMENDED FIX (preferred): make test_train_modern_stack train into a TEMP COPY (shutil.copytree(hello_world, tmp_path) then train_workflow(tmp) and assert there); never rmtree the real example. Alternatives: (b) give the model-dependent FastAPI tests a fixture that trains-or-skips instead of assuming a pre-trained example; (c) back up & restore ___command_info around the fixture. 

HOW TO TRAIN hello_world WITHOUT ERRORS (for local test/verify): use the launch.json train_hello_world paths -> 'fastworkflow train ./fastworkflow/examples/hello_world ./env/.env ./passwords/.env'. The repo-local ./passwords/.env has valid keys; the BUNDLED fastworkflow/examples/fastworkflow.passwords.env has a dead/placeholder Mistral key (causes litellm AuthenticationError Unauthorized). Verified: training restores ___command_info/global/threshold.json and the 4 FastAPI tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed: test_train_modern_stack.trained_hello_world now trains into an isolated temp copy (tmp_path_factory + shutil.copytree, excluding generated dirs) instead of the real fastworkflow/examples/hello_world, so _cleanup()'s rmtree(___command_info) no longer destroys the trained model other tests depend on. Verified: full suite 478 passed / 0 failed (previously 4 test_fastapi_service.py failures), and the real example's ___command_info/global/threshold.json survives a full run -> suite is now idempotent.

description: Code-reading evidence (found during turn-result review R43, 2026-06-11): Topology A blocking ask_user (workflow_agent.py:279) puts the clarification CommandOutput on command_output_queue but emits NO trace sentinel - the only sentinel emitter is _maybe_enqueue_trace_sentinel (workflow_execution_context.py:436), called only at the four turn-END sites. title: R46: Decide the release train (staged vs big-bang) and upgrade-time behavior
description:
FINDING: the design couples three independently-shippable changes - the capture/TurnResult bug fix, the durable review feature, and the command_responses collapse - into one breaking release; only the collapse is intrinsically breaking. Decision 22 also leaves runtime behavior on old pending blobs unspecified (in-flight suspended sessions exist at every deploy). OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) adopt the staged train (stage 1 minor: TurnResult + shim, fixes the xray bug; stage 2 minor: stores behind config + R37 consolidation; stage 3 major: remove command_responses and action_log) vs single major release; (2) confirm graceful degradation on SCHEMA_VERSION mismatch (treat pending as expired, clear, notify user) instead of an exception. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R46.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) TRAIN = QUICK-FIX MINOR + ONE MAJOR. The originally sketched three-stage train was retired during review: A1's accept-loss consolidation means the store work deletes user-visible conversation history, which must not hide inside a minor. ~v2.21 (minor, non-breaking): TurnResult type, capture machinery (ask_user per A7, failure capture per A5), NEW process_turn() method returning TurnResult, A13 constructor shim introduced with DeprecationWarnings (clock starts early); process_message unchanged; xray switches its runner to process_turn() - THE ORIGINAL PAYLOAD BUG IS FIXED HERE. v3.0 (major): process_message returns TurnResult (A3 awaiting_user-artifact removal lands with it), wire hard-break (A13), ConversationTurnStore consolidation with announced data loss (A1), action_log retired, command_responses removed from the model surface while the shim still accepts the legacy keyword. v4.0: shim removed (A13 window pinned: introduced 2.21, removed 4.0). (2) UPGRADE DAY = GRACEFUL EXPIRY: pending blob with old SCHEMA_VERSION is cleared on first touch; user told 'your previous question expired, please re-ask'; no record synthesized (old blob unreadable by definition). Migration guide documents this + optional pre-upgrade drain recommendation. Recorded in design doc Amendment A14 and review doc R46.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 renovation/move-out-weekend with updated map): quick-fix-minor+major and graceful expiry, both recommended options. Key reframing: three-stage retired because A1 data loss belongs in a major. R3's deprecation window now concretely pinned.
close_reason: Finding finalized: quick-fix minor (process_turn + shim) then one major, shim removed at v4.0; graceful expiry for old pending blobs; recorded in bead, review doc R46, design doc Amendment A14

title: R41: Disambiguate the live response path (in-memory payloads vs store handles)
description:

One reading pays put-then-get per turn for bytes already in memory; the other (inline from memory) makes the lazily-by-handle language wrong and balloons bundled-server model_dump responses with all gallery payloads. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) live path maps from the in-memory TurnResult with handles reserved for the review reader (recommended), or serve live from handles for response-size control; (2) per-response payload size cap for the bundled server JSON/SSE bodies. Interacts with R45 eager offload. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R41.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) LIVE RESPONSE SERVED FROM RAM: the runner/mapping reads payloads from the in-memory TurnResult; offload happens on a serialized COPY at the persistence boundary (R10 copy-on-serialize), purely for review. Zero store reads on the hot path. Section 10.3's fetching-lazily-by-handle language corrected to apply ONLY to the review reader, never the live path. (2) BUNDLED-SERVER RESPONSES: payloads inline up to a configurable cap (MAX_INLINE_PAYLOAD, generous default ~10MB); above the cap the response carries the A10 envelope marked not-inlined-available-via-review-record (path depends on the future R32 read API, documented as such). (3) R45 CONSEQUENCE (noted here, finalized there): with the live path pinned to RAM, payloads must stay in memory until the response is built - eager offload buys no memory relief, so R45 collapses to boundary-offload with a documented memory profile. Recorded in design doc Amendment A16 and review doc R41.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 kitchen/warehouse with explicit R45 coupling): serve-from-RAM + configurable cap, both recommended options. R45 (fix-vof.43) is now mostly determined.
close_reason: Finding finalized: live path serves from RAM, configurable inline cap, handles are review-only; recorded in bead, review doc R41, design doc Amendment A16

title: R43: Define the command_output_queue / CLI contract after the redesign
description:
FINDING: the queue transport has its own contract the design never updates: _finalize_agent_output, _process_message and _process_action all enqueue the final CommandOutput; Topology A enqueues mid-turn clarifications directly; the CLI (run/__main__.py) consumes the queue and iterates command_responses. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) queue carries per-event CommandOutputs plus a terminal TurnResult (recommended - mirrors live-then-final), or TurnResult only; (2) enumerate ChatSession.keep_alive and CLI renderer changes in section 11. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R43.
