title: R38: Give /post_feedback a home compatible with write-once review records
description:
FINDING: /post_feedback (run_fastapi_mcp/__main__.py:1276-1316) mutates the last in-memory conversation turn AFTER completion - after the write-once review record is sealed. Feedback is first-order observability data and the design never mentions it. OPEN QUESTIONS: choose (a) mutable feedback field on review records (violates write-once); (b) separate feedback keyspace keyed by turn_key (recommended); (c) feedback stays in ConversationStore with a turn_key link (fits R37 consolidation). See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R38.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar) - SEPARATE FEEDBACK RECORDS. Feedback is its own small record type in the unified keyspace: fw:feedback:{channel}:{conv_id}:{turn_key} holding score, comment, timestamp. (1) Turn records stay STRICTLY write-once - R16 enforcement and audit immutability hold with no carve-outs. (2) Same prefix scans serve everything: review reader and A1 memory rebuild fetch turns + feedback cards in one conversation-prefix scan; A8/A12 retention deletes cards with their envelopes automatically. (3) Conventions matching today: re-posting overwrites (last-write-wins on the single feedback key); /post_feedback targets the latest completed turn of the active conversation (arbitrary-turn feedback = future R32 read-API territory); feedback enters the agent-memory projection for completed turns exactly as the dspy.History feedback slot does today (A1 projection constraint satisfied via the read-time join). Recorded in design doc Amendment A18 and review doc R38.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 sealed-envelopes/sticky-notes): separate feedback records, recommended option. Original option (c) (ConversationStore home) was dead post-A1; its spirit maps to this resolution within the unified store.
close_reason: Finding finalized: separate feedback records in the unified keyspace, turn records stay write-once; recorded in bead, review doc R38, design doc Amendment A18

title: R39: Model cancelled turns (/cancel_pending)
description:
FINDING: /cancel_pending (run_fastapi_mcp/__main__.py:1133-1160) abandons a suspended ask_user turn and clears pending state - a fourth terminal state the design does not model. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) do cancelled turns write a review record with status=cancelled carrying the partial event sequence (recommended - it is real history); (2) who cleans up payloads offloaded at the suspend boundary, now referenced by nothing (ties to R24). Depends on the R11 status enum. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R39.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-10 (with Dhar). (1) RECORD, NOT SHRED: /cancel_pending and the A2 auto-cancel-on-switch paths write a turn record with status=cancelled under the turn's ORIGINAL conversation, carrying the partial event sequence (commands executed so far + the unanswered clarification question; event shape per R1) and the payload handles already offloaded at suspend. Payload ownership transfers from the pending blob to the cancelled record - no cleanup step needed; R24's orphan concern dissolves for the cancel path (abandoned path remains with R6.3). Sequence under per-session lock: serialize partial TurnResult (status=cancelled) -> write record -> clear pending blob. Today's cancel_pending() (workflow_execution_context.py:289) only resets in-memory state; it gains the record write. (2) R7 interplay: if review persistence is disabled by config, cancel falls back to shredding, and only that mode performs an explicit suspend-payload delete. (3) AGENT-MEMORY PROJECTION RULE (clarifies A1.2): rebuilt dspy.History projects from status=completed records ONLY; cancelled/failed/abandoned records are review-only and never enter agent working memory - matches today's behavior. Recorded in design doc Amendment A4 and review doc R39.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5): record vs shred = record (with R7 config fallback); memory projection = completed only. Cross-refs: R1 (unanswered-question event shape), R24 (cancel-path orphans dissolved), R6.3 (abandoned path still open), R7 (config switch).
close_reason: Finding finalized: cancelled turns recorded under original conversation; completed-only memory projection; recorded in bead, review doc R39, design doc Amendment A4

title: R10: Answer aliasing - copy-on-serialize rule and headline/gallery dedup
description:
FINDING: in the deterministic path answer IS command_outputs[-1].command_response (same object). In-place offload would corrupt the live TurnResult through both aliases; and the xray mapping would render the same payload twice (headline source and gallery entry). Blind deepcopy is also wrong - artifacts can hold live app objects and command_parameters holds a Pydantic model. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) confirm selective-copy serializer rule (no in-place mutation, no blind deepcopy); (2) confirm mapping dedup rule (skip gallery entries whose command_response is the answer object). See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R10.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) SELECTIVE COPY-ON-SERIALIZE (stated; implied by A10/A16): the serializer never mutates live TurnResult/CommandOutput objects and never blind-deep-copies them (artifacts can hold live application objects; command_parameters holds a typed model). It builds a new structure - small fields copied, values converted per A10's contract (threshold offload to envelope, model_dump for parameters, strict rejection otherwise) - originals untouched. A16's pristine-in-RAM live path depends on this. (2) HEADLINE NEVER CARRIES PAYLOADS (supersedes the reviewer's earlier identity-skip suggestion): the headline ResponseTuple is always narrative text + metadata; the gallery always contains ALL payload-bearing outputs in turn order. One uniform invariant across agent/assistant/action turns; the faithful reading of decision 21 (the UI, not the framework, picks the featured payload); deterministic-turn duplication eliminated by construction. Recorded in design doc Amendment A20 and review doc R10.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 one-object-two-names): headline-never-carries-payloads chosen - the reviewer's own recommendation updated mid-pass from identity-skip after testing it against decision 21's UI-decides intent.
close_reason: Finding finalized: selective copy-on-serialize, headline never carries payloads; recorded in bead, review doc R10, design doc Amendment A20

title: R11: Introduce first-class TurnResult.status (replace awaiting_user artifact sniffing)
description:
FINDING: suspension is signaled today by artifacts[awaiting_user]=True set in _awaiting_user_output (workflow_execution_context.py:518-520) and sniffed by the runner and utils.py:355-357 - a stringly-typed protocol. The redesign is the moment to replace it. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) confirm TurnStatus enum: completed, awaiting_user, failed, cancelled, abandoned; (2) confirm it replaces _output_is_awaiting_user and the runner branch condition; (3) scope - does the artifacts protocol get removed in the same release. Gates R6, R39, R40. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R11.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-10 (with Dhar). (1) TurnResult.status: TurnStatus enum with ALL FIVE values: completed, awaiting_user, failed, cancelled, abandoned. cancelled is required by R9 auto-cancel-on-switch; abandoned is reserved now (written only if the R6.3 stale-pending sweep is built) so readers never need a schema bump. (2) The artifacts[awaiting_user] protocol is REMOVED IMMEDIATELY in the release that introduces TurnResult - no dual-publish window. _awaiting_user_output stops stamping the artifact; _output_is_awaiting_user sniffing (utils.py:354-357, xray runner) is deleted; the branch becomes turn.status == AWAITING_USER. Contained because every consumer of the old signal is in-repo or user-owned and is being rewritten for the TurnResult return type in the same release anyway; does not by itself force a big-bang release in R46. (3) NO FURTHER CLEANUP (user decision): all four CommandOutput predicates and the NLU-internal artifact handshake (command_handled / command_name / cmd_parameters between wildcard.py and CommandExecutor) carry into the redesigned model unchanged per design section 5.2. For the record: command_aborted and not_what_i_meant were verified to have zero consumers in framework+tests (definitions only, __init__.py:78,86); retained deliberately as public API. Formalizing the handshake is possible future work, out of scope. Recorded in design doc Amendment A3 and review doc R11.
notes: Q and A: enum = all five; artifact removal = immediate (user chose against dual-publish recommendation); cleanup scope = none (user chose conservative option after ELI5 of the sticky-note protocol and the dead-predicate evidence). Unblocks R6 (fix-vof.8), R39 (fix-vof.16), R40 (fix-vof.11).
close_reason: Finding finalized: 5-value TurnStatus, immediate artifact removal, no further cleanup; recorded in bead, review doc R11, design doc Amendment A3

title: R9: Add conversation scoping to the review namespace
description:
FINDING: one channel spans multiple conversations (/new_conversation, ConversationStore conversation ids), so TurnReviewStore.list(channel_id) interleaves turns across conversations with no way to scope a review. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) conversation id in the turn key vs required record metadata with filtered listing; (2) source of the id (ConversationStore owns the counter - interacts with R37); (3) define behavior when the conversation switches while a turn is suspended. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R9.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-10 (with Dhar). (1) Namespace resolved structurally by R37/A1: conversation id is a key component of every turn record (fw:turn:{channel}:{conv_id}:{sortable-ts}-{uuid}); per-conversation listing is a prefix scan; channel-wide observability scans use the channel prefix. (2) Eager conversation-id reservation: active_conversation_id is guaranteed at session creation (restore-last or reserve-new), required because R16 mints the turn key at logical-turn start; deployments that never rotate conversations operate in a single implicit conversation. (3) Switch policy = AUTO-CANCEL: verified that neither /new_conversation (__main__.py:1174) nor /activate_conversation (:1349) checks awaiting_user or the pending store today. Decision: when a turn is suspended, both endpoints first cancel it - record the partial turn under its ORIGINAL conversation with status=cancelled (R39 semantics), clean up pending blob and suspend-offloaded payloads (R24) - then switch. Carry-across rejected (diverges agent memory from store under A1); 409-block rejected (UX). (4) Implementation note: cancel-then-switch must run under the per-session lock, which these endpoints do not currently acquire. Recorded in design doc Amendment A2 and review doc R9.
notes: Q and A: switch-while-suspended policy = auto-cancel (recommended option). Eager id reservation and channel-prefix listing settled without user input (conventional defaults). Cross-refs: R39 cancelled status, R24 orphan cleanup, R16 key minting.
close_reason: Finding finalized: structural namespace via A1, eager id reservation, auto-cancel on switch; recorded in bead, review doc R9, design doc Amendment A2

title: Add TTL/reaper for orphaned suspended-session blobs
description: In Topology B, when an agent suspends on ask_user and the user never returns, the durable pending-state blob persists indefinitely. SessionStateStore.save is called on suspend and on LRU eviction (eviction only SAVES, never deletes), and there is no TTL or background reaper. The only cleanup path is the /cancel_pending endpoint (ctx.cancel_pending() + store.clear()). Over time, abandoned blobs accumulate in DiskSessionStateStore (JSON files) and RedisSessionStateStore. Add a TTL/expiry mechanism: e.g. Redis key TTL on save, and a reaper/age-based sweep for the disk backend, with a configurable max-age. Ensure resuming refreshes the TTL.
acceptance_criteria: Abandoned pending blobs are eventually removed without manual cancel_pending; TTL is configurable; resuming an active suspension refreshes its expiry; tests cover expiry on both disk and redis backends.
notes:
Surfaced during trajectory-serialization review. Related: fastworkflow/session_state_store.py, fastworkflow/run_fastapi_mcp/utils.py (persist_pending_after_turn, _evict_oldest_if_needed).
Reaper contract addition from R24 final confirmation (2026-06-11): when deleting a stale pending blob, also delete the in-flight turn's payload prefix (fw:payload:{channel}:{conv}:{turn_key}:*) - trivial under A8 turn-scoped keys.
IMPLEMENTED v2.29.0.

ORDERING MATTERED, AND NOT IN THE DIRECTION THE ISSUE IMPLIED. Before fix-g03.25 removed the awaiting_user pin, reaping a pending blob was harmless but useless: the pinned in-memory copy kept the session working, so the reaper deleted only the crash-recovery path while the memory leak continued. After the pin was removed the blob can be the ONLY copy of a suspended conversation, which makes the reaper both effective and destructive. Doing this first would have been strictly worse than doing nothing.

DESIGN, mirroring fix-jtr rather than inventing a second shape.
- PendingRetentionPolicy(max_age_seconds=7d, max_entries=10000). Stated, not hidden -- decision 16 forbids a hidden durable-state TTL, not a TTL. Age alone is not a byte bound (steady state is abandonment_rate x window x blob_size, a plateau set by a rate the operator does not control), so the count cap is what makes size independent of arrival rate and it is on by default. 7 days because what is being deleted is a user half-finished conversation: too long costs disk, too short costs their work.
- reap(policy, protected_channel_ids, now, dry_run) -> PendingReapOutcome(reclaimed, protected, scanned, unreadable). Invoked, never scheduled: a timer inside the store would be a second writer on a channel whose only writer is meant to be the owning process.
- Protection is enforced at ChannelSessionManager.reap_pending_state(), which passes set(_sessions) | set(_leases). The store cannot know what is live; the manager is the only layer that does.
- The count cap counts protected entries in the TOTAL but never deletes them, or a process holding many live sessions would silently raise its own cap.
- Save time is stamped by the STORE (_saved_at), deliberately not in SCHEMA_VERSION: when a blob was written is a fact about storage, not about the session, and putting it in the schema would make every retention change a migration.
- Disk falls back to file mtime when _saved_at is absent, so blobs written before this change age out normally instead of being immortal for want of a field. Redis has no per-key write time and therefore no fallback.
- A blob whose age cannot be established is reported and LEFT IN PLACE. Reclaiming on a guess is how a reaper eats live state.
- Wired into the existing lifespan reaper task under its own try, so a failure in one namespace cannot silently disable retention in the other.

VERIFICATION. tests/test_pending_state_retention.py (12) + a manager-level wiring test in test_checkpoint_integration.py. Nine-mutation matrix, all caught on the first run: protection ignored, cap counting only candidates, oldest-first reversed, unreadable reclaimed, no mtime fallback, dry_run deleting, save not stamping, manager protecting nothing, and channel_id parsed from the filename.

TEST UPDATED, NOT REMOVED: test_disk_session_state_store_roundtrip asserted exact dict equality on load, which the save stamp breaks. It now asserts every saved field survives plus the stamp, which is what it was actually for.

DISCOVERED: fix-7hn (P1) -- DiskSessionStateStore._json_path is not injective, so tenant/user-1 and tenant_user-1 share one blob. Cross-session exposure, pre-existing, same defect class the checkpoint store already fixed. The reaper sidesteps it by reading channel_id from inside the blob.
close_reason: Implemented in v2.29.0. Abandoned suspended sessions are now reclaimed under a stated PendingRetentionPolicy by an invoked reaper, on the same terms fix-jtr set for the checkpoint namespace.

title: Param-example prompt renders repr() of field examples, so a default repr leaks a memory address into the LLM prompt
description:
DISCOVERED FROM fix-k0i.46.

generate_param_examples builds the prompt with ', '.join(repr(ex) for ex in field['examples']). An example object that inherits object.__repr__ therefore renders as '<Foo object at 0x7f...>' INSIDE THE PROMPT SENT TO THE MODEL.

fix-k0i.46 fixed the neighbouring instance of this in the cache KEY (_canonical_digest no longer uses default=repr, because the embedded id() made the key differ every run). The prompt instance is untouched and is arguably worse: an unstable cache key causes a wasted regeneration, whereas an address in the prompt is noise the model conditions on, and it changes every run so the generated examples are irreproducible for reasons invisible in the diff.

FIX: render examples through the same canonicalizer the digest now uses, or require examples to be JSON-native at the Field(examples=[...]) boundary and say so in the command-authoring rule.

Low severity: only bites commands whose Field examples are non-primitive objects, which is unusual.

title: Persona-source row matching is outside the utterance-cache fingerprint
description:
DISCOVERED FROM fix-k0i.43 (which closed the four functions it named; this is the residue).

DomainConditionedPersonaSource.rows and _matches are not digested. Editing which rows a keyword matches changes the persona pool a command is generated from, without invalidating any cache entry -- so a developer tunes the matching, retrains, and silently gets the old personas back.

fix-k0i.43 widened _DIGESTED_GENERATION_SOURCES to derived_seed, select_persona_indices, resolve_personas and PersonaSource.select, which covers the SELECTION algorithm. What is still uncovered is the SOURCE's own matching behaviour.

WHY IT WAS LEFT: closing it properly means digesting the active source's own methods, which makes the fingerprint source-dependent -- a different shape from the current 'digest these named module-level functions' design. That is a design decision, not an oversight.

Low severity while there is effectively one source in use.

title: Empty channel_id reaches the storage layer and now 500s instead of 400ing
description:
DISCOVERED FROM fix-7hn. encode_path_component('') raises ValueError, so a request carrying channel_id='' now fails inside the storage layer rather than at the API boundary.

This is strictly better than what it replaced -- the old _json_path('') returned '_pending.json', ONE SHARED FILE for every empty id, which is the same cross-session defect class fix-7hn just closed. Failing loudly beats silently sharing a bucket.

But it fails in the wrong place. No HTTP handler in run_fastapi_mcp validates that channel_id is non-empty, so the caller sees a 500 (an internal error, implying our bug) where they should see a 400 (their malformed request). It also means the error text is a storage-layer message rather than something an API consumer can act on.

FIX: validate channel_id at the API boundary -- non-empty, and probably a length cap since the encoder hashes beyond the filesystem name limit. The Pydantic request models are the natural home. Keep the ValueError as the backstop; the point is that it should be unreachable from a well-formed request.

Low severity: reachable only by a client sending an empty channel_id, which no normal client does.

title: reap() can report reclaiming a pending blob it did not remove
description:
DISCOVERED FROM fix-7hn (pre-existing; not introduced by it).

SessionStateStore.reap() enumerates entries via iter_entries(), which reads channel_id from INSIDE each blob (deliberately -- the storage key is not reversible). It then calls clear(channel_id), which derives the path FROM that id.

If a blob's embedded channel_id does not map back to its own filename, clear() removes nothing and reclaimed is incremented anyway. Reachable when a blob was hand-copied, restored from a backup under a different name, or written by an older tool.

Consequence: the reaper reports reclaiming N and the namespace does not shrink by N, and the offending blob is immortal -- enumerated forever, never removed. An operator watching the metric would conclude retention is working.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) have iter_entries yield the storage path alongside the channel_id and have reap unlink the path it actually enumerated; (b) verify after clear() that the entry is gone and count only confirmed removals, logging the mismatch. (a) is more direct and also removes reap's dependency on the blob's contents being self-consistent.

Severity low: reclaimed is a metric rather than a guarantee, and the situation requires a blob that did not come from this store. fix-7hn's two-path clear() makes it marginally less likely by also trying the legacy name.

title: Follow-up: complete logical-turn and CME continuation serialization (unpins awaiting sessions; needed for multi-pod)
description:
Sections 11.6 and 19.11; decision 26 [R2-8, R2-10 absorption]. NOT required for Release B v1 - v1 pins awaiting and continuation sessions instead.

The existing pending snapshot stores suspension flags, ReAct state, NLU stage, action log and conversation turns. It does NOT store the WEC logical-turn accumulator initialized at workflow_execution_context.py:104-114: _turn_outputs, _turn_key, _turn_started_at, the original and refined message, suspended duration and suspension start, entry workflow and context, and the agent result. Resume deliberately skips _begin_turn() (:547-549) precisely because it expects the old accumulator, so after rehydration the logical turn takes a NEW FALLBACK KEY and loses pre-suspension command outputs, ask-user entry, artifacts and timing.

The deterministic CME continuation is also incomplete: serialize_state() stores only nlu_stage, while clarification and parameter extraction depend on the CME context keys command, command_name and stored_parameters (fastworkflow/_workflows/command_metadata_extraction/_commands/wildcard.py:45, :141-144; parameter_extraction.py:72, :155-165). Workflow.end_command_processing() deletes command and stored_parameters and resets the stage (workflow.py:291-303), so a mid-extraction snapshot that omits them cannot be distinguished from a completed one after restore.

This is a PRE-EXISTING defect in today's suspended-state restore, not something Release B introduces.

Why it still matters with pinning [R2-10 absorption]: pinning removes the controlled-eviction half of the two-record consistency problem but not the crash half, and it does NOT help multi-pod - another pod still cold-rehydrates from the store, so the incomplete restore remains reachable. Redis-backed multi-pod deployments need this completeness work before they can rely on suspension across pods.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exact TurnOutput equivalence across suspend -> evict -> rehydrate -> resume.
- missing-parameter -> evict -> answer completes correctly.
- Only once both pass may the section 11.2 eligibility clause be relaxed so awaiting/continuation sessions become evictable.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED v2.28.0.

WHAT THE ISSUE GOT RIGHT AND WHAT IT MISSED. The listed gaps were all real: serialize_state carried neither the accumulator (_turn_outputs, _turn_key, timings, entry workflow/context, agent result) nor the CME keys (command, command_name, stored_parameters), only nlu_stage. What the issue framed as a multi-pod/crash concern was also a live memory bound: checkpoint.assess() pinned every awaiting session, decision 6 declines an idle TTL, and only the user returning or /cancel_pending clears it -- so an abandoned ask_user held a runtime for the life of the process. Release C lowering the cap 2000 -> 50 made that ~40x more reachable. The state was never unsaved; the blob is written at the end of the suspending turn. It was written lossily.

IMPLEMENTATION.
- WEC._serialize_turn_accumulator / _apply_turn_accumulator. CommandOutput list via model_dump(mode=json) / model_validate; datetimes ISO. _turn_agent_result is distilled to {exhausted: bool} because the finalize path reads only that attribute plus whether it is None -- it is a dspy Prediction that no strict encoder would accept whole.
- WEC._serialize_cme_continuation / _apply_cme_continuation. stored_parameters round-trips through the command Input class looked up from command_name via RoutingRegistry, rebuilt with model_construct (NOT model_validate: the saved instance was itself model_construct-ed and holds NOT_FOUND sentinels in typed fields, e.g. a str in an int field, which is exactly what validation rejects). An unresolvable class resets to intent detection with a warning rather than stranding the session at PARAMETER_EXTRACTION, where wildcard.py reads context[command_name] unconditionally.
- has_open_command() deliberately does NOT key off command_name: end_command_processing() clears command and stored_parameters but LEAVES command_name, so keying off it marks every session that ever ran a command as mid-extraction forever. Found by a test, not by reading.
- Both persist writers (turns._persist_after_turn and utils.persist_pending_after_turn) now save when has_open_command(), not only when awaiting. Mid-extraction sessions are not awaiting_user, so the old writers CLEARED their blob -- a pre-existing silent loss of partially extracted parameters on eviction.
- checkpoint.assess(runtime, store) replaces the awaiting_user pin with: pin iff (awaiting or mid-extraction) AND the blob is not in the store. Omitting the store pins, which is the safe reading for a caller that cannot check.
- SCHEMA_VERSION 1 -> 2. A v1 blob is refused by the fail-closed guard from fix-4od rather than migrated: it is a suspended turn minutes old, and the fields it lacks are the ones that made restoring it wrong.

VERIFICATION. tests/test_turn_and_cme_continuation.py (10) + 4 new in tests/test_checkpoint_integration.py. 8-mutation matrix, all caught; two survived the first run and drove real test additions -- a duplicated policy tested in only one of its two copies, and a model_construct guard tested with a value that validated either way. Behaviour was checked differentially against the live path (same sequence with and without a restore in the middle produces identical output) rather than against an idealised expectation.

TEST CHANGED, NOT REMOVED: test_a_suspended_channel_is_never_evicted asserted decision 26 and is now test_a_suspended_channel_is_evicted_now_that_its_snapshot_is_complete, with the pin half preserved in test_suspended_session_pins_when_its_state_never_reached_the_store.
close_reason: Implemented in v2.28.0. Schema 2 of the pending blob now carries the logical-turn accumulator and the CME continuation keys, and the unconditional awaiting_user pin is gone.

title: S3: dead-code sweep across the new modules (~350 lines beyond the decided deletions)
description: Everything below has zero production callers (grep-verified by reviewers) and is NOT covered by the decided deletions (fix-k0i.13/.19/.22): artifact_versioning.py format_versions_table/describe_version/human_age/human_duration/human_size (~115 lines, CLI-era) plus VersionInfo.size_bytes/_dir_size_bytes which run a full tree walk of EVERY version on each list_versions call including the one inside retain_current_and_previous on every train (wasted I/O); prune_versions keep= branch (~15); selective_training.py only_commands/only_contexts + descendants_of speculative API (~50) and the _resolve_cache_mode/_MODE_REUSE mirror unreachable from __main__ (~30); utterance_cache.py normalize_mode/_unknown_mode_warned/resolve_cache_mode (~35 — modes only arrive as internal constants); generate_synthetic.select_persona_indices production-dead duplicate of PersonaHubSource.select (~20, kept as test oracle — decide); personas.py num_personas_hint plumbing (~15, always 0 — resolved by fix-k0i.38 either way); generate_param_examples.py commented-out old transform block (:483-528, -46), stale regex-era comments in the AST loop (~10), merged duplicate required/optional invalid-params loops (-12), dead 'command in locals()' check (-2), save_examples_to_file/save_examples_to_json dead pair (-26), raw print() debugging to logger.debug (~8 sites); training_report.py get_min_training_rows/get_min_seed_utterances constant wrappers (~15). title: S3: AR2 base+parent compose case covered only by hand-built dicts — build the sibling fixture the spec prescribes
description: test_base_and_parent_axes_compose (tests/test_selective_training.py:83-112) exercises the shipped close_dirty_contexts but with hand-built context maps; no real-workflow reproduction exists — messaging_app_4 has no grandchild, and the spec's prescribed reproduction (AR2: 'give TodoList a second child that does not inherit from TodoItem' — the sibling whose wildcard class fills with TodoItem/* utterances) was never built. title: S3: test hygiene bundle — cleanup not in finally, dead assertions, stale docstrings, brittle --help substring

title: S3: cache-installation wiring tripwires are substring greps over source — comments satisfy them
description: tests/test_cache_installation_wiring.py:41-79: 'assert handle in train_workflow_source' passes if the set_param_example_cache/set_utterance_cache call is commented out or unreachable; test_teardown_happens_in_a_finally_block asserts only source.count('finally:')>=2 — any two finally blocks anywhere satisfy it even if neither contains the teardown. The install<generate<teardown ordering check exists only for the param cache, not the utterance cache or provenance recorder. title: S3: param-example pipeline hardening — legacy string-annotation branch is a reachable fail-open path; default=repr can silently destabilize the fingerprint
description: (1) generate_param_examples.py:941,969: with field_annotations passed as a string (the function's DECLARED type), model_fields={} and every malformed-value type check silently no-ops while 'required' comes from a regex heuristic — the fail-open shape fix-b8h closed remains reachable through the public signature; the only production caller passes dicts. DO: delete the legacy string branch (~68 lines) and type the parameter as dict; if external compat matters, raise loudly on str instead. (2) param_example_cache.py:150-162: _canonical_digest uses json.dumps(default=repr) — any future field_details value with a default object repr (embeds id()) makes the fingerprint differ every run: a permanent cache miss that is invisible-by-construction (looks identical to a first run), costing one LLM call per command per train with zero signal. DO: replace default=repr with a strict encoder that raises on non-JSON-serializable values (fail loudly at fingerprint time), or canonicalize known types explicitly.
close_reason: Fixed both halves. (1) The legacy string-field_annotations branch is gone and a non-mapping now raises: under a string, model_fields became {} downstream and every type and enum-membership check silently passed -- the validation hole fix-b8h closed for dicts stayed wide open through this function's own declared parameter type. No caller has ever passed a string; the only production call site passes fields.model_fields. (2) _canonical_digest no longer uses default=repr: most objects inherit object.__repr__, whose text embeds id(), so the variant key differed every run -- a permanent miss indistinguishable from a first run. It now canonicalizes what a parameter model can realistically hold (Enum, compiled pattern, type, set, bytes, temporal, Decimal) and raises otherwise; param_example_fingerprint catches that, warns by name and returns None, so the command trains uncached rather than failing the run. Verified a JSON-only payload digests exactly as before, so existing caches are not invalidated. NOTE: removing dead code required removing its comments; the substance (what the branch was, why it was fail-open, why removal is safe) was preserved and expanded in the extract_field_details docstring.

title: S3: content-shaped per-command LLM errors abort the entire multi-hour run instead of taking the R3 seed fallback
description: generate_synthetic.py:56-64,375-389: the retryable-exception set is enumerated, and a non-retryable error that is a property of ONE command's prompt rather than the account — ContentPolicyViolationError, ContextWindowExceededError from a huge seed list — propagates and kills the whole run at that command. Safe (previous version stays current, nothing silent) but expensive on a 160-command workflow hours in, and the enumerated-retryables comment only justifies excluding auth/config errors, not content-shaped ones. DO: catch content-shaped exceptions per command and take the existing R3 fallback ([command_name]+seeds, fell_back with reason recorded) — same handling as terminal rate-limit; keep auth/config errors fatal (they doom every subsequent command).
close_reason: Fixed, and this was the highest-value one: a rejection that is a property of ONE command's prompt no longer aborts a multi-hour run. Added CONTENT_SHAPED_LLM_EXCEPTIONS (ContextWindowExceededError, ContentPolicyViolationError, RejectedRequestError) and a second except clause taking the same R3 seed fallback a terminal rate limit takes -- command name plus seeds, fell_back and a reason recorded, nothing cached, run continues. Plain BadRequestError is deliberately NOT included: a bare 400 means the request WE built is malformed, which dooms every command after it too, so aborting is right. tests/test_synthetic_generation_resilience.py pins that each falls back rather than raising, is not retried (one call not six), keeps earlier batches, is never cached, reaches the degraded-training banner, and that AuthenticationError / BadRequestError / NotFoundError / BudgetExceededError still abort. Mutation-checked.

title: S3: AR1's cheap leak-detection instrument (token-overlap ov(u) metrics) never shipped — holdout number has no calibration
description: Spec AR1 specifies two string-operation checks over R6's cached utterances: (1) per held-out utterance, max token overlap vs the command's training rows (report median and fraction >=0.8, compared across random-row split / persona split / benchmark) and (2) fraction of held-out content tokens appearing in utterance_patterns (direct evidence of prompt-induced vocabulary leakage no persona split can remove). grep finds no implementation anywhere — so the persona-holdout number ships with no measure of its residual leak, and the spec's stated instrument for calibrating it does not exist. DO: either implement (small: pure string ops over cached utterances, report in metric_notes/heldout report) or explicitly retract the instrument from the spec/AR1 record as not-shipped — decide, don't leave the spec claiming an instrument that is absent. Pairs with fix-k0i.12 (lower-bound disclosure).

title: S3: utterance-cache fingerprint omits persona-SELECTION code — editing selection logic leaves stale entries valid
description: generate_synthetic.py:434-484: generator_source_digest covers only generate_utterances_for_personas + _is_template_echo. Editing derived_seed, select_persona_indices, PersonaSource.select, or resolve_personas changes WHICH personas generate but leaves every cache entry fingerprint-valid — stale reuse of utterances written by personas a fresh run would no longer pick. (The design rationale for excluding persona IDs themselves from the key is sound — corpus-free validation — but then the selection CODE must be in the source digest; it is not.) DO: add the selection functions (derived_seed, select_persona_indices, the active PersonaSource class's select/resolve) to the digested source set; note in the module docstring which functions participate and why. This will invalidate existing caches once — expected and correct.
close_reason: Fixed. generator_source_digest covered the prompt and the post-filter but not WHO WAS ASKED. The new _DIGESTED_GENERATION_SOURCES also names derived_seed, select_persona_indices, resolve_personas and PersonaSource.select, each labelled qualname:digest so a stale-cache miss is readable without re-deriving six hashes. End-to-end test stores an entry under the PRE-FIX digest formula and proves the real generation path misses it. Known remaining gap, filed separately: DomainConditionedPersonaSource.rows/_matches are still outside the digest, so editing which rows a keyword matches changes the pool without invalidating anything.

title: S3: ~7 full-training tests carry no slow/expensive marker — cannot be deselected
description: Only the selective e2e carries @pytest.mark.slow (test_selective_training_integration.py:658). The trained_hello_world module fixture, test_benchmark_routing_cases_are_scored, test_report_describes_a_real_training_run, and both determinism modules (each doing TWO full trains) carry no marker; tests/conftest.py:97 auto-marks only mcp_server. Do not skip/remove any test (testing_rules.mdc).

title: S3: no cross-process guard around publish/prune — two concurrent trains can interleave pointer writes and prune each other's carry-forward source
description: Two concurrent 'fastworkflow train' runs interleave pointer writes, compat-entry swaps, and retain_current_and_previous prunes — one process can prune the version another is mid-_link_tree carrying forward from. Single-developer CLI makes this low-likelihood, but the modules present publication as transactional and it is single-process best-effort. DO (minimal): a workflow-local lock file around the publish+prune critical section (fcntl/msvcrt or O_EXCL sentinel with stale-lock timeout), OR an explicit docstring/README statement that concurrent trains on one workflow are unsupported. Decide which; either resolves the finding.

title: S3: R5's 'state which contexts were retrained' output prints only when something was carried forward
description: train/__main__.py:203-204: 'if plan.contexts_carried_forward: print(format_plan(plan))' — a full retrain, or a selective plan in which every context turned out dirty, prints nothing about which contexts were retrained or why, even though compute_training_plan deliberately preserves per-context reasons for exactly this audience (selective_training.py:903-906). R5's requirement: 'The output must state which contexts were retrained and which were carried forward, so the developer can see the closure that was computed.' title: S3: --regenerate-utterances is not propagated to the internal CME workflow
description: train/__main__.py train_main: the internal command_metadata_extraction workflow is trained via bare train_workflow(fastworkflow_folderpath) (:505-513) while only the target workflow gets regenerate_utterances=... A poisoned CME cache (the flag's documented purpose: 'when you suspect the cache is wrong') cannot be refreshed by any CLI means; the only remedy is manually deleting the cache dir inside the installed package. Note the CME train only runs when CME is untrained, so also consider whether --regenerate-utterances should force a CME retrain when the flag is given — probably not (scope: the target workflow), but say so in a comment.
notes: Forwarded regenerate_utterances to the internal CME train_workflow call inside the existing needs-training condition. The flag refreshes CME caches when CME training is already required but deliberately does not force otherwise-unneeded internal retraining; the code comment and AST wiring test pin both parts. Verified in the 123-pass focused orchestration batch with clean diagnostics.

title: S3: domain-conditioning top-up nullifies the conditioning when it fires; num_personas_hint dead in production
description: personas.py:490-504: when matched personas fall below the floor, the top-up appends EVERY unmatched row (matched + top_up = the entire ~200k corpus) and samples uniformly over the result — matched personas get probability ~matched/200k, i.e. conditioning is effectively nullified, while the note claims only that 'conditioning is partial'. Also num_personas_hint is never passed in any real call path, so wanted collapses to max(0,4)=4 and the guard only fires below 4 matches — and then does the wrong thing. DO: when topping up, keep all matched rows selected first (or weight matched heavily) and top up only the shortfall; plumb the real requested persona count as the hint or delete the parameter. Sequence after fix-k0i.3 (wiring makes this path reachable for workflow files). BLOCKED-BY fix-k0i.3.
close_reason: Fixed both halves. The top-up now adds only the shortfall (pool = the floor, not the entire ~200k corpus), sampled from a keyword-derived RNG so the pool is identical across runs and training seeds -- previously the conditioning was nullified exactly when it was needed. Matched rows are now drawn FIRST: PersonaSource.priority_pool_size() returns 0 by default, the domain source returns its matched count, and the shared select exhausts the priority tier before padding. The tier logic went in the BASE select rather than a subclass override specifically so it stays under the fix-k0i.43 digest. num_personas_hint now defaults to the configured SYNTHETIC_UTTERANCE_GEN_NUMOF_PERSONAS, so the floor is real in production without train/__main__.py needing to know about persona pools. The note states actual numbers instead of 'conditioning is partial'. Also pinned: the default PersonaHub draw stays byte-identical across seeds, commands and sample sizes.

title: S3: param-example reporting — 'regenerate' summary claims 0 generated after N LLM calls; all-rejected commands degrade near-silently
description: (1) CONFIRMED: in regenerate mode lookup() returns before bumping the miss counter (param_example_cache.py:364-365) and format_summary renders misses as 'generated' (:471), so 'fastworkflow train --regenerate-utterances' prints 'Parameter-example cache (regenerate): 0 reused, 0 generated, 12 written' — a developer auditing LLM spend reads zero calls where every command hit the LLM. Bump the counter (or count stores) in regenerate mode. (2) A command whose examples are ALL rejected ships an empty few-shot corpus (valid_examples: [] written; runtime falls back to zero-shot extraction) with only a generic print/logger.info (generate_param_examples.py:1041-1051, train/__main__.py:342-344) — no warning distinguishes '0 accepted' from '2 of 15 rejected'. Correctly not cached, so it self-heals next run, but the degraded run is near-silent: WARN loudly naming the command when accepted==0 and requested>0.
close_reason: Fixed. lookup() returned before bumping miss when reads are disabled, so --regenerate-utterances printed '0 reused, 0 generated, 12 written' after twelve real completions. A disabled read now counts as a miss, because the caller's next move is identical to a miss's. EXTENDED BEYOND THE NAMED FILE: the identical defect existed in the sibling utterance_cache and was fixed there too -- both summaries print in the same run, and one telling the truth about spend while the other does not would be worse than neither. Separately, a command whose examples are ALL rejected now emits a warning naming it and saying extraction will run zero-shot; a partial rejection stays quiet, which is the boundary that keeps the warning worth reading. Mutation-checked in both caches.

title: S3: utterance-cache ergonomics — misses never say WHY, orphaned variants grow unbounded
description: (1) Miss debuggability: on a cache miss nothing logs which fingerprint input diverged from the on-disk fingerprint_inputs — the developer diffs JSON by hand; the counters (utterance_cache.py:427-434) only say a miss happened. The entry stores fingerprint_inputs precisely to make this answerable: log a one-line diff (first differing key) at INFO on miss. (2) Growth: every seed-list/model/prompt edit orphans the previous <slug>.<variant>.json forever — no GC; _prune_stale_artifacts deliberately skips the cache dir. On an actively-tuned 160-command workflow this accumulates indefinitely. DO: opportunistic GC — when writing a new variant for a slug, delete variants not referenced by current or previous version manifests (conservative: keep N most recent); document the policy in the module docstring. Same pattern applies to param_example_cache.
close_reason: Fixed both halves. (1) A miss now logs one INFO line naming the diverging fingerprint inputs with old and new values, compared against the CLOSEST stored variant rather than the newest -- 'your seed utterances changed' is the useful answer, not 'this is not the variant from three model swaps ago'. A same-variant/missing-seed miss gets its own message listing the seeds present. A first run stays silent, because 160 lines of 'nothing cached yet' would bury the ones that matter. (2) A write now prunes that command's older variants to MAX_VARIANTS_PER_COMMAND=3, matching on the STORED command name so a filename-slug collision cannot delete another command's data, ordering by mtime so the file just written always survives, and never raising. Both mechanisms are shared code used by both caches; retention policy documented in the utterance_cache module docstring. Mutation-checked.

title: S3: heldout report schema inconsistencies — escalation_recall 0.0 vs no-cases, selective merge drops keys and fakes f1=0.0
description: (1) aggregate_totals emits escalation_recall: 0.0 when escalation_total==0 — indistinguishable in JSON from 'measured, 0% recall' without checking the denominator; format_report handles it ('-') but JSON consumers get the ambiguity. (2) selective_training._recompute_heldout_totals (:1054-1088) drops the out_of_scope_*/false_rejection_* keys that fresh aggregate_totals always emits (moot if CR13's deletion lands first) and converts mean_in_distribution_f1 from None to 0.0 when no F1 exists — a merged report has a different totals schema and a fake 0.0 mean vs a fresh one, so diffing reports across selective/full runs misleads. DO: emit null (not 0.0) for zero-denominator metrics in both paths; make _recompute_heldout_totals produce the same key set as aggregate_totals (share the function); preserve None. Sequence after fix-k0i.13.
close_reason: Fixed both halves. (1) Zero-denominator metrics now emit null instead of 0.0 in aggregate_totals -- routing_top1, routing_in_list, escalation_recall, benchmark_routing_*, holdout_escalation_recall. In JSON, 0.0 is indistinguishable from a measured total failure. format_report still renders '-' for both. (2) selective_training._recompute_heldout_totals no longer re-implements the aggregation: it validates entries into HeldoutReport and delegates to aggregate_totals, so the merged and fresh key sets are identical by construction and cannot drift again. It previously dropped keys and converted a missing mean_in_distribution_f1 to a literal 0.0, so diffing a selective run against a full one read as a collapse in quality. ValidationError added to the caller's caught set so a malformed entry still degrades to stale totals with a warning rather than aborting the merge. Tests assert set(merged) == set(fresh) and equality of values.

title: S3: escalation-budget decision leaves no artifact — the AR6 'unreconstructable denominators' problem rebuilt
description: model_pipeline_training.py:1142-1174: neither the computed budget, the coverage_floor, own_rows, nor the selected escalation-row count is printed, logged, or recorded in provenance. 'Why does this context's wildcard class have 87 rows' — the exact question AR6 spent a spec section on because the reference workflow's numbers could not be reconstructed — has no artifact to consult, while every other pipeline decision (generation, skips, fallbacks) got a provenance dimension. DO: record per-context {own_rows, ancestor_candidate_rows, coverage_floor, budget, selected_rows} in provenance schema (context_training or a small escalation_budget block) and surface in the training report. Fold-in from the same review: the coverage floor counts core commands asymmetrically depending on whether a context was first visited as an ancestor or as a trainee (cache filled from commands() vs train_cmds; class_balance.coverage_floor_of counts them as sources), so when the floor binds, renaming a context can change a sibling's training data — normalize the source set used for the floor (exclude core commands consistently) so the budget is visit-order- and name-independent.

title: S3: three silent-failure suppressions — heldout write, provenance save, corrupt manifest pruning the recovery version
description: (1) model_pipeline_training.py:1622: write_report wrapped in contextlib.suppress(OSError) with NO log — a failed write leaves heldout_evaluation.json stale/absent while the run claims success, and the selective merge (train/__main__.py:268) then merges against the wrong baseline; capture_heldout_evaluation silently returns None next run. (2) train/__main__.py:250-256: recorder.save() equally suppressed — the publish gate at :284 then evaluates the PREVIOUS run's training_provenance.json, passing or failing on data describing a different run. (3) artifact_versioning read_manifest returns {} for unreadable JSON (:514-525), so on the no-op path previous_previous=None and retain_current_and_previous prunes the ACTUAL previous successful version — implicit destruction triggered by a damaged manifest.json, against R4's never-destroy-implicitly rule. DO: (1)+(2) log loudly at ERROR and, for (2), refuse the publish gate on a failed save (the gate's input is gone); (3) treat an unreadable manifest as fatal for retention (skip pruning, warn), never as 'no previous'.

title: S3: code comments and docs reference CLI surface that was cut — rollback/prune commands, benchmark flag, rejected_examples.json dump

title: S3: stale fix-eia claims in convergence skill (self-contradiction) and command-authoring rule
description: CONFIRMED. .claude/skills/fastworkflow-intent-training-convergence/SKILL.md contradicts itself: lines 94-101 correctly state the benchmark validators now run (fix-eia FIXED, disjointness raises BenchmarkLeakError before training), but Precondition 1 (:136-141) and Pitfalls (:357-360) still instruct 'The package ships the check but does not yet run it (fix-eia), so enforce it yourself'. .claude/rules/command-authoring.md repeats the stale claim ('as of 2026-08-02 nothing calls it during training (fix-eia), so run it yourself'). fix-eia is closed with call sites at model_pipeline_training.py:887-913 (per its close note; current lines ~996-1043). The 'not called during training' half was the stale one: model_pipeline_training.py calls assert_benchmark_disjoint_from_seeds (deliberately uncaught) and find_near_duplicate_benchmark_cases / validate_routing_cases / validate_escalation_cases before the training loop begins. Also removed stale untracked bytecode from the skill's scripts dir, and fixed the 'Five gaps' heading that sat above seven bullets.

title: R9b: detect and report near-duplicate command capabilities
description:
ADDRESSES F14 (S3). Some workflows expose the same capability twice — on IDO, ControlsMonitor/list_findings and Directory/search_control_findings answer the same question. No amount of utterance engineering separates them. They present as PERMANENT BENCHMARK FAILURES and send developers chasing an unfixable defect.

DO (spec R9): after training, cluster label centroids and warn on near-duplicate commands, NAMING THE PAIR so the developer can merge, alias, or accept them.

The value here is diagnostic honesty: turning an unfixable-looking accuracy failure into a design observation the developer can act on.
notes:
R9b DELIVERED (reporting-only; no integration into the training path, by design). Near-duplicate defined operationally as a property of the TRAINING DATA rather than of the commands' meanings: two commands are near-duplicates when a classifier restricted to that pair, trained on their own utterances, cannot separate them. Implemented as leave-one-out balanced nearest-centroid accuracy in TF-IDF space with document frequency computed across ALL commands, which is what suppresses false positives on command families sharing boilerplate. Chance is 0.5 by construction, so the threshold is the coin-flip line, not a fitted constant. Evidence: on retail (19 commands, 79 pairs) zero duplicates and one low-severity overlap; minimum separability 0.56 and median 1.00 across 171 scored pairs. The positive-control workflow's deliberately duplicated pair scores 0.00 and is flagged; the hard negative in that workflow is not. Documented blind spot: it is a lexical instrument, so a duplicate pair with genuinely disjoint vocabulary is invisible -- covered instead by find_confusable_commands, which asks the trained router what it actually does via a predict_fn.
R9b SHIPPED, and the missing piece was the call site. duplicate_detection.py was complete and unit-tested but had NO caller anywhere in fastworkflow/ -- a developer had no way to run it, which is indistinguishable from the feature not existing. Now wired as `fastworkflow duplicates <workflow> [--json] [--fail-on-duplicates]`.

Wiring it surfaced two defects no unit test could have caught, which is the argument for insisting on call sites: (1) the scan needs fastworkflow.init() before the routing definition resolves -- it failed with "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get_definition'"; (2) find_confusable_commands() requires a trained model's predict_fn, so it CANNOT run in a pre-training scan at all. The command therefore does the lexical scan only, which is the half that works before you have spent an afternoon training two commands no data separates.

--fail-on-duplicates gates on outright duplicates only. Overlapping and confusable pairs are frequently correct -- two commands SHOULD look similar when they do similar things -- and failing on them would teach developers to bypass the check. Verified discriminating: exits 1 on tests/duplicate_capability_workflow, exits 0 on retail (which has an overlapping pair and no duplicate). 5 CLI integration tests run the real binary in a subprocess, because the failure being guarded against is that the entry point is unreachable -- a test importing the function would have passed all through the period the command did not exist.
close_reason: Shipped and integrated; see notes

title: F11: shared encoder with per-context heads — cut 276 MB/context
description:
ADDRESSES F11 (S3). Each context directory holds a full DistilBERT copy PLUS a BERT-tiny (largemodel.pth, tinymodel.pth, two threshold files, a label encoder) — roughly 276 MB per context. 33 contexts -> 8.6 GB for a 160-command workflow.

A shared encoder with per-context classification heads would cut this by roughly two orders of magnitude, and would make selective retraining cheap: rewriting one context would touch a few MB of head weights instead of 276 MB.

DO:
- Evaluate and, if it holds up, implement a shared-encoder / per-context-head architecture.
- Measure the accuracy consequence on BOTH axes (R1) with a paired test — a shared encoder is a real modelling change, not a packaging change, and must clear the same bar as R7.

SCOPED AS P3 DELIBERATELY: it is a cost and ergonomics win that makes versioning (R4) and selective training (R5) cheaper, but neither depends on it. Do not let it block them.

VERIFY current cost: du -sh <workflow>/___command_info/*/ | sort -h | tail -5

RETIRED — NOT A LOSSLESS PACKAGING REFACTOR. One Tiny+Distil context is 287,342,019 bytes (274.0 MiB); 33 contexts are ~8.83 GiB. Frozen shared encoders plus per-context heads could reduce that to ~348 MiB (96.1%, 26x). But current training fine-tunes every encoder independently: sampled contexts shared 0/41 identical Tiny tensors and 0/104 Distil tensors, so existing artifacts cannot be split losslessly. Frozen shared encoders change the trained model and may reduce routing/escalation accuracy; joint multi-context training invalidates every head and defeats R5; adapters add major runtime/serialization/dependency complexity. R4/R5 already hardlink carried-forward contexts, reducing version duplication. Without a pre-registered five-seed non-inferiority experiment, storage savings do not justify this modeling redesign. design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) WRITE FAILURE = BEST-EFFORT + LOUD TELEMETRY: bounded in-line retries, then the turn succeeds for the user regardless - by record-write time the command's side effects are committed; erroring would invite double-execution retries. Failure logged prominently; a MONITORING COUNTER is documented as a deployment alarm expectation (post-A1 stakes acknowledged: a lost write means the turn is missing from conversation history and post-restart memory - the gap is operator-visible by contract). (2) CRASH WINDOWS = BOUNDED LEAKS (stated): payloads under a recordless turn prefix are adopted idempotently by a retry (A22 stable key + A27 hashed leaves) or removed eventually by conversation-prefix retention (A12). (3) STALE-PENDING SAFETY NET (stated): order = record write -> pending clear; at restore, a pending blob whose turn key already has a record is stale and discarded - record-write wins always (blob carries its turn key per A22). (4) LOCK HOLD (stated): write stays in-lock with a tight retry budget (sub-ms/ms writes vs multi-second turns); post-lock writing noted as a permitted future optimization (A24 assigns the ordinal in-lock either way). Recorded in design doc Amendment A28 and review doc R23.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 with the post-A1 stakes shift and the double-execution trap): best-effort + loud telemetry, recommended option. The side-effects-already-committed argument was decisive.

title: R12: Resolve nested_turn open issues (producer, arity, suspension, semantics)
description:
FINDING: nested_turn has zero producers today (the same speculative generality the design kills command_responses for); singular may be wrong (a command can run multiple sub-turns); nested suspension (child ask_user inside parent partial) is undefined for serialize_state; nested user_message semantics undefined; embedded-only records grow unboundedly. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) ship with a synthetic test producer; (2) nested_turns list vs Optional single; (3) define nested suspension serialization; (4) define nested user_message; (5) set a revisit trigger for embedded-only (p95 record size). See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R12.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) ARITY = LIST: CommandOutput.nested_turns: list[TurnResult] = [] (supersedes the singular nested_turn of design section 5.2) - empty in the common case, represents loops/fan-outs over sub-agents, never needs a record-schema break later. (2) NESTED SUSPENSION = ALWAYS ESCALATE: an inner agent's question bubbles up to become the TOP-LEVEL turn's suspension, generalizing the existing wildcard.py:61-71 escalation pattern. Consequence: a nested TurnResult attaches to its command ONLY WHEN COMPLETE; partial-inside-partial pending blobs never exist; all suspend/resume machinery (A19, A30) works unchanged at any nesting depth. Deliberately constrains future nested-agent designs to escalation-style clarification (also the simplest UX - one question stream). (3) STATED CONVENTIONS: nested user_message = the delegation instruction the parent command passed to the sub-agent; a SYNTHETIC TEST PRODUCER ships with the seam (R35 matrix) so the recursive serializer is never dead untested code; embedded-only revisit trigger named (p95 record size over ~256KB with real nested agents -> promote nested turns to references). Recorded in design doc Amendment A32 and review doc R12.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 turn-within-a-turn): list arity + always-escalate, both recommended options. The escalation model's payoff: zero new suspension machinery at any nesting depth.
close_reason: Finding finalized: nested_turns list, escalation-only suspension, test producer + conventions; recorded in bead, review doc R12, design doc Amendment A32

title: Add schema migration for serialized session state (schema_version)
description: serialize_state writes schema_version (currently 1) and apply_serialized_state only logs a warning on mismatch; there is no migration logic. If the serialized blob format evolves, existing pending blobs (disk JSON / Redis) will be misread or silently dropped. Add versioned migration: on load, detect schema_version and upgrade older blobs to the current shape (or explicitly discard with a clear policy).
acceptance_criteria: Loading an older-schema blob either migrates it to the current schema or is handled by an explicit documented policy; mismatch no longer silently warns; tests cover an older-version blob.
notes:
Surfaced during trajectory-serialization review. Related: fastworkflow/session_state_store.py (SCHEMA_VERSION), fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py apply_serialized_state.
PARTIALLY ADDRESSED 2026-08-06 (v2.27.x). The dangerous half is fixed; the migration machinery is deliberately not.

DONE - fail-closed on mismatch. apply_serialized_state() previously logged a warning and then fell through to apply every field, so a blob written by a future build would be HALF-restored onto a live session. It now raises session_state_store.IncompatibleSessionState having applied nothing, and the cold-create path in run_fastapi_mcp/utils.py catches it, clears the stale blob so it cannot re-raise on every subsequent cold create, and starts the session clean. Losing a suspended turn is recoverable by asking again; a partial restore is not.

Tests: tests/test_session_state_serialization.py::test_unreadable_schema_version_applies_nothing (parametrized over newer/older/0/None/string) asserts nothing was applied, plus test_readable_schema_version_still_applies so the first test is about the VERSION rather than about apply_serialized_state doing nothing at all. Mutation-checked: reverting the guard to warn-and-fall-through fails all 5 cases.

STILL OPEN - migration. There is only one schema version, so there is nothing to migrate FROM, and writing migration machinery now means designing against a format that does not exist. Pick this up when SCHEMA_VERSION 2 is actually defined; the policy question (upgrade in place vs discard) is then answerable rather than speculative. The fail-closed behaviour above is the correct default until then.

title: Restore full command-context navigation depth on rehydration
description: serialize_state captures only current_command_context_name (a string). On cold rehydration, startup is re-run which resets to the root context; if the user had navigated several levels deep into a nested context, that exact position is not reconstructed. apply_serialized_state only logs a debug warning when the rehydrated name differs from the saved one. Design a way to serialize and restore the navigation path/position (e.g. an ordered list of context identifiers + a workflow-specific restore hook) so deep navigation survives relocation.
acceptance_criteria: A session navigated N levels deep resumes at the same context after cold rehydration on a fresh process; covered by an integration test using a nested-context workflow.
notes: Surfaced during trajectory-serialization review. Related: fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py serialize_state/apply_serialized_state, tests/test_command_context_serialization_spike.py.
close_reason: Resolved by the serialization-hook locator mechanism in v2.26.0. serialize_state captured only current_command_context_name, so a nested position was lost on rehydration. The checkpoint now serializes one anchor and stores the other context slots as LOCATORS into it, with a serialize-time self-check that find_by_locator(anchor, get_locator(obj)) is obj. Verified by identity rather than equality in tests/test_workflow_serialization_hooks.py: restored.current_command_context is bug (a nested WorkItem), is laundry (a nested TodoList), and bob is chatroom.users[1]. Applies to workflows whose context class implements the hooks; one without them pins instead of losing the position.

title: Step 3 (deferred): distributed durable turn store + external worker pool
description: Step 3, deferred until load/durability demands it. Durable turn store + queue (Redis/Arq/RQ/Celery/SQS); external worker pool sized to safe LLM concurrency; stateless API replicas; sticky channel->worker routing or rehydratable ctx; leasing + heartbeat (visibility timeout > 15 min); prefer litellm.acompletion so a deadline cancels the in-flight HTTP request instead of orphaning a thread (this is where deadline_seconds becomes a HARD kill — deferred item 3). Eliminates the in-process-only LOST state.
